## 8. Monitoring and cost attribution (`monitor.py`)

### 8.1 Record schema (one JSON object per attempt)
`ts` (str), `call_id` (str), `task` (str), `flavor` (str), `model` (str), `family` (str), `attempt` (int, 0-based index within the call), `final` (bool, True on the call's last attempt), `outcome` (str), `error` (str or null), `latency_ms` (float), `input_tokens` (int), `output_tokens` (int), `cost_usd` (float, list price, recorded in both flavors), `routing_cost_usd` (float: equals `cost_usd` in `cost_effective`, `0.0` in `cost_blind`), `below_bar` (bool), `basis` (str), `tags` (object of string to string; `{}` when none; v1.11: `call_delegated` adds `delegated` and `parent`, 7)
- v1.203 `below_bar_fallback` (bool, `true` wherever it is present): written right after `below_bar`, and only on an attempt whose model is in the decision's `below_bar_fallbacks` (5.1), a fallback under the bar behind a primary that clears it, which only a task with `fallback_below_bar` can have (5.3). No other record has the key, so every record of a task without the option keeps v1.202's keys in v1.202's order, and the demo's `calls.jsonl` keeps its bytes. A record's model was under the bar when its `below_bar` is true (then nothing cleared, so every model of the route is under it, 5.3) or it has `below_bar_fallback: true`; `below_bar` keeps its meaning, the decision's flag. `.call` and `.call_delegated` (7) both write the key, the hand-off from `decision.route`
- v1.507 `prompt_tokens` (int) and `prompt_tokens_estimated` (bool), the last two keys, after `tags`, of every record `.call` writes (row FIT1): the size 5.2 rule 5 checked for the call, and whether the executor estimated it (`true`) or the caller passed it (`false`). Records of `.call_delegated` have neither key, and `report` (8.3) reads neither, so its rows and the CLI `report` output are unchanged. A `.call` record thus has two keys more than in v1.506, so `RECORD_TYPES` and the whole-record dict of `test_executor_falls_back_on_providererror_and_records_exact_attempt_schema` of tests/test_executor.py, the `.call` uses of `V1_202_KEYS` (its `.call_delegated` use keeps the v1.506 keys, so FIT1b keeps a v1.506 list for it) and the demo log digest `V1_202_CALLS_SHA256` of tests/test_below_bar_records.py (whose `test_the_demo_records_keep_v1_202_keys` then expects the two keys on the demo's `.call` records and not on its hand-off records) and the demo's pinned `calls.jsonl` digest of tests/test_demo_delegation.py change in the implementing commit (row FIT1b), whose CHANGELOG.md line names every existing test it changes v1.509: README `## Monitoring and cost attribution` names both keys.
- v1.511 `slice` (str or null), right after `tags` on every record `.call` and `.call_delegated` write (row STRAT1): the decision's `slice` (5.1), null when the call named none, so a `.call` record ends `tags`, `slice`, `prompt_tokens`, `prompt_tokens_estimated` and a `.call_delegated` record `tags`, `slice`. `report` (8.3) reads no `slice`, so its rows and the CLI `report` output are unchanged. Every record gains a key, so the implementing commit (row STRAT1b) moves these pins, found by `rg` in this turn: `RECORD_TYPES` and the whole-record dict of tests/test_executor.py, `V1_202_KEYS`, `WITH_KEY`, `CALL_KEYS`, `CALL_WITH_KEY` and `V1_202_CALLS_SHA256` of tests/test_below_bar_records.py, `V111_CALLS_SHA256` of tests/test_demo_delegation.py and the `V1_506_KEYS` record checks of tests/test_prompt_fit.py, and, for the 4.2 field, `test_the_field_is_last_and_off_by_default` of tests/test_fallback_below_bar.py and the `asdict` of `test_task_defaults_and_frozen_dataclass` of tests/test_registry_tasks_data.py; its CHANGELOG.md line names every existing test it changes
- v1.537 `cascade` (str, the route entry's `id`) and `escalated` (bool), in that order right after `slice` and before `prompt_tokens`, only on the attempts of a cascade route entry that `.call` writes (row ESC2c, DESIGN 7 v1.532 and v1.537): on its cheap attempt whether it was handed up, on its strong attempt `true`. A handed-up cheap attempt has `final` false and the outcome `ok` when its completion returned or `error` on a `ProviderError`, so `report` (8.3) counts it in `ok` or `errors`, and the call, whose final attempt is then 1 or later, in `fallback_calls` (until v1.579, which counts route entries, 8.3). No other record gains a key, so no existing record pin moves

- v1.567 `expected_cost_per_success_usd` (number or null), the last key, only on the records of a decision whose `failure_policy` is not `"none"` (5.1, row CPS1a): that decision's value, the primary's estimate whatever model the attempt ran (a fallback's record holds the same number), on every attempt `.call` and `.call_delegated` write. No other record gains a key, so no existing record pin moves, and `report` (8.3), which reads no such key, is unchanged
- v1.578 procedure keys (row PROC1c, 7 v1.578): every record of a procedure route entry that `.call` writes gains `procedure` (str, the procedure's `name`) and `procedure_version` (str, its `version`), in that order right after `slice` and before `prompt_tokens`, where a cascade entry's two keys go (an entry is never both); its closing record then also gains `model_calls` (int, the model calls its handle let through, counted by the executor, so also on a run that raised), `tool_calls` (int, or null when the run raised) and `tool_cost_usd` (number, or null when it raised), in that order. A model call's record has `model` the procedure's `model`, that model's `family` and `final` false; the closing record has `model` the procedure's `.id`, `family` its model's or `""` without one, as its candidate's (5.2 v1.577), input and output tokens 0, `cost_usd` its tool cost (0.0 when it raised), `routing_cost_usd` that in `cost_effective` and 0.0 in `cost_blind`, and `final` true when it is `ok` or the route's last entry. `below_bar_fallback` is read by the route entry, as for a cascade (v1.537). No other record gains a key, so no existing record pin moves
- v1.584 `pricing_basis` (str, `"self_hosted"` wherever it is present), right after `routing_cost_usd` and before `below_bar`, only on an attempt whose `model` is a registry model with `pricing_basis` `"self_hosted"` (row SELF1c, 4.1 v1.581, 7 v1.584): a plain entry's attempt, a cascade's cheap or strong attempt and a procedure's model call, from `.call` and `.call_delegated`. A procedure's closing record, whose `model` is its `.id` and whose cost is its tool cost, never has it. Every record of a list-priced model keeps v1.583's keys in their order, so no existing record pin moves and the demo's `calls.jsonl` keeps its bytes; `report` reads the key only for `by="pricing_basis"` (8.3 v1.584)
- v1.589 `cached_input_tokens` (int) and `cache_write_tokens` (int), in that order right after `output_tokens` and before `cost_usd`, each only on a record whose attempt's count is not `None` (row CACHE1c, 7 v1.589): the cached reads and cache writes its provider returned for the call, inside the record's `input_tokens`, which still counts every input token. Each key stands alone, so a record of the OpenAI-compatible adapter (6 v1.589) gains `cached_input_tokens` alone, and `cost_usd` and `routing_cost_usd` are the attempt's cost at those counts. An error record, a procedure's closing record and every record of a provider that returns no count keep v1.588's keys in their order, so no existing record pin moves and the demo's `calls.jsonl` keeps its bytes. By default `report` (8.3) reads neither key, so its rows and the CLI `report` output are unchanged; its hit rate is row CACHE1f (done in v1.590, 8.3 and 10: with `cache=True` it reads `cached_input_tokens` alone)
- v1.596 `budget_moves` (row B1b, 7 v1.596): on every record of a call written after a `downgrade` budget first moved it, a list of one object per move so far, in order, `{"entry": <the route entry>, "model": <the model whose hold was refused>, "budget": <the budget's name>}`, a cascade's entry its ID and its model the leg's; it goes after any cascade or procedure keys and before `prompt_tokens` and `expected_cost_per_success_usd`. No other record has the key, so a call that never moved keeps v1.595's keys.
- v1.598 budget records (row B1e, 7 v1.598): a record with a `budget_event` key is no attempt record but a budget's, written only by an executor with a ledger. Its keys, in order: `ts`, `call_id`, `task` (the decision's), `tags` (the call's, a delegated call's with `delegated` and `parent`), `budget_event` (`"warn"` or `"refused"`), `budget` (the name), `mode` and `window` (the label, `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM`, or null for a `total` budget); then for `"warn"` the 4.6 event's `share`, `spent_usd` and `limit_usd`, and for `"refused"` the `BudgetExceeded`'s `model` (the model, or the procedure's ID, whose hold or entry was refused), `spent_usd`, `held_usd`, `estimate_usd`, `limit_usd` (its budget's) and `unbounded`. It has no `attempt`, `final`, `outcome`, token or cost key, so a reader of attempt records skips it by its `budget_event` key, as `report` does (8.3 v1.598), and no attempt record has that key.
- v1.607 `pair_id` (str) and `shadow` (bool), in that order right after `slice` and before any cascade, procedure or `budget_moves` key (row CANARY1a, 7 v1.607): on every record of a shadowed call, the routed call's and its shadow's, budget records included, where they follow `tags`; `pair_id` is the routed call's `call_id` and `shadow` is `true` only on the shadow's records, whose `tags` hold `shadow: "true"`. No record of a call that is not shadowed has either key, so it keeps v1.606's keys
- v1.608 a shadow's `below_bar` and `below_bar_fallback` (row CANARY1g, review iter-457 should-fix 1, 7 v1.607): the shadow's attempt record takes both keys from the routed call's decision, as a record of a plain route entry of the shadow route does (v1.203). `below_bar` is the decision's flag, so it is `true` on the shadow's record too when nothing cleared the bar and a named `shadow_route` was shadowed, and `below_bar_fallback: true` is written, right after `below_bar`, exactly when the shadow route is one of the decision's `below_bar_fallbacks`. Only a named `shadow_route` can be one, since the default shadow route `passes` (7 v1.607), and only on a task with `fallback_below_bar` whose route holds that model within `max_fallbacks` (5.3). A named route that is not one of them gets no key: one that passes, or one that does not pass and that the route does not hold (the option off, a candidate past `max_fallbacks`, or one with no trials), since the key names the route's below-bar fallbacks and not every model that does not pass. So the record of such a shadow of a model that does not pass, behind a decision whose `below_bar` is false, does not say its model was under the bar, against the reading of v1.203 above, and `below_bar_calls` does not count it; whether the pair file records a shadow's own standing is row CANARY1b's. With `shadow=False`, its default, `report` counts in `below_bar_calls` (8.3 v1.203) a shadow call whose attempt is `ok` and whose record has `below_bar` or `below_bar_fallback` true, as it counts a shadow call as a call of its own (7 v1.607); with `shadow=True` it counts routed calls alone (8.3 v1.611, row CANARY1c). The code, and every record that is not a shadow's, keep v1.607's keys and values.
- v1.609 a skipped shadow (rows CANARY1h and CANARY1i, 7 v1.609): a shadowed call whose routed answer came from the shadow route's model writes the routed call's records alone, each with `pair_id` and `shadow: false`, and no record with `shadow: true` and that `pair_id`. With a monitor, a shadow that is sent writes at least one record under its own call ID (its attempt record, or its refused budget record, 7 v1.607) unless a bug's exception propagates from it to the caller, so a `pair_id` with no shadow record is a skipped pair, whose answer is the shadow route's own. Whether the pair file records such a pair, and how, is row CANARY1b's; `report` counts the call once, as the routed call it is.
- v1.618 `checked` (bool), right after `shadow` (row CANARY1l, 7 v1.618): on every record that carries `pair_id` and `shadow` (v1.607), budget records included, so the three keys come in the order `pair_id`, `shadow`, `checked`, still right after `slice` and before any cascade, procedure or `budget_moves` key, and right after `tags` on a budget record. It is `true` when the shadowed call was given a `validate` and `false` when it was not, on the routed call's records and the shadow's alike. A record of a call that is not shadowed has none of the three keys, as from v1.607, and a log written before v1.618 has `pair_id` and `shadow` without `checked`, a record that 8.3 v1.618 reads as v1.610 read every record.
- v1.639 `pinned_by` (str), right after `basis` and before `tags` (row PIN1a, 7 v1.639): on every attempt record of a pinned call, the call's tag. The same record's `basis` is `"pinned"`, which says the route was the caller's pin and not ranked, and its `below_bar` says whether the pin ran under the bar. Budget records (v1.598) take no key. No record of a call that is not pinned has the key, so it keeps v1.638's keys.
- v1.642 `policy` (str), right after `basis` and any `pinned_by` and before `tags` (row POL2a, 7 v1.642): on every attempt record of a call under a policy whose `label` (5.1 v1.642) is not None, that label, so a pinned call's record under a policy holds `basis`, `pinned_by`, `policy` and `tags` in that order; on that call's budget records (v1.598) right after `task` and before `tags`. Its value is the policy's name when it has one, else `sha256:` and the digest of its rules, and a name never starts with `sha256:`. No record of a call under no policy or `Policy()`, and no record of `.call_delegated`, has the key, so each keeps v1.641's keys; `report` (8.3) read no `policy` key in v1.642, so its rows and the CLI `report` output were unchanged; from v1.643 `by="policy"` groups by it (8.3 v1.643, row POL2b).
### 8.2 `Monitor(path=None)`
- `.record(rec: dict)` appends to `.records` (a list) and, when `path` is set, appends one JSON line to that file
- `load_records(path) -> list[dict]` reads a JSONL file, skipping blank lines. v1.1: a non-blank line that is not valid JSON, or is valid JSON but not an object, raises `ValueError` whose message contains the path and the 1-based line number (for example `calls.jsonl:3`)
- v1.569 `load_audits(path) -> dict[str, bool]` (row CPS1b): reads a JSONL file of audits, one line per audited call, skipping blank lines as `load_records` does, into a dict from each line's `call_id` to its `correct`, in file order. Each non-blank line is a JSON object with `call_id` (a non-empty string) and `correct` (JSON `true` or `false`); other keys are ignored, so an audit may carry its grader or a note. A line that is not valid JSON or not an object, lacks either key, has a `call_id` that is not a non-empty string or a `correct` that is not a JSON boolean (`1`, `"true"` and `null` are not), or repeats the `call_id` of an earlier line raises `ValueError` whose message holds `<path>:<line number>`, as `load_records` does. Exported right after `load_records` in `__all__`
- v1.616 threads (row PROD1c, 7 v1.616): a `Monitor` holds a `threading.Lock`, and `.record` holds it from its append to `.records` through the close of the file, so a `Monitor` shared by threads writes each record as one whole line, never two lines mixed, and `.records` and the file hold the records in one order. The file is still opened in append mode for each record, so two `Monitor` objects on one path, or two processes, are not guarded by the lock: give each process a log of its own. While calls run, `.records` holds the records written so far, so `report(monitor.records)` reads a call's records whole only once that call has returned.
- v1.620 `load_logs(paths) -> list[dict]` (row PROD1d): the logs of many processes, or the files of a rotated log, as one record stream. `paths` is a non-empty list or tuple of paths, each a `str` or a `Path` (anything else, a bare path included, raises `ValueError` before any file is opened); each file is read with `load_records`' rules (a bad line raises `ValueError` naming `<path>:<line number>`, a missing file `OSError`), in the order given, and the records are returned in that order, so `report` (8.3) sums over all of them and `shadow_pairs` (8.3 v1.610) joins a pair whose routed and shadow records are in different files. A `call_id` found in two files is read as one call's records, in the order given: the default `id_factory` (7) returns random hex, so two processes do not share an ID, and the files of a log rotated between two attempts of one call do; give such files in the order they were written, since 8.3 reads a call's first record before its last. An injected `id_factory` whose IDs repeat across processes is the caller's to avoid. But a record equal to a record of an earlier file, compared as `json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True)`, raises `ValueError` naming both `<path>:<line number>`s, since one attempt written to two files is a log given twice or a copy of one, which would count its calls and its spend twice. No record is compared with another of its own file, so `load_logs([path])` returns `load_records(path)`. Exported right after `load_audits` in `__all__`

### 8.3 `report(records, by="model") -> list[dict]`
- `by` is `"model"`, `"task"`, `"flavor"`, `"family"`, or `"tag:<key>"` (records without that tag group under `"(none)"`), and the keys the v1.584, v1.640 and v1.643 bullets below add; anything else raises `ValueError`
- Attempt-level sums per group use each attempt's own value: `attempts`, `ok`, `errors`, `invalid`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cost_usd`, `routing_cost_usd` (costs rounded to 6 decimals)
- Call-level metrics use the call's FINAL attempt to pick the group: `calls` (calls whose final attempt is in the group), `failed_calls` (final outcome not ok), `fallback_calls` (final attempt index > 0; v1.579: a final record of another route entry than the call's first record, below), `fallback_rate` (`fallback_calls / calls`, 0.0 when no calls)
- `p50_latency_ms`, `p95_latency_ms`: nearest-rank percentile over the group's `ok` attempts (sorted ascending, index `ceil(q * n) - 1`), `None` when there are none
- Each row is a dict with key `group` plus the keys above; rows sorted by descending `cost_usd`, then `group`
- v1.203 `below_bar_calls`: a call-level count by the same final-attempt rule, the calls whose final attempt is `ok` on a model under the bar (8.1: its `below_bar` is `true`, or its `below_bar_fallback` is `true`), so the calls whose answer the bar did not cover. A call with no `ok` attempt counts in `failed_calls` and not here. Only a JSON `true` counts in either key (v1.205): a missing key, `false`, `null`, `1` or the string `"true"` reads as false, so on a log written before v1.203 the count is the `ok` calls of `best_available` routes. Every row has the key, 0 when none, as its last key (after `p95_latency_ms`)
- v1.569 `report(records, by="model", audits=None)` (row CPS1b): `audits` maps a `call_id` to whether an audit found that call's answer correct (`load_audits`, 8.2). With `None`, the default, every row is v1.568's, key for key. Otherwise each row gains four keys after `below_bar_calls`, in this order, each by the final-attempt rule of `calls`: `audited_calls`, the group's calls whose `call_id` is a key of `audits`; `correct_calls`, those whose final attempt's outcome is `ok` and whose audit is `True` (only `True` counts, so `1` or `"true"` does not; an `ok` call with no audit, the unvalidated case, never counts, nor does a call whose final attempt failed, whatever its audit says); `cost_per_success_usd`, the `cost_usd` of every attempt of the group's calls (each record with the call's `call_id`, so a failed attempt on another model before a fallback is charged to the call's final group too), summed with `math.fsum`, over `correct_calls`, rounded to 6 decimals; and `successes_per_100k_tokens`, `correct_calls * 100000` over the summed `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` of those same attempts, rounded to 6 decimals. Both are `None`, never 0, when `audited_calls < calls` (the group's audit coverage is incomplete); `cost_per_success_usd` is also `None` when `correct_calls` is 0, and `successes_per_100k_tokens` when one of those attempts lacks a token count key (a `null` count raises `TypeError` in the attempt sums, as in v1.568) or their sum is 0, and it is 0.0 when every call is audited and none is correct. An audit whose `call_id` is on no final record is ignored, so one audit file can serve several logs; the attempts of a `call_id` with no final record belong to no call; and two final records with one `call_id` raise `ValueError` naming it, since the join could not tell their audits apart. A group with no calls has 0, 0, `None` and `None`
- v1.578 procedures (row PROC1c): `report` reads none of the 8.1 v1.578 keys and is unchanged. It charges a procedure's tool cost through its closing record's `cost_usd`, so `--by model` gives the tool cost to the row of the procedure's `.id` and its model calls to its model's row, and the rows of a call add up to what it spent. Two limits, as for a cascade (7 v1.537): the closing record of an entry that made a model call has attempt index 1 or more, so the call counts in `fallback_calls` and `fallback_rate` even when the procedure was the primary, the `procedure` key telling it from a fallback (row RPT2, lifted by v1.579 below); and its `latency_ms`, the whole run's, enters the percentiles of its group, so a `--by task`, `--by flavor` or `--by family` group mixes it with its model calls' own
- v1.579 route entries (row RPT2, review iter-425 should-fix 2): `fallback_calls` counts a call when its final record belongs to another route entry than its first record, so a call whose first entry is a cascade that handed up (7 v1.537) or a procedure that made model calls (8.1 v1.578) is no fallback call when that entry gave its final record, and a call that moved on from either, or onto either, is one. Each record's entry is read from the record alone, so no record gains a key: a record with a `cascade` key belongs to that cascade (the key's value); one with a `procedure` key and no `model_calls` key, a model call's record, to `proc:<procedure>@<procedure_version>+<model>`; a closing record, one with both keys, to its `model`, the procedure's `.id`; any other record to its `model`. A call's first record is the latest record with its `call_id` and an `attempt` equal to 0 at or before its final record in the order `report` reads them, so logs appended one after another keep a reused `call_id` apart and the calls of one log may interleave; a `call_id` that is a JSON array or object matches no record, as it cannot be a dict key, a missing `call_id` reads as null, and values equal as dict keys (`1`, `1.0` and `true`) are one `call_id`. A final record whose attempt index is 0 is its call's first, no fallback as before; one above 0 with neither a `cascade` nor a `procedure` key is a fallback, as in v1.577, since a plain entry writes one record, so the call's first record belonged to an earlier entry even when it names the same model; one above 0 with either key is a fallback when its entry differs from its call's first record's, or when no first record of its call is at or before it (v1.577's count). So every log without `cascade` and `procedure` keys gives v1.577's rows key for key, `fallback_rate` stays `fallback_calls / calls`, and the CLI `report` table, every evidence file and README transcript keep their bytes; v1.578's first limit above is lifted and its second, the closing record's latency, stays
- v1.584 `by="pricing_basis"` (row SELF1c): groups each record under its `pricing_basis` key as a string, and a record without the key (every record of a list-priced model, a procedure's closing record and every record written before v1.584) under `"list"`, so a log's spend splits into what self-hosted models cost by their hour and the rest. The `ValueError` for an unknown `by` names `pricing_basis` right after `family`. Every other `by` gives v1.583's rows, key for key
- v1.590 `report(records, by="model", audits=None, cache=False)` (row CACHE1f): with `cache=False`, the default, every row is v1.589's, key for key. With `cache=True` each row gains three last keys, after `below_bar_calls` and after v1.569's four when `audits` is given too, in this order, each summed by the attempt-level rule of `input_tokens` (each record in its own group): `cached_input_tokens`, the summed `cached_input_tokens` (8.1 v1.589) of the group's records that carry that key; `cache_counted_input_tokens`, the summed `input_tokens` of those same records; and `cache_hit_rate`, the first over the second, rounded to 6 decimals, so 9,000 cached of 10,000 input tokens gives 0.9. A record without the key (an error record, a procedure's closing record, every record of a provider that returns no count and every record written before v1.589) is unknown: it adds to neither sum and is never read as a miss. So both sums are 0 and the rate is `None`, never 0, when no record of the group carries the key, and the rate is also `None` when their `input_tokens` sum to 0; a group whose records say 0 cached of a positive count has rate 0.0. `cache_write_tokens` enters no part of the rate, since a write is no read from the cache: it is never read, so any value of it raises nothing, and a record carrying it alone is unknown. A carried `cached_input_tokens` that is not an integer >= 0 (a bool, a float such as `900.0` or `null` is not one) or is above its record's `input_tokens` (read as the attempt sums read it, a missing one as 0) raises `ValueError` naming the record's `call_id`, as no record the executor writes holds one (7 v1.589); with `cache=False` no record's key is read, so nothing new raises
- v1.598 budget records (row B1e): `report` drops every record with a `budget_event` key (8.1 v1.598) before it reads any, so with any `by`, `audits` and `cache` a log's rows are those of its attempt records alone, key for key, and a log without budget records gives v1.597's rows. `budget_report(records, budgets) -> list[dict]`, exported right after `report`, gives each budget's spend in each window as a percent of its limit, the row's `budget_used_pct`, beside `report`, whose rows and signature are unchanged, since a budget's scope (a task, tags or both) cuts across `report`'s groups, so one budget's spend is no one group's (review iter-446 should-fix 4); `budgets` is a list or tuple of `Budget` with unique names, else `ValueError`. Its rows, in the budgets' order, are one for a `total` budget and, for a `day` or `month` budget, one per window, in ascending label order, that holds the `ts` of one of its attempt records or is the `window`, a `str`, of one of its budget records, none when it has neither; a `total` budget's row counts its budget records whose `window` is null. Each row has, in order, `budget`, `window` (the label, or None for `total`), `mode`, `limit_usd`; `spent_usd`, the `math.fsum` of `cost_usd` (a missing one 0.0) over the attempt records the budget applies to (`Budget.applies` on the record's `task` and `tags`, missing tags read as `{}`) whose `ts`, read as 4.6 reads `at`, is in the window, rounded to 6 decimals; `budget_used_pct`, 100 times that sum, unrounded, over `limit_usd`, rounded to 6 decimals; and `warn_records` and `refused_records`, the counts of the budget records with that `budget`, that `window` and that `budget_event`; a budget record whose `budget_event` is neither is ignored (review iter-446 nit 5). None without `audits`, with no audited call, or when `items_needed` gives None (a rate at or under a bar above 0, or 10,000 items not clearing). Like the saving, it assumes such a route and checks none.
  - Keys, in order: v1.645's through `cost_per_day_usd` and, with `audits`, `cost_per_success_usd`; then with `router`, `route` and `route_list_cost_usd`; then with a target, `target_cost_per_call_usd` and `saving_per_day_usd`, as in v1.645; then with `router` and a target, `items_to_admit`, last. The sort is v1.645's.
  - Checks, after v1.645's target check: `router` is None or a `Router`, else `ValueError` before any record is read; with one, every row's task must be a task of `router.tasks`, else `ValueError` naming each one that is not, sorted, before any row is returned, as `select` refuses an unknown task (`KeyError`, 5); any other error `select` raises propagates.
  - Unchanged: with `router` None every v1.645 row keeps its keys and values; `report`, `select` and every other function are unchanged, and no evidence or research script, README transcript or workflow calls `opportunities`, so every evidence file and transcript keeps its bytes.
  - Tests (tests/test_opportunities_route.py): a written log of four tasks on a two-model registry by hand count, one admitted on the cheaper model, one on the dearer, one with no measured route under `refuse` and one below the bar under `best_available`; agreement with `select`; a `retry_same` task whose primary is not the cheapest per call, a prior decision and a bar of 0 (review iter-501 should-fix 1 and nit 1); the items at rates 1.0 and 2/3, raised to `min_samples` and not, and None without audits; the keys in order; no router keeping v1.645's rows; an unknown task and a bad router; the CLI table, `--json`, a price warning and its exit-2 cases; the note's two lines.
  - Not in this version: the README sentence, which v1.654 adds (5.2). `model_routing.__all__` is unchanged.

## 9. Data files
- `model_routing/data/models.json`: `{"version": str, "as_of": "YYYY-MM-DD", "currency": "USD", "models": [{"id", "family", "price_in", "price_out", "context_window", "source"}]}`; IDs are provider-neutral (`vendor/model-name`); map them to a provider's IDs with `aliases`; extra keys such as `notes` are allowed and ignored by `Registry.load`; `aliases` is optional; v1.15: `price_valid_until` is optional (format in 4.1) and is set on a row whose vendor page states an end date for the price, such as a promotional rate (the packaged `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` row: `2026-11-21`)
- v1.212 `price_tiers` (format in 4.1) is optional and is set on a row whose vendor page gives a higher price for long prompts. Two packaged rows carry one tier each: `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`, `above_input_tokens` 100000, `price_in` 0.5, `price_out` 2.5 (its page: 0.10 and 0.50 "for prompts up to 100,000 tokens", 0.50 and 2.50 "for prompts over 100,000 tokens", the prompt length counting all input tokens); `openai/gpt-6-astra`, 272000, 20 and 75 (its page: "Prompts with more than 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output for the full request", 272K read as 272,000). The `xai/grok-4.7` page says that requests over its 200K context are charged different rates and gives no rate, so to v1.454 its row had no `price_tiers` and kept its note (v1.455 below). All three pages were read on 2026-11-10 and agree with the rows' 2026-10-29 `notes`; no base price changed, so `version` and `as_of` stay `2026.10.29` and `2026-10-29`, and every README transcript keeps its bytes (no packaged task's expected input reaches 100,000 tokens). README, as v1.212 wrote it (restated since, last by v1.455 below): the pricing notes under the capability table opened with `Pricing notes (a row's price_tiers in models.json prices a long-prompt tier whose page states its rates; see Limitations):` with `price_tiers` and `models.json` backticked; the claude-haiku-5.5 and gpt-6-astra notes each added that the row priced the tier, with its threshold; the grok-4.7 note added that its page did not state the higher rates, so its row had no tier; and the Limitations bullet that said cost is linear and tiers are not modelled was replaced by one that said a tier is priced per call where `models.json` gives it, named the two costs that stayed at the base prices (grok-4.7 above 200K, and the inline-or-delegate cost of 13.2) and the over-statement for a task whose line is a conversation. Tests: `tests/test_price_tiers.py`
- v1.572 `variants` (format in 4.1, row VAR1a) is optional, and no packaged row has one, so the packaged registry's models and every packaged decision are v1.571's
- v1.581 `pricing_basis` (format in 4.1, row SELF1a) is optional, and no packaged row sets it, so every packaged row is `list` and the packaged registry's models and every packaged decision are v1.580's
- v1.582 `deployment` and `base_model` (format in 4.1, row SELF1b) are optional, and no packaged row sets them, so every packaged model is `api` with no base and every packaged decision is v1.581's
- v1.586 `scope_tasks` (format in 4.1, row SCOPE1) is optional, and no packaged row sets it, so every packaged model is a candidate on every task and every packaged decision is v1.585's
- v1.587 `price_cached_in` and `price_cache_write` (format in 4.1, row CACHE1a) are optional, and no packaged row sets them, so a packaged model would price a cached read or a cache write at its input price, and since no package module passes a cache count, every packaged decision is v1.586's
- v1.455 the `xai/grok-4.7` tier (row P4): the page's text says only that requests which exceed the 200K context window are charged different rates, and its HTML embeds three price objects whose `name` is exactly `grok-4.7`, one per cluster. Two give the same prices, `promptTextTokenPrice` 20000, `cachedPromptTokenPrice` 5000 and `completionTextTokenPrice` 60000, the visible 2.00, 0.50 and 6.00 USD per 1M input, cached input and output tokens, so one unit is 0.0001 USD per 1M tokens, and with them `longContextThreshold` 200000, `promptTextTokenPriceLongContext` 40000 and `completionTokenPriceLongContext` 120000, beside a `maxPromptLength` of 500000, the row's `context_window`, so the threshold is read as a prompt length, as on the other two tiers; the third is 10% higher on every price (22000, 5500 and 66000 at the base), so it is not read (4.1 v1.455). So the row gains `price_tiers` `[{"above_input_tokens": 200000, "price_in": 4, "price_out": 12}]` and its `notes` become `price for context up to 200K tokens; longer prompts cost 4.00 in and 12.00 out, from the price data its page embeds (read 2026-11-17)`. A call over 200,000 input tokens pays 4 and 12 on all of its tokens, as 4.1 prices every tier, since the page names the request, not its tokens over the threshold. The page was read on 2026-11-17 and its base prices are the row's, so `version` and `as_of` stay; no packaged task's expected input reaches 100,000 tokens and no committed results file prices the packaged `xai/grok-4.7` row (every evidence registry is its own, and the registry pair reads only its two `openai/` rows), so every README transcript and results file keeps its bytes. README: the pricing notes' opening says `whose page gives its rates` where v1.212 said `states`; the grok-4.7 pricing note gives the tier's rates and says the page gives them in its embedded price data but not in its text; and the Limitations long-prompt bullet, in place of naming a cost still at the base prices, says where those rates come from and that the threshold counting input tokens and the whole request paying the tier are readings, not stated, so 13.9's v1.242 clause on that bullet holds to v1.454. Tests: `tests/test_price_tiers.py`, `tests/test_delegation_eval_tiers.py`
- v1.417 a price error in the README (row DOC30, the Recommendation of the 12.22 v1.403 note): README Limitations' prices bullet gives, in one sentence right after the one that asks the reader to refresh `models.json` and check the model the gateway serves, how far a wrong price moves `cost_effective` routing, from `research/price-sensitivity.md`, which it links: on LLMRouterBench, with one model's price halved or doubled, one model at a time, the most picks that changed, one per (task, seed) cell, as a count of the cells and a share, the range of the held-out success gap and, apart from it, the highest cost ratio, at the lowest committed bar and then at the highest; then that a price is to be refreshed whenever its vendor changes it, most of all for a task with a low bar, at no fixed interval, since the note measures what a wrong price does, not how often prices change. Its numbers are the note's own: the two bars, the cells per bar, which are its tasks times its seeds, each bar's highest changed count, success gap range and highest cost ratio from its closing `over the` line, and each share, that count over the cells to one decimal, the share the script prints beside it, all of which tests/test_research_price_sensitivity.py reads from the note's Results block to build the sentence, pinned once in that place; the bars are the lowest and highest of `evidence/llmrouterbench/results.json`. No code, cost, committed result or README transcript changes
- v1.428 a price error in a delegation decision in the README (row DOC36, the Recommendation of the 13.16 v1.424 note): README Limitations' prices bullet gives, in one sentence right after the v1.417 one, how far a wrong price moves `cost_effective` delegation decisions, from `research/delegation-price-sensitivity.md`, which it links: with one model's prices halved or doubled, one model at a time, the largest share of a bar's `cost_effective` cells that a run changes on each of the four delegation datasets, over all of its grids, from the least moved to the most, the Response Bank's saying that all of its changed cells are on one task, and that no `cost_blind` cell moves, since that flavor compares no costs; then that a small effect on one dataset bounds none on another. Each share is the one the note's Results blocks print, which tests/test_research_delegation_price_sensitivity.py reads from them to build the sentence, pinned once in that place, checking on the way that the order is from the least to the most and that the Response Bank's changed cells are all of one task; the note's Recommendation says that README Limitations links it. No code, cost, committed result or README transcript changes
- `model_routing/data/priors.json`: format in 4.4; each category cites one public leaderboard with its date
- `model_routing/data/example_tasks.json`: three judge tasks (`faithfulness_judge`, `code_correctness_judge`, `pairwise_preference_judge`) whose generator-independence and bars are realistic, and, from v1.2, three non-judge tasks from different domains that check no other model's output and set `independent_of_generator` to `false` to document that intent: `support_ticket_triage` (classification), `invoice_field_extraction` (structured extraction) and `unit_test_codegen` (code generation, accepted when the generated tests pass). For `invoice_field_extraction` an item is accepted only when every field matches exactly, which is why its bar is 0.95. `support_ticket_triage` uses `professional_writing` as the closest packaged prior; priors only order cold-start candidates (4.4). Every packaged task routes in both flavors against the packaged registry once its candidates have passing stats
- v1.90 `tool_calling_support_agent`, a fourth non-judge task, from a fourth domain (a tool-calling agent), with `independent_of_generator` `false` since it checks no other model's output: one item is one whole conversation in which the agent serves a customer by calling tools, accepted when the program checks on the conversation's end state pass, as tau2-bench scores its runs (12.14). Its values, and the reason for each:
  - `bar` 0.7, the bar of `unit_test_codegen`, the other packaged task that program checks accept. The 2025 agents of the tau2-bench evidence reach 0.368 to 0.798 per domain at trial 0 (12.14), so 0.7 is above every airline and telecom rate and below two of the four retail ones (0.737 and 0.798)
  - `min_samples` 50: each sample is a whole conversation of 2 to 100 model calls (median 14 over the 834 per-call rows of 12.14 v1.76), so it costs more to label than a one-call sample, and 50 is the size of the smallest of the three pinned tau2-bench domains (airline, 50 tasks, 12.14). At 50 a model clears 0.7 only with 42 or more successes (Wilson lower bound 0.7149 at 42 and 0.6920 at 41, 4.3)
  - `expected_input_tokens` 89,000 and `expected_output_tokens` 1,500, to two significant figures the medians of the 1,112 trial-0 conversations of the four tau2-bench agents read with `--tokens` (12.14), each the sum over the conversation's agent calls: 88,833.5 input and 1,532 output tokens, against means of 118,822.7 and 2,671.0, which conversations of up to 2,096,093 input tokens pull up. The router prices this task per conversation, so a calibration row records a conversation's sums (README Calibrate step 2), and from then on each model is priced at its own mean (5.2 v1.33). Rule 5 of 5.2 reads these sizes as one call, so here it compares the conversation's summed reads, which count every re-read of the history, with each context window: a stricter test than any one call of the conversation needs. Every packaged window is at least 500,000 tokens, so no packaged model fails it
  - `timeout_s` 120.0, as for `unit_test_codegen`, the longest of the packaged tasks until v1.282 gave `math_final_answer` 440.0: `Executor.call` (7) passes it to each provider call and runs no tool loop, so for this task it limits one call of the agent's loop, which can read the whole conversation so far, not the conversation
  - `on_no_model` `refuse`: the agent's tool calls change records, such as a booking or an order, so when no model clears the bar the caller gets `NoModelClearsBar` and can hand the conversation to a person rather than run it on a model below the bar
  - `prior_category` none, as for `invoice_field_extraction`: no packaged category (4.4) scores conversational tool use, and none of the four tau2-bench agents is in `models.json` (12.14), so the evidence gives no prior either. 5.3 reads a prior only on the `best_available` path, so on this `refuse` task a prior would order nothing
  - `max_fallbacks` 2, as for every packaged task
  - README: Calibrate step 1 says the file ships three judge tasks and four from other domains and lists `tool_calling_support_agent` after the other three; step 2 gains, after the `unit_test_codegen` sentence, "For `tool_calling_support_agent` a line is one whole conversation: `correct` means the checks on its end state passed, and its token counts are the sums over the conversation's model calls."
  - Tests: `tests/test_registry_tasks_data.py` checks the task's values, the Wilson numbers above from `wilson_lower_bound`, the smallest packaged window, every candidate passing in both flavors once it has passing stats, and the README Calibrate lines that name it; when the 12 pinned tau2-bench files are in the default cache (12.14), one more test rebuilds from them the token medians, means and maximum above, requiring the rounded medians in the task, and the retail rates above the bar (CI never downloads the files, so there it skips)
- v1.282 `math_final_answer`, a fifth non-judge task, from a fifth domain (exact-answer math), with `independent_of_generator` `false` since it checks no other model's output: one item is one problem with a known answer, accepted when the final answer in the output agrees with the key's answer, a check a program makes with no person or judge, as LLMRouterBench grades its `aime` records against the reference answer by a math-equivalence test (research/check-fallback.md). Its values, and the reason for each, come from the 780 `aime` cells of the pinned LLMRouterBench file (13 models, 60 items, 12.18), none scored 0.5 (the 12.18 report's `half_scores` is 0 there):
  - `bar` 0.8, the bar of `code_correctness_judge`. On the 60 items the 13 models reach 0.367 to 0.883, and 0.8 is below five of those rates (`openai/gpt-5` 0.883, `qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507` 0.867, `deepseek/deepseek-r1-0528` 0.85, `google/gemini-2.5-pro` 0.85 and `z-ai/glm-4.6` 0.817) and above the other eight
  - `min_samples` 100, as for `support_ticket_triage`: a label costs only the call it grades, since a program compares the answer with the key, so a set this size is cheap wherever the answers are known. At 100 a model clears 0.8 only with 88 or more successes (Wilson lower bound 0.8019 at 88 and 0.7902 at 87, 4.3), a rate of 0.88, which only the best `aime` rate (0.883) reaches; at 60, the size of `aime`, it needs 55 (0.917), above all 13 rates, so those 60 items alone could show none of the 13 clears the bar
  - `expected_input_tokens` 160 and `expected_output_tokens` 5,500, to two significant figures the medians of the 768 cells with a `cost_usd` above 0, each one call's `prompt_tokens` and `completion_tokens` (12.18): 159.5 input and 5,455.5 output tokens, against means of 184.2 and 9,785.3, which outputs of up to 65,543 tokens pull up. The other 12 cells, all misses, record 0 output tokens and a cost of 0 (11 of them 0 input tokens too), so they give no size. Per model the median output runs from 1,280 (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`) to 17,721 tokens (`qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507`), 13.8 times as many, so a calibration line with token counts (README Calibrate step 2) matters here: from then on each model is priced at its own mean (5.2 v1.33) instead of at 5,500
  - `timeout_s` 440.0, the longest of the packaged tasks: the 120 s of `unit_test_codegen` scaled by the ratio of the two tasks' expected outputs, 5,500 to 1,500, since a call's time grows with what it writes and LLMRouterBench records no time per call. `Executor.call` (7) passes it to each provider call, so it limits one answer
  - `on_no_model` `best_available`: a final answer changes no record, unlike the agent task's tool calls, so when no model clears the bar the caller gets the best available model, with `below_bar` true (5.3), and decides what to do with its answer
  - `prior_category` `abstract_reasoning` (ARC-AGI-3, 4.4), the closest packaged category, as `professional_writing` is for `support_ticket_triage`: none scores math, and none of the 13 LLMRouterBench models is in `models.json` (12.18), so the evidence gives no prior. 5.3 reads a prior only on the `best_available` path, so here it orders the cold-start candidates, and `model-routing select math_final_answer` with no stats gives a route with `basis: prior`
  - `max_fallbacks` 2, as for every packaged task
  - README: Calibrate step 1 says the file ships three judge tasks and five from other domains and lists `math_final_answer` after `tool_calling_support_agent`; step 2 gains, after the `tool_calling_support_agent` sentence, "For `math_final_answer` a line can give the final answer as `prediction` and the key's answer as `gold`, both in one form (for example an integer), so the `==` comparison is the exact-answer check."
  - Tests: `tests/test_registry_tasks_data.py` checks the task's values, its row last in the file with its `prior_category`, the timeout rule, the Wilson numbers above from `wilson_lower_bound`, every candidate passing in both flavors once it has passing stats, the prior route and the `select` command without stats, and the README Calibrate lines that name it; `tests/test_price_tiers.py` counts eight packaged tasks; when the pinned LLMRouterBench file is in the default cache, one more test rebuilds from the converter's rows (the 12.19 session fixture, so the file is still read once per run) the cell counts, the rates and the five models above the bar, and the medians, means, maximum and per-model spread above, requiring the rounded medians in the task (CI never downloads the file, so there it skips)

## 10. CLI (`model-routing`, entry point `model_routing.cli:main(argv=None, *, today=None) -> int`)
- `select TASK [--flavor cost_effective|cost_blind] [--generator MODEL] [--exclude MODEL ...] [--prompt-tokens N] [--slice S] [--policy FILE] [--registry PATH] [--tasks PATH] [--stats PATH] [--priors PATH] [--window Nd --log PATH [--log PATH ...] --audits PATH] [--json]`
  - prints primary, fallbacks, basis, below_bar and a candidate table; `--json` prints `RouteDecision.to_dict()`
  - v1.201: on the `fallbacks:` line each model of `below_bar_fallbacks` (5.3) is followed by ` (below bar)`, for example `fallbacks: fiction/dear, fiction/few (below bar)`; a decision without one prints v1.200's bytes
- v1.507 `select ... [--prompt-tokens N]` (row FIT1): passes `prompt_tokens=N` to `select` (5.2), so the candidate table and `--json` show which models cannot hold a request of N tokens; without the option the output is v1.506's bytes. N must be an integer of at least 0: anything else is a usage error that prints the usage line and `error: argument --prompt-tokens: must be an integer >= 0, got '<text>'` on stderr, nothing on stdout, and exits 2. `delegate` gains no such option
- v1.511 `select ... [--slice S]` (row STRAT1): passes `slice=S` to `select` (5.2); the text output gains a `slice:     S` line right after the `task:` line, `--json` the `slice` key (5.1), and the synopsis above names `[--slice S]` after `[--prompt-tokens N]` from row STRAT1b; without the option the output is v1.510's bytes. An empty S, or one that holds `@`, is a usage error that prints the usage line and `error: argument --slice: must be a non-empty name without '@', got '<text>'` on stderr, nothing on stdout, and exits 2; the two task checks of 5.2 exit 2 with one `error:` line. `calibrate` reads `slice` through `calibrate_from_results` (4.3), and `delegate` gains no such option
- v1.567 `select` (row CPS1a): for a task whose `failure_policy` is not `"none"` the text output gains, right after the `below_bar:` line, `policy:    <policy>, expected cost per success $X (an estimate assuming independent retries)`, X to 6 decimal places or `n/a` when the value is None, and then `pick:      cheaper_per_success` when `pick_reason` is set; `--json` gains the 5.1 keys. Every other task's output is v1.566's bytes
- v1.573 `select` (row VAR1c): when some candidate's route has `items_per_call` above 1 (4.1), the candidate table, on stdout or after the exit-3 `error:` line on stderr, gains an `items` column right before `list_cost`, each route's `items_per_call`, and right after the table the line `list_cost and routing_cost are per item; items is how many items one call of the route handles`. `--json` keeps v1.572's keys, its costs being the table's. A decision with no such route prints v1.572's bytes, so every README transcript is unchanged
- v1.584 `select` (row SELF1c): when some candidate's `pricing_basis` is `"self_hosted"` (5.1 v1.584), the candidate table, on stdout or after the exit-3 `error:` line on stderr, gains a `pricing_basis` column right before `list_cost`, after `items` when that column is shown (v1.573): each registry model's basis, and `-` for a cascade or a procedure; `--json` gains the 5.1 key. A decision with no such candidate prints v1.583's bytes, so every README transcript is unchanged. `report --by pricing_basis` groups as 8.3 v1.584
- v1.625 `select ... [--policy FILE]` (row POL1d): reads FILE as UTF-8 JSON, one object whose keys are among `allowed_routes`, `allowed_families`, `region` and `require_zdr`, each optional, with the meaning and types of 5.1 v1.622: a list of strings, or `null` for no limit, for each of the first two, a string for `region` and `true` or `false` for `require_zdr`; it builds `Policy(**object)` and passes it as `policy=` to `select` (5.2 v1.622), so `{}` is `Policy()`, and the synopsis above names `[--policy FILE]` after `[--slice S]`. The file is read once the registry, tasks, stats and priors are loaded and the `--generator` and `--exclude` IDs checked, right before `select`, and each failure exits 2 with one `error:` line on stderr, its last, and nothing on stdout: a missing or unreadable file and bad JSON as for the other files; a value that is not an object, `error: FILE: expected a JSON object of policy keys, got T`, T its JSON type (`array`, `string`, `number`, `boolean` or `null`); an unknown key, `error: FILE: unknown policy keys K; a policy holds allowed_routes, allowed_families, region and require_zdr`, K the unknown keys sorted, as a Python list, checked before any value; and a value `Policy` refuses, `error: FILE: ` and its `ValueError` message. No ID of the policy is checked against the registry, since a cascade's or a procedure's own ID is a route too (5.2 v1.622), so an ID that names no route allows nothing. The output keeps its form: a route the policy rules out shows `policy_excluded`, `region_unavailable` or `zdr_required` in the candidate table's `reason` column and in `--json`, and when no route is left the command exits 3 with the `error:` line and that table on stderr, as for any other rule. The price expiry warnings (v1.411) read the eligible candidates only, so a model the policy rules out never warns. With `{}`, or without the option, every output is v1.624's bytes, and no README transcript passes the option, so every transcript is unchanged.
  - Tests (tests/test_policy_cli.py): `--policy FILE` in the help of `select` and `delegate`; a tenant in one region with one family disabled getting the cheapest allowed route in each flavor, the fallbacks inside the allowed set and each reason in the table, stdout byte for byte what `select(..., policy=Policy(**object))` prints; an allow-list naming no route exiting 3; each bad file exiting 2 with its line, and the `--exclude` check coming first; a ruled-out model with an expired price not warning; `{}` and no option giving the sha256 of every `select` and `delegate` output over the shipped tasks in both flavors taken on v1.624 (1cb1645); no README transcript, evidence or research script or workflow passing `--policy`
- v1.630 the latency bar (row LAT1c, 5.2 v1.628): no option is added, since the bar is a task's (4.2 v1.628), read from `--tasks`, and a route's times come from `--stats` (4.3 v1.626). Under a bar `select --json` prints `max_p95_ms` right before `candidates` and each candidate's `p95_latency_ms`, a number or `null`, as its last key, and `delegate --json` the same inside its `route` (5.1 v1.628, 13.7); the text output names `too_slow` or `latency_unknown` in the candidate table's `reason` column, which `select` prints and `delegate` prints only on exit 3 (review iter-483 nit 1), and gains no column, so the p95 a route was judged on is shown by `--json` alone. `calibrate --results` keeps a row's `latency_ms` in the stats file it writes (4.3 v1.626), so a team with a results file and no Python holds a route to a bar with `calibrate` and then `select`. A task whose row sets no bar prints v1.629's bytes on every command, with or without `latency_unknown`.
  - Tests (tests/test_latency_docs.py): results rows with `latency_ms` through `calibrate`, then `select --json` naming the cheaper route `too_slow` with each candidate's p95 and the next one picked, the text table naming the reason under the same header as without a bar, `delegate --json` holding the bar in its `route`, `deny` ruling the untimed route out as `latency_unknown`, and a row whose bar is `null` printing the bytes of a row without the keys
- v1.643 `select ... [--policy FILE]` reads `name` (row POL2b, 5.1 v1.642): the object's keys are among `allowed_routes`, `allowed_families`, `region`, `require_zdr` and `name`, the fields of `Policy` in order, `name` a string or `null` with the checks of 5.1 v1.642, so `{"name": "tenant-a", "region": "eu-west"}` is `Policy(region="eu-west", name="tenant-a")`. An unknown key's line becomes `error: FILE: unknown policy keys K; a policy holds allowed_routes, allowed_families, region, require_zdr and name`, still checked before any value, and a name `Policy` refuses (not a string, empty, or starting with `sha256:`) exits 2 with `error: FILE: ` and its `ValueError` message, as any value `Policy` refuses (v1.625). Before any file is read, `--window` without both `--log` and `--audits` exits 2 with `error: --window needs --log and --audits: the window's stats come from the logs' audited calls`, and `--log` or `--audits` without `--window` with `error: --log and --audits need --window: select reads them only for a window's stats`. The window's stats are read where `--stats` is, after the registry and the tasks, so their failures exit 2 as `drift`'s do, and the output keeps its form: `select --window ...` prints the bytes `select --stats FILE` prints for a FILE holding the window's stats. Without `--window`, `--log` and `--audits` every output is v1.633's bytes, and no README transcript, evidence or research script or workflow passes `--window` or runs `drift`, so every transcript and evidence file keeps its bytes; README `## Layout` names `drift` among the subcommands.
  - Tests (tests/test_drift_cli.py): the options in each command's help and none in `delegate`'s; `drift --json` equal to `drift_check` on the stats file and the window's stats, writing no file; the text output byte for byte; a route at 0.92 all-time and 0.70 in the window flagged `fell_below` and losing admission under `select --window`, whose stdout is `select --stats` on the window's stats; a rise flagged once; the window's UTC edges and its 30-day default; the all-time counts of the logs without `--stats`; `--log` once per log; each bad `--window`, option combination and file exiting 2 with its line; the sha256 of every `select` output over the shipped tasks in both flavors taken on v1.633 (c3e0c6c).
  - Not in this version: README's paragraph on the command, its Limitations line, DESIGN 14's deferral and the note's GitHub line (row M1e, which v1.635 adds, 5.2 and 14); a cascade's or a procedure's route, which `audited_results` gives no row (row M1d, which v1.636 adds, 8.3).
- `demo [--out DIR] [--budgets FILE]`: runs `run_demo` and prints its summary (v1.12: the inline-or-sub-agent lines are pinned in 11; v1.599 `--budgets`, below)
  - v1.599 `--budgets FILE` (row B1f): reads FILE with `load_budgets` (4.6) before the demo writes anything, so a missing file, bad JSON or a bad budget exits 2 with one `error:` line on stderr, nothing on stdout and no file written, and runs `run_demo(DIR, budgets=...)` (11 v1.599). When a call raises `BudgetExceeded` (a `refuse` budget, or a `downgrade` one with no route entry left to move to, 7 v1.596), the demo ends at that call and the command exits 4 with one line on stderr, `error: ` and the exception's message, which names the budget, its limit, the model refused and the amounts its check read, and nothing on stdout; `calls.jsonl` keeps the records written before, its last line that call's refused budget record (8.1 v1.598). Otherwise it prints the summary lines of 11 up to the hand-off lines and then, right before the `log:` line, a blank line, `budgets:` and a table of the rows of `budget_report` (8.3 v1.598) over the `calls.jsonl` it wrote, in their order, with columns `budget`, `window` (the label, `total` for a `total` budget), `mode`, `limit_usd` and `spent_usd` (6 decimals), `budget_used_pct` (1 decimal), `warn_records` and `refused_records`; a file whose `budgets` list is empty prints the two lines and the table's header and rule. Without the option every line and file is v1.598's, so every README transcript is unchanged
- `evaluate --outcomes PATH ...` (v1.3): offline evaluation; options, output and exit codes in 12.4
- `delegate TASK --parent MODEL ...` (v1.4): inline or sub-agent for one piece of work; options, output and exit codes in 13.7
- `plan --success P --bar B [--confidence C] [--max-items N]` (v1.140): the calibration items per model of 4.3 `items_needed`, `--confidence` default 0.95 and `--max-items` default 10000. It prints six `key: value` lines with the values in one column (each key padded to 13 characters): `success`, `bar` and `confidence` as Python prints the parsed floats, then `items` (the count), `successes` (`floor(items * s)`, 4.3) and `lower_bound` (`wilson_lower_bound` at those counts, 6 decimals), and exits 0. When no count up to `--max-items` clears, its fourth line is `items:       none up to --max-items N` and it prints nothing after it and exits 3. An invalid value (for example a success outside [0, 1], a confidence of 1 or `nan`) exits 2 with one `error:` line on stderr and nothing on stdout
- Defaults: `--registry` and `--priors` and `--tasks` point at the packaged files under `model_routing.DATA_DIR`; `--stats stats.json` in the current directory (a missing stats file means empty stats; a missing priors file means no priors)
- Exit codes: 0 success; 2 bad input (missing file, bad JSON, unknown task or model, invalid value); 3 `NoModelClearsBar` on `select` and `delegate`, on `plan` no count up to `--max-items` that clears (v1.140), and on `promote` a challenger the bar does not admit (v1.603); 4 a `BudgetExceeded` that ends a call of `demo --budgets` (v1.599)
- v1.1: every `--exclude` ID and the `--generator` ID must exist in the loaded registry, else exit 2; `calibrate` validates every result row before writing, so bad input leaves an existing stats file byte-identical and creates no new one
- v1.15 price expiry warnings: once `select` or `delegate` has printed its decision (exit 0) or the candidate table of `NoModelClearsBar` (exit 3), it prints on stderr, after all its other output, one line for each model in `Registry.expired_prices(today)` of the loaded registry that the v1.411 scope bullet below names, in file order: `warning: list price of MODEL was stated valid through YYYY-MM-DD; check the vendor page and update the registry`. Up to v1.410 that was every expired model, on the reading that every registry model is a candidate of the decision (5.3), but a model that 5.2 rules 1 to 5 rule out is a candidate whose price no choice reads (row P2b). stdout is unchanged, `--json` included, so every README transcript is too. A run that exits 2 prints no warning, so its `error:` line stays the last line (13.7)
- v1.15 `today` is a `datetime.date`; `None` means `datetime.date.today()` when `main` runs, and any other type raises `TypeError` before the command runs, so nothing is printed. `calibrate`, `report` and `demo` read no registry prices, so they never warn. `evaluate` warns from v1.411, for the models of its token-form rows only (below and 12.4); up to v1.410 it did not, as matrix rows normally carry their own `cost_usd`
- v1.411 warning scope (row P2b): a run warns only for an expired model whose price its result can depend on, and for the `delegate` parent on every run, exit 3 included, where no cost is printed, so the rule reads no row of 13.5. `select`: each model whose candidate (5.1) is `eligible` in the decision it prints or, on exit 3, in the `.candidates` of `NoModelClearsBar`. A model that 5.2 rules 1 to 5 rule out (an `--exclude` ID, a family in the task's `exclude_families`, the generator or its family on an `independent_of_generator` task, a window too small) is chosen at no price, since those rules read none; its `list_cost` is still in the candidate table, unflagged. `delegate`: the parent, since its price gives `inline_cost_usd` (13.2) whether or not `--exclude` names it, and each `eligible` candidate of the delegate's `select` (13.3), from `route.candidates` or, on exit 3, the `.candidates` of `NoModelClearsBar`; when that `select` found no route and the command exits 0 (`route` is `None`), no delegate was priced, so the parent alone. Each model warns at most once, in registry file order, and the line, its place after all other output and the exit-2 rule are v1.15's, so a run in which every candidate is eligible (and, for `delegate`, there is a route) prints v1.410's lines
- v1.411 `evaluate` (12.4): once it has printed its tables or its `--json` result (exit 0), it prints the same line for each model of `Registry.expired_prices(today)` of `--registry` that has at least one row of the outcome file in token form (12.1: no `cost_usd`, so priced with `registry.get(model).cost`), each once, in registry file order. Those prices give every cost of the model's token-form rows: its mean calibration cost, which `cost_effective` routes on (12.3), and the `cost_usd` columns. A model whose rows all carry `cost_usd` never warns, as no cost of it comes from the registry; a run that exits 2 prints no warning, and stdout is unchanged

## 11. Demo (`demo.py`)
- `run_demo(out_dir: str | Path, seed: int = 7) -> dict` uses `FakeProvider` and clearly fictional models (`demo/` prefix) so no one mistakes simulated accuracy for a real measurement: four judges in two families with different prices and true accuracies, one generator in a third family
- Steps: build a 300-item synthetic labeled calibration set; calibrate every judge; select in both flavors; run 200 judge calls per flavor with a simulated outage on a fraction of the primary's calls; write `calls.jsonl` and `stats.json` to `out_dir`
- v1.5: `run_demo` also writes `outcomes.jsonl`, the same calibration set as an outcome matrix in the 12.1 format so `model-routing evaluate` has a ready input: one row per (judge, item), judges in the demo's order and items in order within each judge, item IDs `item-000` to `item-299`, `correct` when the judge's prediction equals the gold label, and `cost_usd` equal to `model.cost(1000, 200)` (the demo task's expected tokens). Each judge's correct count equals its successes in `stats.json`. Writing it draws no random numbers, so `calls.jsonl`, `stats.json` and the summary are unchanged
- v1.9: `run_demo` also writes its registry as `models.json` (the four judges in the demo's order, then the generator, each row with `id`, `family`, `price_in`, `price_out` and `context_window` in the 9 file format) and its task as `tasks.json` (one task with every 4.2 field, `slices` (v1.511) and `cascades` (v1.535) only when set), so `select` and `delegate` run on the demo's output with `--registry`, `--tasks` and `--stats` pointing into `out_dir`. `Registry.load` and `load_tasks` read them back equal to the demo's registry and task. Writing them draws no random numbers, so the other files and the summary are unchanged
  - v1.202: since `tasks.json` holds every 4.2 field, it gains `"fallback_below_bar": false` as its last key, the one change v1.201 makes to the demo's output (the `timeout_s` line before it gains a comma); `calls.jsonl`, `stats.json`, `outcomes.jsonl`, `models.json` and the summary keep their bytes, and the demo task keeps the option off
- v1.12: after both flavors' 200 calls, `run_demo` asks `Router.decide_delegation` one question in each flavor, in summary order: a `demo/atlas-max` parent (module constant `DELEGATION_PARENT`) 60,000 tokens into a session (`DELEGATION_CONTEXT_TOKENS`) reaches one call of the demo task, with `brief_tokens=400`, `result_tokens=60`, `generator_model` the demo generator and the other options at their defaults. It is the question of the first README `delegate` transcript (13.8). A `delegate` decision is run once through `Executor.call_delegated` (7) with the demo's validator, tags `{"suite": "demo", "dataset": "synthetic"}` and call ID `<flavor>-delegated-0001`, and the simulated outage applies to its route's primary as it does to any primary. An inline decision runs nothing, because inline work happens in the parent's own call. With seed 7, `cost_effective` delegates to `demo/atlas-mid` (`delegate_cheaper`) and `cost_blind` stays inline (`inline_as_good`)
  - The hand-off's records follow the 400 judge-call records in `calls.jsonl` and its random draws come after theirs, so those records, `stats.json`, the other files and every pre-v1.12 summary value are unchanged: each flavor's `calls`, `fallback_calls` and `cost_usd` still count its 200 judge calls only. `report --by flavor` over `calls.jsonl` counts the hand-off under its flavor; `--by tag:delegated` splits it out
  - Each flavor's summary gains `delegation`, a dict with keys in this order: `parent`, `context_tokens`, `mode`, `model`, `reason`, `inline_cost_usd`, `delegate_cost_usd` (the decision's values, not rounded), `hand_off_calls` (1 for a delegate decision, 0 for inline) and `hand_off_cost_usd` (the list-price cost of the hand-off's attempts rounded to 6 decimals, `0.0` for inline)
  - The `demo` CLI prints every pre-v1.12 line unchanged up to and including the spend line, then a blank line, `inline or sub-agent, a <parent> parent at <context_tokens with comma thousands separators> context tokens:`, one line per flavor in summary order (two spaces, `<flavor>:` padded with spaces to 15 characters, one space, `delegate to <model>` or `inline on <model>`, then ` (<reason>), inline <inline_cost_usd> vs delegate <delegate_cost_usd> USD` with 6 decimals and `-` for `None`), then `  hand-off calls: <sum of hand_off_calls>, list-price USD <sum of hand_off_cost_usd, 4 decimals>`. The `log:` line stays last
- Returns a summary dict with keys `cost_effective` and `cost_blind`, each holding `primary`, `fallbacks`, `calls`, `fallback_calls`, `cost_usd` (from v1.12 also `delegation`, below); deterministic for a given seed
- v1.1 safety: `run_demo` writes an empty marker file `.model-routing-demo` into `out_dir`. If `out_dir` already contains `calls.jsonl` or `stats.json` (from v1.5 also `outcomes.jsonl`, from v1.9 also `models.json` or `tasks.json`) and has no marker, it raises `FileExistsError` and modifies nothing (CLI exit 2). With the marker present it replaces its own previous output
- v1.599 (row B1f): `run_demo(out_dir, seed=7, budgets=None)`. `budgets` is None or a list or tuple of `Budget` (4.6), checked by `BudgetLedger(budgets)` before any file is written, so a bad value raises `ValueError` and modifies nothing. With budgets, one `BudgetLedger` of them goes to every executor of the run, both flavors' 200 judge calls and the hand-offs, so a budget counts their spend together; a budget's scope reads task `demo_faithfulness_judge` and the tags `{"suite": "demo", "dataset": "synthetic"}`, a hand-off's also `delegated` and `parent` (7 v1.11), and each executor's `now` is the simulated clock's timestamp, so a `day` budget's window is `2026-01-01` and a `month` budget's `2026-01`. The executors write each warn crossing and refusal to `calls.jsonl` as a budget record (7 and 8.1 v1.598), and the summary and each `delegation` count the attempt records alone, so a run in which no budget refuses or moves a call returns v1.598's summary and writes v1.598's attempt lines in order, the budget records among them (a budget record reads `now` and draws no random number). A `BudgetExceeded` is not caught (only `AllModelsFailed` is), so it ends the run, the files written before it kept. With `budgets` None nothing changes
- v1.580 (row PROC1d): `run_procedure_demo() -> dict`, in `demo.py` and not in `__all__` (a worked example, not an API), routes a fictional recurring job, submit, poll and fetch, between an agent route that does it by model turns and a procedure that does it in code (4.5). `run_demo`, its files and the `demo` CLI keep every byte, so no README transcript changes. It writes no file, draws no random number and reads no clock: each executor's `clock` returns 0.0, its `now` `2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`
  - Fixtures (module constants): the registry holds `demo/atlas-mid` alone (`PROCEDURE_MODEL`, its `JUDGES` row); task `demo_job_summary` (`PROCEDURE_TASK`), bar 0.8, `min_samples` 30, `max_fallbacks` 1, the other fields at their defaults. Job `i` is done at its `2 + i % 4`-th status poll and holds `30 + (7 * i) % 20` rows, row `k` of amount `(31 * i + 17 * k) % 100`; its raw payload is one line `row <k>: amount <a>` per row, joined by newlines, and its answer `job <i>: <rows> rows, total <sum>`. A call's messages are one user message `Run job <i> and report its row count and total.`, and its `validate` accepts exactly job `i`'s answer
  - The agent route is `demo/atlas-mid`, and its one provider call stands for a whole agent run: the fake provider answers it with the tokens its turns would bill, a submit turn, one turn per poll, a fetch turn and an answer turn, 20 output tokens each, each turn's input the context so far: the request's `estimate_prompt_tokens`, plus 20 for each earlier turn's output, 12 for each earlier submit or poll result and, after the fetch turn, the payload's estimate (its characters over 4, rounded up). It gives job `i`'s answer, except that when `i % 20 == 19` it reports one row fewer with the true total (a misread; review iter-427 nit 4)
  - Two procedures name `demo/atlas-mid`, each with `max_model_calls=1` and `max_tool_calls=8`, each submit, poll and fetch one tool call at 0.00001 USD (`PROCEDURE_TOOL_COST_USD`). `job-summary@1` polls at most 3 times and then fetches, and a fetch before the job is done returns its first `rows // 2` rows; `job-summary@2` polls until the job is done. Each then counts the rows and sums the amounts in code and makes one model call whose one message is `Write one line: <answer>.` for what it counted, which the fake provider answers with the text between `Write one line: ` and the final period, at that message's estimate in and 20 tokens out. So the raw payload never enters a model call
  - Calibration: each of the three routes runs jobs 0 to 39 (`PROCEDURE_JOBS`) once outside the executor, one `calibrate_from_results` row per run, `correct` by the job's check: the agent's with its completion's tokens, a procedure's with `cost_usd`, its model call's list price plus its tool calls' cost. With these fixtures the agent passes 38 of 40, `@1` 20 of 40 (it fetches early on every job that needs 4 or 5 polls) and `@2` 40 of 40
  - Stages, each `select(PROCEDURE_TASK, flavor="cost_effective", procedures=[p])`, in this order: `cold`, on the agent's rows, `p` = `@2`; `below_bar`, on the agent's and `@1`'s rows, `p` = `@1`; `admitted`, on all three routes' rows, `p` = `@2`. Each is a dict `stage`, `procedure` (`p.id`), `reason` (its candidate's reason), `primary`; they give `insufficient_samples`, `below_bar` and `passes`, with primary `demo/atlas-mid`, `demo/atlas-mid` and `@2`'s ID
  - Routed calls: on the `admitted` stats, jobs 40 to 59 (`PROCEDURE_CALLS` = 20) run once through `Executor.call(..., procedures=[@2])` and once with no procedures, each path with its own `Monitor`, call IDs `procedure-0001` and `agent-0001` onward; an `AllModelsFailed` is caught, as `run_demo` does. `routed` holds `procedure` and then `agent`, each a dict `route` (its first call's decision primary), `calls`, `fallback_calls`, `failed_calls` (from `report(records, by="task")`, 8.3 v1.579), `cost_usd` (its records' sum, rounded to 6 decimals) and `input_tokens` (its records' sum). The procedure path makes 20 calls with no fallback and no failure; the agent path fails job 59
  - Returns `{"task", "bar", "stages", "routed"}` in that order, the same on every run. Test status: `tests/test_procedure_demo.py`; its contract tests were committed under strict xfail and the implementing commit removes the marks; review iter-427's nits 1 to 3 added the calibration counts, the tool calls, an agent run's tokens, the two paths' exact cost and input tokens, the shaping message's exact form and the digests of all five `run_demo` files

## 12. Offline evaluation (`evaluate.py`, v1.3)
Purpose: show from a public outcome matrix, with no API key, whether routing at a bar holds that bar on items it never saw, and what it costs next to simple baselines. The evaluator routes through `Router.select`, so the evidence exercises the shipped rules (min_samples, the Wilson admission rule, the 5.3 sort keys) and not a re-implementation of them.

Size budget of sections 12 and 13 (v1.386, row DOC21): at 6c79574 DESIGN.md is 660,506 bytes, `## 12.` 353,758 of them and `## 13.` 238,905 (89.7% together), because each slice that added a dataset, a research note or a README trim wrote the history of its values and rules into the subsections it touched, while CHANGELOG.md holds each version's change already. As the 12.8 size budget (v1.334) does for the README evidence section:
- Measure, as in the 12.8 size budget (v1.335): a subsection is the UTF-8 bytes from its `### 12.N` or `### 13.N` heading line, included, through the line before the next `##` or `###` heading, each line with its newline, so a `####` line stays inside it and the blank line before the next heading counts; a section runs from its `##` line to the next `##` line; a line is measured without its newline.
