### 12.1 Outcome matrix
- JSONL, one object per (task, item, model): `task` (str), `item` (str), `model` (str), `correct` (bool, strict as in 4.3), and the cost of that one call as either `cost_usd` (an int or float that is not a bool, finite and `>= 0`) or both `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` (integers `>= 0` that are not bools), priced with `registry.get(model).cost(input_tokens, output_tokens)`. When `cost_usd` is present it is used and token counts are ignored. Extra keys are ignored
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class Outcome`: `task: str`, `item: str`, `model: str`, `correct: bool`, `cost_usd: float`
- `outcomes_from_rows(rows: Iterable[dict], registry: Registry | None = None) -> tuple[Outcome, ...]`, in input order. `ValueError` for: a row that is not a dict; `task`, `item` or `model` missing or not a non-empty string; `correct` missing or not a bool; neither `cost_usd` nor both token counts; an invalid cost or token value; a token-form row when `registry` is `None` or does not contain the model; a repeated (task, item, model)
- `load_outcomes(path, registry: Registry | None = None) -> tuple[Outcome, ...]` reads JSONL and skips blank lines; a non-blank line that is not valid JSON, or is not an object, raises `ValueError` whose message contains `<path>:<line>` (1-based) as in 8.2; rows are then validated as above
- v1.514 slices (row STRAT2): `Outcome` gains a last field, `slice: str | None = None`, so an Outcome built with five positional arguments keeps its meaning. `outcomes_from_rows` and `load_outcomes` gain a keyword `slice_by=None`, the row key that holds each row's slice (`--slice-by FIELD`, 12.4); given, it is a non-empty `str`, else `ValueError`. A row's value at that key is its slice: absent or null is none; anything else must be a non-empty `str` that holds no `@`, on a row whose `task` holds no `@` (as a calibration row's `slice`, 4.3), else `ValueError` naming the row. Without `slice_by` every Outcome's slice is None and a `slice` key is an extra key, so every v1.513 call returns what it returned
- v1.538 cascade rows (row ESC4, DESIGN 7 v1.532): `Outcome` gains a last field, `escalated: bool | None = None`, after `slice`, so an Outcome built with six positional arguments keeps its meaning. A row whose `model` holds `>` is a cascade row: its `model` is a cascade `id` (7, `parse_cascade_id`), it carries `escalated` with `type(value) is bool` and neither `input_tokens` nor `output_tokens`, so its cost is `cost_usd`, the whole cascade's spend, and its Outcome's `escalated` is that bool. Any other row that carries `escalated`, null included, is refused, as `calibrate_from_results` refuses it (7), so the two read one file alike; each refusal is a `ValueError` naming the row. Before v1.538 `escalated` was an extra key and a row whose `model` held `>` reached `evaluate` as a model, whose `Stats.add` then raised `ValueError` (v1.535), so a file with no such row and no `escalated` key gives every v1.537 Outcome, `escalated` None
- v1.573 items per call (row VAR1c): a token-form row whose `model` is a route with `items_per_call` k above 1 (4.1) is one item carrying its whole call's counts (4.3 v1.573), so its cost is `registry.get(model).cost(input_tokens, output_tokens) / k`, the item's share as 5.2 v1.573 prices a measured route; a `cost_usd` is the caller's cost of the item and is used as given. With no such route in the registry every Outcome is v1.572's

### 12.2 Split
- `split_items(items: Iterable[str], seed: int, calibration_fraction: float = 0.5) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], tuple[str, ...]]` returns `(calibration, held_out)`, each sorted ascending with duplicates collapsed. An item is in calibration exactly when `int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(f"{seed}:{item}".encode("utf-8")).digest()[:8], "big") < calibration_fraction * 2**64`; otherwise it is held out. The split depends only on the seed and the item ID, so it is the same on every machine and for every row order
- `calibration_fraction` outside the open interval (0, 1) raises `ValueError`

### 12.3 `evaluate(outcomes, bars, seeds=range(10), flavors=("cost_effective", "cost_blind"), calibration_fraction=0.5, min_samples=30, confidence=0.95, cost_per_correct=False) -> dict`
- Checked before any work, each a `ValueError`: no outcomes; no bars, a bar that is a bool, not an int or float, not finite (so NaN is rejected) or outside [0, 1], or a repeated bar; no seeds, a seed that is a bool or not an int, or a repeated seed; no flavors, a name not in 5.1, or a repeated flavor; a `min_samples` that is a bool, not an int, or below 1, the message starting `min_samples must be an integer >= 1` (v1.261; before it `True` passed as 1 and a float such as 2.5 was taken); a `confidence` that is a bool, not an int or float, not finite or outside (0, 1), the message starting `confidence must be a finite number in (0, 1)` (v1.261; before it a string or `None` raised `TypeError`); `calibration_fraction` as in 12.2; a repeated (task, item, model) among the outcomes, the message naming it as `outcomes_from_rows` does (12.1) (v1.261; before it the last of them replaced the others, so Outcomes given to `evaluate` without `outcomes_from_rows` were never checked for a repeat); an incomplete matrix (every model that appears anywhere must have a row for every (task, item) pair that appears anywhere; the message names one missing (task, item, model)); a (task, seed) whose calibration or held-out split is empty (the message names the task and the seed)
- The empty-split rule is deliberately strict: a task with very few items would otherwise be scored on a handful of items in some seeds and not at all in others. When it trips, drop or enlarge that task, use fewer seeds, or move `calibration_fraction` toward 0.5
- One **cell** per (bar, flavor, seed, task), nested in that order: bars, flavors and seeds in the order given, tasks ascending. In a cell, C and H are the task's calibration and held-out items from `split_items(task_items, seed, calibration_fraction)`
  - calibration counts per model: successes = correct rows in C, trials = |C|; mean calibration cost = total cost over C divided by |C|
  - `routed`: the primary of `Router.select(task, flavor)` for a task with this `bar`, `min_samples` and `confidence` and `on_no_model="best_available"`, over a registry in which each model's list cost per call equals its mean calibration cost exactly (so `cost_effective` ranks by measured cost) and no model is excluded by rules 1 to 5 of 5.2. `cleared` is `not decision.below_bar`. v1.263: each model of that registry returns its mean from `cost` (and, v1.265, from `base_cost`) for a call of any size, and `research/check_fallback.py` and `research/below_bar_fallback.py` rebuild a cell's router over the same registry (`_routed_registry` of `model_routing/evaluate.py`, a private name on purpose: it is not in `__all__`, so the rule that public names keep working does not bind it, and the two scripts that import it live in this repo and change with it); before it each model was priced at its mean times 1,000,000 USD per million input tokens for a one-token task, so its list cost was `(mean * 1e6) / 1e6`, which is one ulp off the mean for some means and, though it keeps their order, maps some pairs of means one ulp apart to one cost (`0x1.47ae147ae1488p-7` and `0x1.47ae147ae1489p-7`, both near 0.01, become the second), a tie the 5.2 order then gave to the higher bound and then the lower model ID, where `cheapest` takes the lower mean
  - `cheapest`: the model with the lowest mean calibration cost, ties by model ID
  - `best_on_calibration`: the model with the highest calibration success rate, ties by lower mean calibration cost, then model ID (no bar and no confidence bound); v1.266: it is ranked on the calibration correct count, not on the rate as a float, since |C| is one number for every model of a (task, seed), so the two give the same order for any |C| below 2^52 and no cell changes
  - `oracle`: on each held-out item it is correct when any model is correct, and its cost is the lowest cost among the correct models on that item, or the lowest cost among all models when none is correct
  - `model:<id>` for every model in the matrix: that model on every held-out item
  - for every strategy, `success` = correct held-out items / |H| and `cost_usd` = total cost over H
  - v1.135, computed once per split: the calibration counts and mean calibration costs, each model's held-out correct count and cost, and the `oracle`'s held-out `success` and `cost_usd` depend only on the task and the seed, through C and H, never on the bar or the flavor; `routed`, `best_on_calibration` and `cheapest` take the held-out pair of the model they name, and only `Router.select` reads the bar and the flavor. So a run computes them once per (task, seed), the first time a cell needs them, and every later cell of that (task, seed), at any bar or flavor, reads the same integers and floats: per (task, seed), with M models, one `sum` per model over C and one over H (2M) and one `math.fsum` per model over C and one over H plus one for the `oracle` (2M + 1), and none per cell, where the v1.134 code made 2M + 3 and 2M + 4 per cell. No value is kept from one call to the next, and each cell has its own `models`, `success` and `cost_usd` dicts. Every cell, summary row and per-task row is the v1.134 one bit for bit
- Strategy order everywhere: `routed`, `oracle`, `best_on_calibration`, `cheapest`, then `model:<id>` by ascending ID
- Cell keys: `bar`, `flavor`, `seed`, `task`, `calibration_items` (int), `held_out_items` (int), `cleared` (bool), `models` (`{"routed": id, "best_on_calibration": id, "cheapest": id}`), and `success` and `cost_usd`, each a dict keyed by strategy name in strategy order
- Return value keys:
  - `config`: `bars`, `seeds` and `flavors` (lists, in the order given), `calibration_fraction`, `min_samples`, `confidence`
  - `tasks`: `{task: {"items": int, "models": [ids ascending]}}`
  - `cells`: the cells above, in cell order
  - `summary`: one row per (bar, flavor, strategy), in that order, with keys `bar`, `flavor`, `strategy`, `success` (mean over seeds of that seed's item-weighted held-out success across all tasks: total correct held-out items / total held-out items), `cost_usd` (mean over seeds of that seed's total held-out cost across all tasks), `below_bar_rate` (fraction of that strategy's (task, seed) cells whose held-out success is below the bar), `cleared_rate` (for `routed`, the fraction of cells with `cleared`) and `bar_violation_rate` (for `routed`, among cleared cells the fraction whose held-out success is below the bar, `None` when no cell cleared); the last two are `None` for every other strategy
  - `per_task`: one row per (bar, flavor, task, strategy), in that order, with the summary keys plus `task` and `routed_models`; `success` and `cost_usd` are means over seeds of that task's cell values, the three rates count that task's cells only, and `routed_models` is `{id: number of seeds routed to it}` for `routed` and `None` otherwise
- Arithmetic: every success rate and every rate is an integer count divided by an integer count (for the summary `success`, total correct held-out items over total held-out items, both integers). Every cost total, and the sum behind every mean, is computed with `math.fsum`, which is exactly rounded and so independent of summation order; a mean is that sum divided by its count. v1.266: the correct count a cell gives the summary is the held-out correct count of the model its strategy names (for `oracle`, the number of held-out items some model gets right), an integer carried from the (task, seed) sums of v1.135, never recovered as `round(success * held_out_items)` from the cell's rate. The cell keys stay as listed: no committed results file keeps cells (the CLI's `--json` drops them, 12.4), but `cells` is part of the return value, so the count stays internal
- Granularity: in `summary`, `success` and `cost_usd` weight every held-out item equally within a seed, while `below_bar_rate`, `cleared_rate` and `bar_violation_rate` count (task, seed) cells, so a small task weighs as much as a large one in the rates but not in `success`. `success` above the bar does not imply a zero `below_bar_rate`
- Deterministic: the same outcomes in any row order with the same arguments give an equal dict, and `json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True)` is byte-identical
- Reading the numbers: `wilson_lower_bound` is the lower end of a two-sided interval (4.3), so for one model judged once its nominal chance of admitting a true rate below the bar is about `(1 - confidence) / 2` (2.5% at 0.95), and that figure is approximate because Wilson coverage is not exact. Three things push the observed `bar_violation_rate` above it: the routed model is the cheapest (or best) of several passing models, and that selection favours models whose calibration rate came out high by chance; the held-out rate is itself a noisy estimate, so a model whose true rate sits just above the bar misses it on a small held-out set often; and the seeds are re-splits of one item pool, so cells are correlated rather than independent trials. Read the rate as a resampling estimate for this matrix, next to `(1 - confidence) / 2` and the held-out size, never as a guarantee and never against zero
- v1.514 slices (row STRAT2): a run in which no Outcome has a slice returns v1.513's dict, bit for bit. Otherwise these are checked with the others, before any work, each a `ValueError`: two rows of one (task, item) with different slices (the message names the task and the item, the first such pair in ascending order); a task with an item that has a slice and one that has none (it names the task and its first item with none, in ascending order); a (task, slice, seed) whose calibration or held-out part is empty, checked by task ascending, then seed in the order given, then slice ascending (the message is v1.3's empty-split one with ` slice '<S>'` after the quoted task name, for example `task 'support' slice 'lone', seed 0: the calibration or held-out split is empty`, v1.515). A task whose items have slices is sliced. Slice S's calibration and held-out items, C_S and H_S, are the items of C and H in S, so the split is the task's (12.2 reads only the seed and the item), and every key and row above is the unsliced run's. Added:
  - `tasks[task]` of a sliced task gains, after `models`, `slices`: `{slice: number of items}`, slices ascending
  - each cell of a sliced task gains a last key `slices`, `{slice: entry}` slices ascending, an entry's keys `calibration_items` (|C_S|), `held_out_items` (|H_S|), `cleared`, `models` (`{"pooled": id, "sliced": id}`), `success` and `cost_usd` (each `{"pooled": ..., "sliced": ...}`, over H_S as above). `pooled` is the cell's `routed` model. `sliced` is the primary of `Router.select(task, flavor, slice=S)` for the cell's task over `_routed_registry` of the models' mean calibration costs on C_S, with stats holding each model's counts on C_S under `<task>@<S>` (4.3), so the slice takes the run's bar and `min_samples` (5.2); `cleared` is that decision's `not below_bar`. The C_S and H_S sums are computed once per (task, seed), as v1.135
  - after `per_task`, `per_slice`: one row per (bar, flavor, sliced task, slice, strategy) in that order, slices ascending, strategy `pooled` then `sliced`, keys `bar`, `flavor`, `task`, `slice`, `strategy`, `success` and `cost_usd` (means over seeds of the entry's values), `below_bar_rate` (the fraction of seeds whose success is below the bar), `cleared_rate` (of seeds cleared: the cell's `cleared` for `pooled`, the entry's for `sliced`), `bar_violation_rate` (among cleared seeds, the fraction below the bar; `None` when none) and `routed_models` (`{id: seeds}`, ascending)
  - then `slice_summary`: one row per (bar, flavor, strategy), keys `bar`, `flavor`, `strategy`, `success` (mean over seeds of the correct held-out items over the held-out items of all sliced tasks), `cost_usd` (mean over seeds of their total held-out cost, one `fsum` over the items' costs, so with one task, sliced, `pooled` is `summary`'s `routed`, v1.517), `below_bar_rate`, `cleared_rate` and `bar_violation_rate` as in `per_slice` over every (sliced task, slice, seed), and `slice_miss_rate`: among the (sliced task, seed) pairs in which the strategy cleared (`pooled` the cell, `sliced` every slice) and its held-out success over H (its correct held-out items over |H|, integers, as v1.266) is at or above the bar, the fraction with some slice below the bar, `None` when there are none. That is the headline, how often a route that meets the bar on the task misses it on a slice, next to what the sliced route costs against the pooled one
  - Reading them: a slice is calibrated on its own items only, so a small slice gets a looser Wilson bound and may route to a dearer model than the pooled route, or, under `min_samples` calibration items, clear nothing (`cleared` false, the `best_available` pick on its counts) until it has enough items
- v1.538 cascades (row ESC4): a run with no Outcome whose `model` holds `>` returns v1.537's dict, bit for bit. Checked with the others, before any work, each a `ValueError`: 12.1's cascade-row rules on each Outcome, so one built in code is checked as a row is (a `model` holding `>` that is no cascade `id`; a cascade Outcome whose `escalated` is not a bool, `a cascade outcome needs escalated true or false`; an `escalated` that is not None elsewhere, `only a cascade outcome carries escalated`); a cascade whose cheap or strong model is not a model of the matrix (cascades ascending, cheap first, the message naming both). The single models are the matrix's models that are not cascades: `cheapest`, `best_on_calibration` and `oracle` range over them, so each stays a single-model baseline, while `model:<id>` covers every model, cascades included. `routed` is the primary of `select(task, flavor, cascades=True)` over `_routed_registry` of the single models, for a task whose `cascades` are the matrix's by ascending `id`, with stats holding each cascade's calibration successes, trials and escalated items under its `id`: a cascade clears by its own Wilson bound, and 5.2 prices it at its cheap model's mean calibration cost plus p times its strong model's, p its escalated share of C (every size costs the mean, v1.263), not at its rows' mean; every strategy's held-out success and cost are those of the rows of the model it names. A sliced cell's `sliced` decision takes the same cascades with their counts on C_S under `<task>@<S>`. Added:
  - each cell gains, after `cost_usd`, `escalation_share`, a dict in strategy order: for a strategy that names a cascade (`routed` when it routes to one, `model:<cascade>`), that cascade's escalated held-out items over |H|, and None for every other
  - each `summary` and `per_task` row gains a last key, `escalation_share`: over its cells whose value is not None, their escalated held-out items over their held-out items, integers, None when there are none, so `routed`'s is how often the cheap model escalated on the held-out items routed to a cascade
  - Not in this version: an escalation share in `per_slice` and `slice_summary` (row ESC5)
- v1.570 cost per correct item (row CPS1c): `evaluate` gains a last keyword, `cost_per_correct=False`; a value that is not a bool raises `ValueError` (`cost_per_correct must be True or False`) with the other checks. With True each `summary` and `per_task` row gains a last key, after `escalation_share` when there is one, `cost_per_correct_usd`: one `math.fsum` of its cells' held-out `cost_usd` over the sum of their held-out correct counts (integers, v1.266), `None` at 0 correct; `cost_usd` over the held-out items is the cost per call. Without it the dict is v1.569's, bit for bit; `per_slice` and `slice_summary` never gain it

### 12.4 CLI
- `model-routing evaluate --outcomes PATH [--bar B [B ...]] [--seeds K] [--flavor NAME [NAME ...]] [--calibration-fraction F] [--min-samples N] [--confidence C] [--registry PATH] [--slice-by FIELD] [--cost-per-correct] [--json]`
  - `--bar` takes one or more values and may be repeated (default `0.8`); `--seeds K` means seeds `0` to `K - 1` (default 10, `K >= 1`); `--registry` defaults to the packaged models.json and is only used to price token-form rows. v1.266: the parser checks `K`, so a value that is not an integer or is below 1 is an argparse usage error, the usage line on stderr and then `error: argument --seeds: must be an integer >= 1, got '<value>'` (exit 2), before any file is read; before v1.266 a value below 1 gave the command's one line `error: --seeds must be >= 1` and a value that is not an integer argparse's `invalid int value`
  - `--flavor` (v1.63) takes one or more flavor names of 5.1 and may be repeated, as `--bar`; the flavors run in the order given and are the result's `config.flavors`, and without the option both run, `cost_effective` then `cost_blind`, as every run did before v1.63. An unknown or repeated name is an invalid option value (exit 2): `evaluate` checks it (12.3), so it is reported after the outcome file is read. The option is for a matrix that records no cost, such as 12.16's, where a `cost_effective` run would rank every model as equally cheap; with one flavor the text output has one table per bar
  - prints one table per (bar, flavor) with a row per strategy and the columns success, cost_usd, below_bar_rate, cleared_rate and bar_violation_rate; `--json` prints the result without `cells` (keys `config`, `tasks`, `summary`, `per_task`) so a committed results file stays small
  - v1.5 text layout: for each (bar, flavor) in config order, a heading line `bar <bar>, <flavor>` (the bar as Python `str` prints it), then a table in the layout of the other commands (header, a dash row, one row per strategy in strategy order) with columns `strategy`, `success`, `cost_usd`, `below_bar_rate`, `cleared_rate`, `bar_violation_rate`, built from the `summary` rows; rates and success to 3 decimals, `cost_usd` to 4, `-` for `None`. One blank line between tables and none after the last
  - exit codes: 0 success; 2 bad input (missing or unreadable file, bad JSON, invalid row, incomplete matrix, empty split, invalid option value), with a one-line `error: ...` message on stderr as for the other commands; an error the parser finds (a missing `--outcomes`, an option value that does not parse, a bad `--seeds`, v1.266) prints the usage line before that `error: ...` line
- v1.411: after its output (exit 0), the price expiry warnings of section 10 for each expired model with a token-form row. The command reads the outcome file once, as `load_outcomes` does, and keeps which rows are in token form, so a row is read and priced once
- v1.514 `--slice-by FIELD` (row STRAT2) reads each row's slice from FIELD (12.1); a bad FIELD or row value is bad input (exit 2). `--json` keeps `per_slice` and `slice_summary`. In text, after each (bar, flavor) table of a sliced run, a blank line, the heading `bar <bar>, <flavor>, slices` and a table of that (bar, flavor)'s `slice_summary` rows with the columns above and `slice_miss_rate` last, in the same formats. Without the option the output is v1.513's
- v1.538 (row ESC4): when the outcomes hold a cascade row, each (bar, flavor) table gains a last column, `escalation_share`, from the `summary` rows in the rates' format (`-` for None), and `--json` keeps the key in `summary` and `per_task`; the slices table is unchanged. Without a cascade row the output is v1.537's
- v1.570 `--cost-per-correct` (row CPS1c) passes `cost_per_correct=True` (12.3): `--json` keeps the key in `summary` and `per_task`, and each (bar, flavor) table gains a last column, `cost_per_correct_usd`, to 6 decimals as `report`'s `cost_per_success_usd` (8.3), `-` for None; the slices table is unchanged. Without the option the output is v1.569's

### 12.6 Public evidence: the RouterBench converter (`evidence/routerbench/convert.py`, v1.6)
Purpose: turn a public dataset that already holds every model's output, correctness and cost per prompt into the 12.1 matrix, so the evaluator runs on third-party data with no API key. It lives outside the package: `model_routing` never imports it, it is standard library except that reading the frame needs pandas (the `evidence` extra), and the tests that need pandas use `pytest.importorskip`, so CI passes without it
- Source, pinned: dataset `withmartian/routerbench` on Hugging Face at revision `784021482c3f320c6619ed4b3bb3b41a21424fcb`, file `routerbench_0shot.pkl`, `SIZE = 99567659` bytes, `SHA256 = "ba4f77f19517610a707c374e99322d7750c30fc4ae7ff5527888595a1e65d36d"` (its LFS object ID). The RouterBench code is MIT licensed (https://github.com/withmartian/routerbench); the dataset card states no data licence, and the evidence README says so
- `default_cache_dir()` is `~/.cache/ai-model-routing-evidence/routerbench/` (from `Path.home()`), never inside the repo. `fetch(cache_dir=None) -> Path`: the file is `cache_dir / "routerbench_0shot.pkl"`. A present file is verified and used, and one that fails `verify` is a `ValueError` naming it and is left in place (delete it to download again); a missing file is downloaded with `urllib.request.urlopen` from `https://huggingface.co/datasets/withmartian/routerbench/resolve/<revision>/routerbench_0shot.pkl` into a `.part` file next to it, verified, then renamed, and the `.part` file is removed when the check fails
- `verify(path, size=SIZE, sha256=SHA256)`: `ValueError` naming the expected and the actual value when the byte size or the sha256 differs. Nothing is unpickled before it passes
- `RestrictedUnpickler(pickle.Unpickler)`, `restricted_load(fileobj)` and `load_frame(path)`; `load_frame` opens the file, runs `restricted_load` and turns any other exception raised while unpickling (an empty or truncated file, an allowed callable given bad arguments) into a `ValueError` naming the file, so only `pickle.UnpicklingError` and `ValueError` leave it. In `restricted_load`, `find_class` resolves only the (module, name) pairs in `ALLOWED_GLOBALS`, exactly the 11 globals the pinned file references (found with a static `pickletools` opcode scan, which runs no code): `builtins.slice`, `numpy.dtype`, `numpy.ndarray`, `numpy.core.multiarray._reconstruct`, `numpy.core.numeric._frombuffer`, `pandas._libs.internals._unpickle_block`, `pandas.core.frame.DataFrame`, `pandas.core.indexes.base.Index`, `pandas.core.indexes.base._new_Index`, `pandas.core.indexes.range.RangeIndex`, `pandas.core.internals.managers.BlockManager`. Any other global raises `pickle.UnpicklingError` naming it, with no module-prefix wildcard; names are checked as written, with no Python 2 name mapping (`fix_imports=False`), and persistent IDs are refused. Because the file is hash-pinned, the list only has to cover that one file; a pickle written by another pandas or numpy version is refused, not trusted
- `model_id(column) -> str`: a column name of the form `vendor/model` (one `/`, both sides non-empty) is kept as is, and any other name containing `/` is a `ValueError`; a name starting `claude-` becomes `anthropic/<name>` and one starting `gpt-` becomes `openai/<name>`; anything else is a `ValueError` rather than a guess
- `frame_columns(frame) -> dict[str, list]`: `ValueError` naming the type when `frame` has no `columns` attribute (a pickle that loads to something other than a frame); otherwise plain Python lists, from `.tolist()`, for `sample_id`, `eval_name` and, for every model column `<m>`, both `<m>` (the score) and `<m>|total_cost`. A model column is any column without `|` other than `sample_id`, `prompt`, `eval_name` and `oracle_model_to_route_to`. Prompts and responses are never read. `ValueError` when `sample_id` or `eval_name` is missing, there is no model column, or a model has no `|total_cost` column
- `convert(columns, pass_score=None, min_items=100) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]`, where `columns` is what `frame_columns` returns (any `dict[str, list]` of that shape):
  - `ValueError`, checked before any output: columns of different lengths; a `sample_id` that is not a non-empty string or is repeated; an `eval_name` that is not a non-empty string; a score that is a bool, not an int or float, NaN or outside [0, 1]; a cost that is a bool, not an int or float, not finite or below 0 (score and cost messages name the `sample_id` and the column); `pass_score` that is not `None` and is a bool, not an int or float, or outside (0, 1] (so NaN is rejected); `min_items` that is a bool, not an int, or below 1; a model column that `model_id` rejects, or two columns mapping to one ID
  - each source row is one item: task = `eval_name`, item = `sample_id`, and one output row per model with model = `model_id(column)`, `cost_usd` = the recorded `total_cost` as a float, with a negative zero written as `0.0`
  - scores and costs must be Python `int` or `float` values (a `float` subclass such as numpy's float64 counts); other numeric types such as numpy's int64 or float32 are rejected, which `.tolist()` never produces but a hand-built `columns` dict could
  - graded tasks: a task is graded when any of its scores, for any model, is not exactly 0 or 1. With `pass_score=None` a graded task is dropped; otherwise it is kept. In a kept task `correct` is `score >= pass_score` when `pass_score` is set and `score == 1` when it is not, which agree on 0 or 1 scores for every allowed `pass_score`. The pinned file's graded tasks (`grade-school-math` with scores in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}, `consensus_summary`, the `mtbench` tasks, `chinese_idioms`) do not document what a partial score means, so excluding them is the default and including them is the user's stated choice
  - small tasks: a task left with fewer than `min_items` items is dropped. The default 100 gives calibration and held-out halves of about 50 items, so in practice 12.3's empty-split rule does not trip and `min_samples = 30` can be met
  - output rows have the keys `task`, `item`, `model`, `correct`, `cost_usd` in that order, sorted by (task, item, model) as strings; they form the complete matrix 12.3 requires, and the result does not depend on the source row order
  - the report has keys `models` (IDs ascending), `kept`, `dropped_graded` and `dropped_small` (each `{task: number of items}` with tasks ascending) and `rows` (the number of output rows)
- `write_jsonl(rows, path)`: one `json.dumps(row)` per line, newline-terminated, in the given order
- CLI: `python evidence/routerbench/convert.py --out PATH [--cache DIR] [--pass-score T] [--min-items N]`, entry point `main(argv=None) -> int`. Options are checked first, so a bad one downloads nothing (`--out` must pass the 12.14 `--out` check, v1.174, row H4b; to v1.173 `--out` was not checked before the fetch, so a bad one failed only at the write or the rename, after the download and the unpickling); then it fetches, verifies, loads with `load_frame`, converts, writes `<out>.part`, prints the report as `json.dumps(report, indent=2)`, flushing stdout, and only then renames `<out>.part` onto `--out` (v1.94, as 13.11), so a write to stdout that fails (a closed pipe) is an I/O error that leaves `--out` as it was. After a `BrokenPipeError` from the print, stdout is pointed at `os.devnull` as in 13.11 (v1.150), so the process exits 2 with that one `error:` line, not 120 with two more lines from the interpreter's flush at exit. It returns 0 on success and 2 with exactly one `error: ...` line on stderr and nothing on stdout for a missing or invalid option, a size or hash mismatch, a refused global, a file that does not unpickle to a frame, invalid data or an I/O error, but for a rename that fails after the print, the one failure with the report already on stdout. The matrix is written to `<out>.part` and renamed onto `--out`; on any failure `--out` is not written and `<out>.part` is removed
- Reading it: the 11 models date from 2023 and the costs are the ones the dataset recorded at that time's prices; the evaluator routes per task (an `eval_name`), not per prompt

### 12.7 RouterBench results (`evidence/routerbench/results.py`, v1.7; slices v1.521)
Purpose: commit the evaluator's numbers on RouterBench in a file small enough to review, regenerated byte for byte from stated commands, with the tables in `RESULTS.md` checked against it by the test suite. Standard library only: it reads JSON and never imports pandas
- `reduce(result: dict) -> dict`: from an `evaluate` result (12.3, with or without `cells`, so the `evaluate --json` output too), a new dict with the keys `config`, `tasks`, `summary` and `per_task` in that order, where `per_task` keeps only the rows whose `strategy` is `routed`, in their order; `cells` and the other per-task strategies are left out so the file stays under about 300 KB. Values are copied unchanged and the input is not modified, so `reduce(reduce(r)) == reduce(r)`. `ValueError` naming the key when one of the four is missing
- `table(results: dict) -> str`: two tables in the layout of 12.4 (header, a dash row, one row per line, trailing spaces stripped), separated by one blank line, with no newline after the last:
  - routed: one row per (bar, flavor) in config order, from that block's `routed` summary row, with columns `bar` (as Python `str` prints it), `flavor`, `success`, `cost_usd`, `vs_best_model`, `cleared_rate` and `bar_violation_rate`; `vs_best_model` is the routed `cost_usd` divided by the best model's `cost_usd`
  - baselines: from the summary rows of the first (bar, flavor) in config order (held-out success and cost do not depend on the bar or the flavor), one row per strategy other than `routed`, in summary order, with columns `strategy`, `success` and `cost_usd`
  - the best model is the `model:<id>` row of that first block with the highest `success`, ties by lower `cost_usd`, then by strategy name
  - success, rates and `vs_best_model` to 3 decimals, `cost_usd` to 4; `-` for `None`, and for `vs_best_model` when the best model's cost is 0
  - `ValueError` when `config` or `summary` is missing, a (bar, flavor) in the config has no `routed` summary row, or the first block has no `model:` row
- Slices (v1.521, row STRAT3e): a result with `per_slice` and `slice_summary` (12.3 v1.514) keeps both after `per_task`, unchanged, and one with only one of them is a `ValueError` naming the other; with `slice_summary`, `table` adds a third table after one blank line: per (bar, flavor) in config order, its `slice_summary` rows in their order, with columns `bar`, `flavor` and then those of the CLI's slices table (12.4 v1.514), in the formats above, and a `ValueError` when a (bar, flavor) has none. Without either key the output is as before. Tests: `tests/test_evidence_results_slices.py`
- Cost per correct (v1.571, row CPS1d): `reduce` keeps a row's `cost_per_correct_usd` (12.3 v1.570) as it keeps its other keys. When some `summary` row has that key, `table` gives the routed and the baselines tables each a last column, `cost_per_correct_usd`, taken from the summary row the line is built from, to 6 decimals as in 12.4 v1.570 and `-` for None; a row either table reads that lacks the key is then a `ValueError` naming its bar, flavor and strategy, and the slices table never gains the column. When no summary row has the key the output is v1.570's, so every other committed `RESULTS.md` table keeps its bytes. Tests: `tests/test_evidence_results_cost_per_correct.py`
- CLI: `python evidence/routerbench/results.py --evaluate PATH --out PATH` writes `json.dumps(reduce(result), indent=2)` and a newline to `--out`, where `result` is the JSON object read from `--evaluate`; `python evidence/routerbench/results.py --table PATH` prints `table(results)` for the JSON object read from `PATH`. Exactly one of `--evaluate` and `--table` is given, and `--out` comes with `--evaluate` and never with `--table`. The file is written to `<out>.part` and renamed onto `--out` only after the write completes; on any failure an existing `--out` is left as it was, a new one is not created, and `<out>.part` is removed. Entry point `main(argv=None) -> int`: 0 on success, 2 with exactly one `error: ...` line on stderr and nothing on stdout for a usage error, a missing or unreadable file, invalid JSON, a JSON value that is not an object, a write or rename error, or a `ValueError` above; a carriage return or line feed inside the message (a path can contain one) is written as `\r` or `\n`, so the message stays on one line
- Committed: `evidence/routerbench/results.json`, from the default converter matrix (12.6) and `model-routing evaluate --bar 0.6 0.7 0.8 0.9 --seeds 50 --json` reduced as above, and `evidence/routerbench/RESULTS.md` with the regenerate commands, the caveats of 12.6 "Reading it", and the `table` output in a fenced `text` block whose first line is `$ python evidence/routerbench/results.py --table evidence/routerbench/results.json`. `tests/test_evidence_results.py` checks that the committed file is under 300,000 bytes, is exactly `json.dumps(reduce(itself), indent=2)` plus a newline, has that config, the converter's 11 model IDs on every task and its 65 tasks with their item counts (pinned by the sha256 of `json.dumps({task: items}, sort_keys=True)`, which matched the converter's `kept` report when the file was made), 28,281 items in all, unique summary and per-task keys and 50 seeds behind every `routed_models`, and that `RESULTS.md` contains that block with the current `table` output, so the published tables cannot drift from the published file
- CI: one Python version also installs the `evidence` extra and runs the converter tests, so the tests that need pandas run in CI and not only locally
- RESULTS.md prose (v1.18): `tests/test_evidence_results.py` also builds from the committed file, and requires verbatim in `RESULTS.md`, the intro counts (models, evals, prompts, seeds) and every number of the "Reading it" bullets: for `cost_effective` the first bar's cleared rate as a percentage to 1 decimal, its cost ratio to the best single model, its success and that model's, the last bar's cleared rate as a percentage and its cost ratio (the ratio must rise with the bar), and the lowest and highest bar-violation rate over the bars next to the nominal one-sided `(1 - confidence) / 2` and the confidence; for `cost_blind` its success and cost ratio, which must be the same at every bar, next to those of `best_on_calibration` and how much more it costs as a percentage to 1 decimal, with the words "the same success to three decimals" allowed only while both successes print the same to 3 decimals and `cost_blind` costs more; how many evals hold the fewest prompts and that count; the oracle's success and cost. No bullet may call `cost_blind` level with `best_on_calibration`
- Checks on the pinned file (v1.18): when the pinned pickle is found (the `ROUTERBENCH_PKL` path when that variable is set, else the default cache) and pandas is installed, the tests also rebuild, from the converter's output, the held-out half sizes of the evals with the fewest prompts over the seeds (the 12.2 split on their prompt IDs, as a lowest-to-highest range) and the graded-evals sensitivity counts (the graded evals dropped by default, the two that `--pass-score 0.75` brings back with their prompt counts, the rest still under 100 prompts, and that matrix's evals, prompts and rows), and require them verbatim in `RESULTS.md`; without `ROUTERBENCH_PKL` they skip when the file or pandas is missing, so CI never downloads the file, and with it set a missing file or a missing pandas is a failure, not a skip. The sensitivity run's routed numbers need an evaluate of about 20 seconds, so they are rebuilt only when `ROUTERBENCH_PKL` is set. The evaluate time and output size in the Regenerate paragraph are not checked
- README trim (v1.372, row DOC19k, to the 12.8 v1.334 size budget): from v1.373 the README subsection `### RouterBench` is 4,301 bytes by that budget's measure (4,731 at 0b3e142, cap 6,500 then) and holds, in this order: its heading; its four source bullets (the dataset, the licence, what was run, the full results), unchanged; the paragraph that defines held-out success, the ratios and the rates, and the routed and baselines tables, unchanged; `Reading it:` and its first two bullets, on the `cost_effective` rows and on the `cost_blind` rows, the pair the 12.8 v1.335 rule keeps; `Limits:` and its first bullet, on the model dates and the recorded costs, the one the 12.8 v1.334 Limits rule keeps; the line "The other limits are in [RESULTS.md](evidence/routerbench/RESULTS.md#caveats) `## Caveats` (routing per task, the MMLU share, what the converter drops) and its `## Sensitivity: graded evals` (the graded evals at a pass score), and the other Reading it bullets in its `## Reading it` (the bar-violation rate, the per-prompt oracle).", whose anchor is this file's `## Caveats` heading; and the regenerate paragraph and its five-line `bash` block, unchanged. Of the lines it drops, the bar-violation bullet is this file's third `## Reading it` bullet in other words and the per-task limit its second caveat in other words; the oracle bullet's two facts this file lacks, the highest routed success and the hindsight bound, join its fourth `## Reading it` bullet, which then opens "The per-prompt oracle reaches 0.959 at 1.9634 USD, against at most 0.819 for a routed row. It is a hindsight bound, and routing per eval gets nowhere near it"; and the MMLU-share and converter limits, which it lacks, become its third and fourth caveats, before the licence caveat, word for word but for `(57 of the 65)` in place of `(count above)` and `the sensitivity run above keeps` in place of `RESULTS.md has a sensitivity run that keeps`. The tests that required in the subsection (12.8 to v1.371) the kept-of-86 count, and the oracle's success and cost next to the highest routed success of either flavor at any bar, which must be at least 0.1 below the oracle's for "nowhere near", require each here and absent from the subsection; a test builds the third caveat's MMLU count from the committed file, and the subsection's only bullets after its source bullets are the three it keeps. With this trim `PENDING` is empty, so the README evidence section, 68,693 bytes from v1.373, is required at most 70,000 (12.8 v1.335)

### 12.8 README evidence section (v1.10; AutoBench v1.17; at a glance v1.23; judges v1.28; workflow v1.30; variant points v1.48; tau2-bench v1.55; LiveCodeBench v1.65; delegation on tau2-bench v1.80; LLMRouterBench v1.164; delegation on LLMRouterBench v1.200; LLM Routing Response Bank v1.296; delegation on the LLM Routing Response Bank v1.316; size budget v1.334; shrinks with each trim v1.344; ledger hand-off v1.396; room for one more v1.444; registry pair v1.452; room for a thirteenth v1.473)
Purpose: the README itself shows what the router did on public data, with links a reader can follow to the source, and no number that can drift from the committed results
- README.md has a section `## Evidence: held-out results on public data`, placed before the price and leaderboard section, with one `###` subsection per dataset that has committed results and no other `###` heading, the routing ones before the delegation ones, in this order, each with the version that added it and its results spec: `RouterBench` (v1.10, 12.7), `AutoBench` (v1.17, 12.10), `AutoBench judges` (v1.28, 12.12), `tau2-bench` (v1.55, 12.15), `LiveCodeBench` (v1.65, 12.17), `LLMRouterBench` (v1.164, 12.19), `LLM Routing Response Bank` (v1.296, 12.21), `Registry pair` (v1.452, 12.24), `Delegation on AutoBench` (v1.22, 13.10), `Delegation on tau2-bench` (v1.80, 13.12), `Delegation on LLMRouterBench` (v1.200, 13.13) and `Delegation on the LLM Routing Response Bank` (v1.316, 13.14). ### 12.9 Public evidence: the AutoBench 2026 converter (`evidence/autobench-2026/convert.py`, v1.14; tokens and registry v1.21; labels v1.518)
Purpose: a second public outcome matrix in the 12.1 format, with 2026 models and billed cost per call. Standard library only (argparse, csv, hashlib, json, math, re, sys, urllib, pathlib), so it needs no extra; the package never imports it
- Source, pinned: dataset `AutoBench/router-benchmark-2026-10` on Hugging Face at revision `43755180be7d8097068982d7a3f37fc04cd15379`, licence CC-BY-4.0 (the card asks users to cite its paper). `FILES` maps each file the converter reads or checks to its byte size and sha256: `matrix.csv` (1,899,644 bytes), `questions.csv` (298,329), `pool.json` (6,582), `frozen_params.json` (2,042) and `SHA256SUMS` (1,198). The pins in the script are the trust root; the dataset's own `SHA256SUMS` must agree with them for the four data files, as a second check that the pins came from this revision
- `default_cache_dir()` is `~/.cache/ai-model-routing-evidence/autobench-2026/` (from `Path.home()`), never inside the repo. `fetch(cache_dir=None) -> Path` returns that folder after, for each file in `FILES` order: a present file is verified and kept, and one that fails `verify` is a `ValueError` naming it and is left in place; a missing one is downloaded with `urllib.request.urlopen` from `https://huggingface.co/datasets/AutoBench/router-benchmark-2026-10/resolve/<revision>/<name>` into `<name>.part`, verified, then renamed, and the `.part` file is removed when that fails. Last, `check_sums` runs on the text of `SHA256SUMS`
- `verify(path, size, sha256)`: `ValueError` naming the expected and the actual value when the byte size or the sha256 differs, as in 12.6
- `check_sums(text)`: reads lines of the form `<64 lowercase hex>  <name>` (two spaces, as `sha256sum` writes them); blank lines are skipped and any other line is a `ValueError`. `ValueError` when one of the four data files has no entry, or an entry that differs from `FILES` (the message names the file)
- `model_id(openrouter_id) -> str`: a string with exactly one `/` and both sides non-empty, else `ValueError`. Hyphens are removed from the vendor part with `re.sub("-", "", vendor)`, so `x-ai/grok-4.6` becomes `xai/grok-4.6` (models.json writes `xai/grok-4.7`) and `z-ai/glm-5.3` becomes `zai/glm-5.3`; the model part is kept as is. A rule, not a list, so a new hyphenated vendor needs no code change
- `pool_models(pool) -> dict[str, str]`: display ID to `model_id(openrouter_id)` for each entry of `pool["members"]`, in pool order. `ValueError` when `pool` is not a dict, `members` is missing or not a non-empty list, an entry is not a dict, a `display_id` or `openrouter_id` is not a non-empty string, a display ID repeats, or two entries map to one ID
- `pool_registry(pool) -> dict` (v1.21): a registry in the models.json format that `Registry.load` (4.1) reads, built from the pool's list prices: `{"source": {"dataset": "AutoBench/router-benchmark-2026-10", "revision": <the pinned revision>, "file": "pool.json"}, "models": [...]}`, one model per `members` entry, sorted by ID ascending so the pool order does not matter, each with the keys `id` (`model_id(openrouter_id)`), `family` (as written), `price_in` and `price_out` (`input_cost_per_mtok` and `output_cost_per_mtok` as floats, USD per 1M tokens, the unit of 4.1) and `context_window`, in that order. `ValueError` for an invalid pool as in `pool_models` (checked first, with its messages), and for a member whose `family` is not a non-empty string, whose `input_cost_per_mtok` or `output_cost_per_mtok` is not a finite number `>= 0` (a bool is not a number), or whose `context_window` is not an int `>= 1` (a bool is not an int); these messages name the display ID and the key. The prices are the pool's recorded list prices, frozen with it, so a cost from this registry is a list-price estimate (13.9), never the billed `cost`
- `delta_hit(score, pool_scores, width, top_k) -> bool`: the reference is the `math.fsum` of the `top_k` highest values of `pool_scores` divided by `top_k`, and the result is `score >= reference - width`. This is the dataset's Delta-Hit: with `width = delta_signal` and `top_k` from `frozen_params.json`, it gives the `delta_hit_signal` value of the dataset's `decisions.csv` on all 6,291 router decisions that carry one (checked when this section was written, against every scored pool cell of the question; `>` instead of `>=` also gives 6,291, so the boundary is not tested by the data)
- `convert(matrix, questions, pool, width, top_k=3, task_by="domain", tokens=False, labels=False) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]`; `matrix` and `questions` are lists of dicts as `csv.DictReader` yields them (every value a string), `pool` is the parsed `pool.json`:
  - `ValueError`, checked before any output and the pool first, because `top_k` is bounded by its size: an invalid pool as in `pool_models`; a `width` that is a bool, not an int or float, not finite or `<= 0`; a `top_k` that is a bool, not an int, below 1 or above the number of pool models; a `task_by` other than `domain` and `all`; a `tokens` that is not a bool; a question whose `prompt_id` is not a non-empty string or repeats, or whose `ddc_domain` is not a non-empty string when `task_by` is `domain`; a matrix row whose `prompt_id` or `model` is not a non-empty string, whose `prompt_id` is not a question, or whose (`prompt_id`, `model`) pair repeats; for a pool model's row, a non-empty `score` that does not parse as a finite float, or a scored row whose `cost` does not parse as a finite float `>= 0` or, only when `tokens` is True, whose `input_tokens` or `output_tokens` is missing or does not parse as a finite float that is a whole number `>= 0` (these messages name the `prompt_id`, the model and, for a token count, the column)
  - repeated pairs: a (`prompt_id`, `model`) pair in two rows, for example once with `source` `original` and once with `fill_7_4`, is refused, never resolved by picking one. The pinned file has none: its 388 `fill_7_4` rows are all for 13 models outside the 20-model pool
  - out of pool: rows for a model that is not a pool display ID are dropped and counted (in the pinned file, exactly those 388 `fill_7_4` rows, which the dataset uses to grade router picks outside the pool)
  - unscored: an empty `score` is an unscored cell, and a pool model with no row for a question counts as one too. A question is kept only when every pool model has a score on it, so the output is the complete matrix 12.3 requires; a question with an unscored pool cell is dropped and counted, never scored as a miss
  - each kept question is one item: item = `prompt_id`; task = its `ddc_domain` as written (for example `9 History`), or `all` for every item when `task_by` is `all`; one row per pool model with model = its mapped ID, `correct` = `delta_hit(score, the scores of all pool models on that question, width, top_k)` and `cost_usd` = the billed `cost` as a float, with a negative zero written as `0.0`
  - output rows have the keys `task`, `item`, `model`, `correct`, `cost_usd` in that order, sorted by (task, item, model) as strings; the result does not depend on the row order of either file
  - tokens (v1.21): with `tokens` True each row also has `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`, in that order after `cost_usd`: that cell's `matrix.csv` columns written as ints (the pinned file writes them as, for example, `303.0`). `output_tokens` already counts the reasoning tokens (13.9), so `reasoning_tokens` is never read. With `tokens` False, the default, no token column is read, so the rows, the report and every error are those of v1.14. The report is the same in both
  - labels (v1.518, row STRAT3a): with `labels` True each row also has `difficulty`, `skill` and `domain`, in that order after `cost_usd` and any token counts, so `evaluate --slice-by` (12.1, 12.3 v1.514) can score a slice of each. `difficulty` is the question's `difficulty` mapped by `DIFFICULTY`: `a very simple` to `1-very-simple`, `a simple` to `2-simple`, `a` (the level the questions file writes with no adjective, between the simple and the difficult ones) to `3-unmarked`, `a difficult` to `4-difficult` and `a very difficult` to `5-very-difficult`, so the slices, which the evaluator lists ascending, read in difficulty order; `skill` is its `intended_skill` and `domain` its `ddc_domain`, both as written. Each question is checked in the questions loop, before any matrix row: `ValueError` naming the `prompt_id` and the column for a `difficulty` not in `DIFFICULTY`, or an `intended_skill` or `ddc_domain` that is not a non-empty string or holds `@` (12.1's slice name rule); a `labels` that is not a bool is a `ValueError`, checked after `tokens`. The report gains a last key `labels`, `{"difficulty": {...}, "skill": {...}, "domain": {...}}`, each `{value: number of kept questions}` with values ascending. With `labels` False, the default, no label column is read beyond v1.14's `ddc_domain`, so the rows, the report and every error are those of v1.21. On the pinned files at the default options the kept questions are 48, 50, 42, 33 and 30 for `1-very-simple` to `5-very-difficult`, and `coding` 15, `creative_synthesis` 23, `math_reasoning` 43, `planning_agentic` 31 and `world_knowledge` 91, so a slice's calibration half holds about 15 to 25 questions, under the default `min_samples = 30` (row STRAT3b reads it)
  - the report has keys `models` (IDs ascending), `width`, `top_k`, `task_by`, `kept` and `dropped_unscored` (each `{task: number of questions}` with tasks ascending), `unscored_cells` (pool cells with no score, missing rows included), `dropped_out_of_pool` (`{model as written: rows}`, ascending) and `rows` (the number of output rows)
- `read_csv(path) -> list[dict]` reads UTF-8 with `csv.DictReader`; `write_jsonl(rows, path)` as in 12.6
- CLI: `python evidence/autobench-2026/convert.py --out PATH [--cache DIR] [--width W] [--task-by {domain,all}] [--tokens] [--labels] [--registry PATH]`, entry point `main(argv=None) -> int`; `--labels` passes `labels=True` (v1.518). Options are checked first, so a bad one downloads nothing (`--out`, and `--registry` when it is given, must pass the 12.14 `--out` check, in that order and before the four-files check below, v1.174, row H4b; to v1.173 only the four-files check came before the fetch, so a bad `--out` or `--registry` failed at the write or the rename after the download); then it fetches and checks the files, takes `top_k`, and `delta_signal` as the width unless `--width` is given, from `frozen_params.json`, converts, writes `<out>.part` (and, with `--registry`, the registry's `.part` file), prints the report as `json.dumps(report, indent=2)`, flushing stdout, and only then renames them (v1.94, as 13.11), so a write to stdout that fails (a closed pipe) is an I/O error that leaves `--out` and `--registry` as they were. After a `BrokenPipeError` from the print, stdout is pointed at `os.devnull` as in 13.11 (v1.150), so the process exits 2 with that one `error:` line, not 120 with two more lines from the interpreter's flush at exit. `--width 0.3011090610836323` is the dataset's official width (`delta_official`). `--tokens` (v1.21) passes `tokens=True`. `--registry PATH` (v1.21) also writes `json.dumps(pool_registry(pool), indent=2)` plus a newline to PATH; a `--registry` for which `--out`, `--registry` and their two `.part` paths do not resolve to four different files (for example `--registry` equal to `--out`, or `--out x.part --registry x`) is a usage error whose message says they name the same file, and an invalid pool for the registry fails before any file is written. Both files are written in full to their `.part` paths before either is renamed, `--out` first. A `--width` that is not a finite number `> 0` is a usage error whose message names the value; a `frozen_params.json` that is not an object, has no `top_k`, or has no `delta_signal` when `--width` is not given is invalid data whose message names the file and the key. It returns 0 on success and 2 with exactly one `error: ...` line on stderr and nothing on stdout for a bad option, a size, hash or `SHA256SUMS` mismatch, invalid data or an I/O error, but for a rename that fails after the print (v1.94), the one failure with the report already on stdout; on any failure before the renames neither `--out` nor `--registry` is written, and each `.part` file is removed
- Default options on the pinned files (checked when this section was written): 20 models; 203 of 252 questions kept, 49 dropped for 107 unscored pool cells; 4,060 rows; 10 domain tasks of 12 to 33 questions. Mean hit rate over all cells 0.667 at the default width and 0.762 at the official width. With `--tokens` (v1.21) the rows are the same with the two counts added: `input_tokens` 66 to 2,341 and `output_tokens` 3 to 42,188; 2 rows are billed 0, and on the other 4,058 the `--registry` list prices times those counts give a median ratio of 1.000 to the billed `cost`
- Reading it: a Delta-Hit is relative, not an absolute acceptance check. It means "rated about as well as the best three answers in this pool on this question" by a committee of up to 10 judge models taken from the same pool, so a hit depends on which other models were asked, and the ratings are model judgments, not gold labels. The costs are the billed USD per call in the matrix frozen on 2026-08-29 (the card dates the `fill_7_4` rows 2026-09-05, and every one of them is dropped). A domain has 12 to 33 kept questions, so its calibration half holds fewer than 30 items and the default `min_samples = 30` (5.3) cannot be met per domain; `--task-by all` pools them into one task of 203 items, which is the matrix the results slice commits (the per-domain matrix only as a stated sensitivity at a lower `--min-samples`)
