### 12.18 Public evidence: the LLMRouterBench converter (`evidence/llmrouterbench/convert.py`, v1.154)
Purpose: a fifth public outcome matrix in the 12.1 format, with many routing tasks whose best model differs and a cost on every record, the dataset `research/datasets.md` `## Many-task routing data (2026-11-09)` recommends. Standard library only (argparse, hashlib, json, math, os, re, sys, tarfile, urllib, pathlib); the package never imports it
- Source, pinned: the Hugging Face dataset `NPULH/LLMRouterBench` at `REVISION = "b95870f9e60c589e82f7972c91ffa8de9ca89f85"`, `LICENCE = "MIT"` (its LICENSE file, whose scope paragraph keeps third-party material under its own licence), one file `FILE = "bench-release.tar.gz"`, `SIZE = 1283503080` bytes, `SHA256 = "b79f8cde1a6f029c2efa663a3a3b6f7748defb22341fe59f328cebef6648c8f1"`, `URL = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/NPULH/LLMRouterBench/resolve/<REVISION>/bench-release.tar.gz"`
- `POOL`: the 13 model folders of the GitHub README's performance-cost setting, ascending: `claude-sonnet-4`, `deepseek-r1-0528`, `deepseek-v3-0324`, `deepseek-v3.1-terminus`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-pro`, `glm-4.6`, `gpt-5`, `gpt-5-chat`, `intern-s1`, `kimi-k2-0905`, `qwen3-235b-a22b-2507`, `qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507`
- `model_id(folder) -> str`, a rule, not a list: a non-empty ASCII string without `/` that fully matches `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*`, prefixed with the vendor of the first `VENDORS` pattern that matches its start (`claude-` anthropic, `deepseek-` deepseek, `gemini-` google, `glm-` z-ai, `gpt-` openai, `intern-` internlm, `kimi-` moonshotai, `qwen` qwen); anything else is a `ValueError`, never a guess
- `member_path(name)`: `(benchmark, split, folder)` for a member named `bench-release/<benchmark>/<folder>/<file>.json` (split `""`, the layout of `arenahard` and its subset folders) or `bench-release/<benchmark>/<split>/<folder>/<file>.json`; `None` for any other name, a non-string, a part that is empty, `.` or `..`, or a file name that is only `.json`
- `query_digest(query) -> str`: the sha256 hex digest of `json.dumps(query, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)` in UTF-8, so a question can be compared across models without being kept
- `extract(doc, benchmark, split, folder) -> dict` reduces one parsed result file to the keys `benchmark`, `split`, `model` (`model_id(folder)`) and `cells`, in that order. `cells` maps each record `index`, ascending, to `{"score", "cost_usd", "input_tokens", "output_tokens", "query"}`: `score` a float or `None`, `cost_usd` the record `cost` as a float (a negative zero written as `0.0`), the token counts the record `prompt_tokens` and `completion_tokens`, a negative count as `None`, and `query` the `query_digest` of its `origin_query`. `ValueError`: a `benchmark` that is not a non-empty string or holds `|`, a `split` that is not a string or holds `|`, a folder `model_id` refuses; a `doc` that is not a dict with a non-empty `records` list; a record that is not a dict; an `index` that is not an int `>= 0` (a bool is not one) or repeats; a `score` other than 0, 0.5, 1 or null; a `cost` that is not a finite number `>= 0`; a token count that is not an int; no `origin_query`. Nothing else of a record is read
- `convert(extracts, pool=None) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]`, `pool` the model IDs (default: `model_id` of each `POOL` folder):
  - `ValueError`, before any output: a `pool` that is not a non-empty list or tuple of distinct non-empty strings; `extracts` that is not a non-empty list or tuple; two extracts for one (benchmark, split, model); no row kept. An extract whose model is not in the pool is ignored
  - subsets: a benchmark whose name is another benchmark's name plus `_` and more is dropped as `subset of <that benchmark>` (on the pinned file `arenahard_coding`, `arenahard_creative_writing` and `arenahard_math`, whose 253, 250 and 247 questions are the 750 of `arenahard`, so counting both would count each question twice)
  - splits: a benchmark's split is the one in which every pool model has an extract; with none it is dropped as `no split holds every pool model`, and `lacking` lists, per split it has, the pool models without one; with two or more it is a `ValueError`. A benchmark that lacks a pool model is never routed over fewer models, so every task routes over the same pool
  - items, checked in this order per index of the chosen split: an index some pool model lacks is dropped (`dropped_incomplete`); one where any pool model's score is null is dropped (`dropped_unscored`), never scored as a miss; one whose `query` differs across the pool is dropped (`dropped_question_differs`), since the join is on `index` and the same index must name the same question; the rest are kept
  - one row per kept item and pool model with the keys `task` (the benchmark), `item` (`<benchmark>|<index>`), `model`, `correct` (`score == 1`; a 0.5 is a miss), `cost_usd`, `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` (an int or null), in that order, sorted by (task, item, model) as strings; the rows do not depend on the order of the extracts or of the records in a file; the input is not modified
  - the report has the keys `models` (the pool, ascending), `tasks` (per kept benchmark, ascending: `split`, `items`, `dropped_incomplete`, `dropped_unscored`, `dropped_question_differs`, `half_scores`, the kept cells scored 0.5, and `null_tokens`, the kept cells with a null token count), `dropped_benchmarks` (benchmark to reason, ascending), `lacking` and `rows`
- `read_archive(path, folders=POOL) -> list` opens the tarball with `tarfile.open(path, mode="r|gz")` and reads it once as a stream: for each regular-file member whose `member_path` is not `None` and whose folder is in `folders` it parses the bytes as UTF-8 JSON and calls `extract`; every other member is skipped unread, and nothing is written to disk, so no member name can reach the file system. Invalid UTF-8 or JSON, or nesting past the recursion limit, is a `ValueError` naming the member; a file that is not a readable gzip tarball is a `ValueError` naming it. The extracts come in member order
- `default_cache_dir()` is `~/.cache/ai-model-routing-evidence/llmrouterbench/`; `verify(path, size, sha256)` as in 12.14; `fetch(cache_dir=None) -> Path` returns the path of the cached file after `verify`, a present file that fails it being a `ValueError` and left in place, and a missing one downloaded with `urllib.request.urlopen(URL, timeout=60)` into `<FILE>.part`, verified, then renamed, the `.part` file removed on any failure, a failed download an `OSError` naming the file after up to three attempts (12.13 v1.406)
- CLI: `python evidence/llmrouterbench/convert.py --out PATH [--cache DIR]`, entry point `main(argv=None) -> int`, as 12.16: options checked first, so a bad one downloads nothing (`--out` must pass the 12.14 `--out` check, v1.171); then fetch, read, convert, write the rows to `<out>.part` with `write_jsonl`, print the report as `json.dumps(report, indent=2)` with `print_report` (13.11 v1.150), and only then rename it onto `--out`; `<out>.part` is removed on any failure; 0 on success, 2 with one `error:` line (a newline or carriage return escaped) on a `ValueError` or `OSError`
- Choices (v1.154):
  - pool: the 13-model performance-cost pool, since every one of its records has a cost and token counts; 9 of the 20 models of the README's other pool record a cost of 0.0, so that pool could feed `cost_blind` only and is left to a later version
  - cost: `cost_usd` is each record's `cost`. Summed per model it is 0.853 to 1.502 times the README's price list applied to the same token counts (research/datasets.md), so the files do not say which price table produced it, and none of the 13 models is in `models.json`. The token counts are kept for a later cross-check; 12.1 uses `cost_usd` when it is present, so a null count never reaches a cost
  - negative token counts: 10 of `gpt-5`'s records (5 in `hle`, 5 in `simpleqa`) have a negative `completion_tokens` beside a valid cost; their score and cost are kept and the count is written as null, rather than dropping 10 items for a field routing does not read
  - success: `score == 1`. Among the pool's files only the four `arenahard` folders, scored by a model judge, hold a score other than 0 and 1, always 0.5 (2,149 records in `arenahard`, by a survey of the pool's records when this was written); a 0.5 is not a full success, so it counts as a miss and `half_scores` says how often, so a later version can state a sensitivity
  - one routing task per benchmark: a benchmark is one kind of job, as a tau2-bench domain is (12.15)
- Default output on the pinned file (a private prototype of this contract, run when this section was written; the cached-file test pins it): 13 models; 9 tasks, `aime` (split `hybrid`) 60 items, `arc-agi` (`v1`) 400, `arenahard` (`""`) 749, `gpqa` (`test`) 198, `hle` (`test`) 2,157, `livecodebench` (`test`) 1,055, `livemathbench` (`test`) 121, `mmlupro` (`test_3000`) 3,000 and `simpleqa` (`test`) 4,326, 12,066 in all, the item counts of research/datasets.md; `dropped_question_differs` 1 in `arenahard` and 1 in `hle`, every other dropped count 0; `half_scores` 2,144 in `arenahard`; `null_tokens` 5 in `hle` and 5 in `simpleqa`; dropped: the three `arenahard` subsets, `humaneval` (only `openai/gpt-5-chat` has a file), `swe-bench` (lacks `qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507`) and `tau2` (lacks `openai/gpt-5-chat`); 156,858 rows (12,066 times 13). The `hle`, `mmlupro` and `simpleqa` splits not chosen (`subset_500`, `test_1000`, `subset_500`) each lack one pool model. Verifying, reading and converting the cached file took about 13 seconds

### 12.20 Public evidence: the response-bank converter (`evidence/response-bank/convert.py`, v1.288)
Purpose: a seventh public outcome matrix in the 12.1 format, five 2026 models on four task families with an exact-answer or test label and a billed cost on every response, the dataset `research/datasets.md` `### Recommendation (2026-11-12)` recommends (row E20). Standard library only (argparse, hashlib, json, math, os, re, sys, urllib, pathlib); the package never imports it
- Source, pinned: the Hugging Face dataset `DATASET = "Lurume/llm-routing-response-bank"` at `REVISION = "547beb31ecd8f12b116b87eb4f56feee73edda6c"` (2026-09-17), `LICENCE = "ODC-BY-4.0"`: its LICENSE file names ODC-BY-4.0 as the planned licence and, until a formal publication, grants its terms with attribution to the dataset repository, so a later revision may word the terms otherwise and the pin keeps the ones read here. `FILES` maps the four files read, ascending, to `(size, sha256)`: `responses_cal.jsonl` 62,806,440 bytes with sha256 `31262ff3c39cf66c17332bdc3f104bdf25c4abedd8dc75767297fa67c2a08de5`, `responses_eval.jsonl` 942,083,749 bytes with sha256 `c0b9df2c194730cd24757001878a1e24648b4990747d60157261b60818e42305`, `scores_cal.jsonl` 349,266 bytes with sha256 `58826526608edd7ffaa16540fb0393ef631ee428cb708da92dae32d690a995cd`, `scores_eval.jsonl` 12,952,125 bytes with sha256 `09b7376e7964a85aee77644af64188b8b14156fab6201e6f3e80852ea6e42b4b`; three are the tree API's large-file sha256, and `scores_cal.jsonl`, stored without one, is the sha256 of a copy whose git blob hash is the tree API's `3c6fdeceef3466bb0a0cd017c98ef3dfcbdc7852`. `url(name)` is `https://huggingface.co/datasets/<DATASET>/resolve/<REVISION>/<name>` for a name in `FILES` and a `ValueError` for any other; `TIMEOUT = 60`. The two `tasks` files (prompts and reference answers, 4,550,282,953 bytes) are never read
- `MODELS`: the five raw IDs, ascending: `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`, `glm-5-3-flash`, `glm-5.3`, `kimi-k2.7-code`
- `model_id(raw) -> str`, a rule, not a list: an ASCII string that fully matches `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*`, prefixed with the vendor of the first `VENDORS` pattern its start matches (`deepseek-` deepseek, `glm-` z-ai, `kimi-` moonshotai); in a `glm-` ID a version written `<digits>-<digits>` right after the prefix and followed by `-` or the end is read as `<digits>.<digits>` (regex `^glm-(\d+)-(\d+)(?=-|$)`), so `glm-5-3-flash` is `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, in the dotted form of the release's own `glm-5.3` and of 12.18's `glm-4.6`; anything else is a `ValueError`, never a guess
- `score_record(obj) -> dict`, one parsed line of a scores file, to the keys `task_id`, `family` (the record's `dataset`), `model` (`model_id` of its `model_id`), `correct` (`quality == 1`) and `missing` (the `evaluator`'s `missing` reason, or `None`), in that order. `ValueError`: not a dict; a `dataset` that is not a non-empty string or holds `:` or `|`; a `task_id` that is not a string starting `<dataset>:` with more after it; a `quality` other than 0 or 1 (an int or float; a bool is not one); an `evaluator` that is not a dict; a `missing` that is present and not a non-empty string (a null one included, v1.289), or a `missing` cell scored 1. Nothing else of a record is read
- `response_record(obj) -> dict`, one parsed line of a responses file, to the keys `task_id`, `family`, `model` (checked as above), `sample_index` (an int `>= 0`, not a bool), `prompt_sha256` (64 lowercase hex digits), `finish_reason` (a string or `None`), `cost_usd` (`official_usd` as a float, finite and `>= 0`, not a bool and not an int too large for a float (v1.289), a negative zero written `0.0`), `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` (`usage.input` and `usage.output`, ints `>= 0`, not bools), in that order, each failed check a `ValueError`. `text`, `reasoning_content`, `response_sha256` and every other field are never kept
- `read_jsonl(path, parse) -> list` reads a file in binary mode one line at a time (the evaluation responses file is 942,083,749 bytes and is never loaded whole), decodes each line as UTF-8, skips blank lines and returns `parse` of each parsed line in file order; invalid UTF-8 or JSON, nesting past the recursion limit, or a `ValueError` from `parse` is a `ValueError` naming `<file name>:<line>` (1-based)
- `convert(scores, responses) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]`, over `score_record` and `response_record` outputs:
  - `ValueError`, before any output: `scores` or `responses` that is not a non-empty list or tuple; a repeated (task_id, model) among the scores or (task_id, model, sample_index) among the responses; a response whose (task_id, model) has no score; no row kept. From v1.289 each message opens with the words that name its case, so a test can tell one refusal from another: `scores must be a non-empty list or tuple` (or `responses ...`), `repeated score`, `repeated response`, `response without a score` and `no row kept`
  - the models are every model the scores name, ascending; a response whose `sample_index` is not 0 is ignored and counted (`ignored_samples`), so each (item, model) is one call
  - items, one per `task_id`, checked in this order: one that some model has no score for is dropped (`dropped_incomplete`); one where a model's cell has neither a `missing` reason nor a sample-0 response is dropped (`dropped_unbilled`), since its cost is unknown; one whose sample-0 responses do not all share one `prompt_sha256` is dropped (`dropped_prompt_differs`), since the join is on `task_id` and one ID must name one prompt; the rest are kept
  - one row per kept item and model with the keys `task` (the family), `item` (the `task_id`), `model`, `correct`, `cost_usd`, `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`, in that order, sorted by (task, item, model); a `missing` cell with no response is a miss with `cost_usd` 0.0 and null token counts, and one with a response keeps its bill; the rows do not depend on the order of the input, and the input is not modified
  - the report has the keys `models`, `tasks` (per family the scores name, ascending, a family whose every item is dropped included: `items`, `dropped_incomplete`, `dropped_unbilled`, `dropped_prompt_differs`, `missing_cells`, the kept cells with a `missing` reason, `length_finishes`, the kept cells whose response stopped at its length limit (`finish_reason` `length`), `length_successes`, those of them scored 1, and `other_finishes`, the kept cells whose `finish_reason` is neither `stop` nor `length`, a null one included), `ignored_samples` and `rows`
- `default_cache_dir()` is `~/.cache/ai-model-routing-evidence/response-bank/`; `verify(path, size, sha256)` as in 12.14; `fetch(cache_dir=None) -> dict` maps each name of `FILES`, in that order, to the path of the cached file after `verify`, each file handled as 12.18 `fetch` handles its one (a present file that fails `verify` is a `ValueError` and left in place; a missing one is downloaded with `urllib.request.urlopen(url(name), timeout=TIMEOUT)` into `<name>.part`, verified, then renamed, the `.part` file removed on any failure, a failed download an `OSError` naming the file after up to three attempts, 12.13 v1.406)
- CLI: `python evidence/response-bank/convert.py --out PATH [--cache DIR]`, entry point `main(argv=None) -> int`, as 12.18: options are checked first (`--out` must pass the 12.14 `--out` check), so a bad one downloads nothing; then it fetches, reads the two scores files and the two responses files with `read_jsonl` (calibration before evaluation), converts, writes the rows to `<out>.part` with `write_jsonl`, prints the report as `json.dumps(report, indent=2)` with `print_report`, and only then renames it onto `--out`; `<out>.part` is removed on any failure; 0 on success, 2 with one `error:` line (a newline or carriage return escaped) on a `ValueError` or `OSError`
- Choices (v1.288):
  - both splits: the 256 calibration tasks share no `task_id` with the 13,059 evaluation tasks, and together they give each family its whole benchmark slice (`aime` 30, the AIME 2025 I and II problems; `gpqa_diamond` 198; `livecodebench` 1,055; `mmlu_pro` 12,032), so the converter joins them and 12.2 draws its own halves by seed, as on every other dataset; the release's split served its own study and is not reused. A `task_id` in both files would be a repeated score, a `ValueError`
  - one routing task per family, as 12.18 takes one per benchmark: the files read hold no finer label (an `mmlu_pro` ID is `mmlu_pro:<number>`, with no MMLU-Pro category; only the 4,135,614,754-byte `tasks_eval.jsonl` might hold one), so `mmlu_pro` is one task of 12,032 items, 90% of the matrix, and `aime` has a calibration half of at most 30 items, under the default `min_samples` 30 on any seed that holds an item out (12.3 then falls back; 12.21 measures 10 to 21 items over its 50 seeds, so it falls back on every one)
  - success: `quality == 1`, the label of the helm exact-answer parser or of LiveCodeBench's tests (`codegen_metrics` at commit 28fef95ea8c9f7a547c8329f2cd3d32b92c1fa24), so no model judges. A response that stopped at its length limit keeps that label: of the 450 such responses on the pinned files 433 score 0 and 17 score 1 (16 of `deepseek-v4-flash` on `livecodebench`, whose code passed the tests, and 1 of `glm-5.3` on `mmlu_pro`). The label is what an acceptance check reads from the returned text, which is what a caller of a cut-off call gets, so the converter neither fails nor drops these cells, and the report counts them
  - missing cells: the six cells with a `missing` reason (all `mmlu_pro`, three of `glm-5.3` and three of `glm-5-3-flash` on 4 items: five provider content filters and one refusal) score 0 and have no response row, so they are misses at a cost of 0.0 with null token counts: `official_usd` is response charges only by the card, and none is recorded for them. Dropping their 4 items instead would hide a failure that a router choosing either model meets
  - cost: `cost_usd` is the response's `official_usd`, "provider billing in USD including cache discounts" by the card, a recorded bill and never tokens times a list price; the files give no price pair, and none of the five models is in `models.json`. The token counts are kept as recorded and are not read by 12.1 when `cost_usd` is present: on 25,471 of the 66,569 responses `usage.cache_read` is above `usage.input`, so `input` does not always include the cache reads the card says it does, and `total_tokens`, never read, is not `input + output` on 25,479
- Default output on the pinned files (a private prototype of this contract, run when this section was written; the cached-file test pins it): 5 models, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code`, `z-ai/glm-5.3` and `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`; 4 tasks, `aime` 30 items, `gpqa_diamond` 198, `livecodebench` 1,055 and `mmlu_pro` 12,032, 13,315 in all; every dropped count 0 and `ignored_samples` 0 (every response is at `sample_index` 0); `missing_cells` 6 in `mmlu_pro`; `length_finishes` 5, 71, 246 and 128, `length_successes` 0, 0, 16 and 1, and `other_finishes` 0, 6, 3 and 12 (15 null, 5 `content_filter` and 1 `engine_overloaded`, each scored 0); 66,575 rows (13,315 times 5), 11,054,218 bytes of JSONL (not committed), the 6 missing cells the only rows with a `cost_usd` of 0.0. Reading and converting the four cached files took about 4 seconds

### 12.23 Public evidence: the registry-pair converter (`evidence/registry-pair/convert.py`, v1.431)
Purpose: a public outcome matrix in the 12.1 format whose two models and their prices are the registry's own, the dataset `research/registry-pair.md` (12.22 v1.430) recommends (row E24). Standard library only (argparse, hashlib, json, math, os, sys, urllib, pathlib); it reads `model_routing/data/models.json` as JSON and never imports the package, and the package never imports it
- Source, pinned: the Hugging Face dataset `DATASET = "superlinked/train-a-router-reasoning"` at `REVISION = "63336f25fc54597a8e161a7245613f91bd60177e"` (last modified 2026-10-21), `LICENCE = "mixed-mit-and-apache-2.0"`, its card's `license_name` (its `license` is `other`): MIT for the MMLU-Pro and BIG-Bench Hard questions, Apache-2.0 for the KOR-Bench questions and the study's code and metadata. `FILES` maps the three files read, ascending, to `(size, sha256)`, the values of `research/registry_pair.py` `FILES`: `pair.json`, `recordings/grades-calibration.json` and `recordings/grades-final.json`. `url(name)` is `https://huggingface.co/datasets/<DATASET>/resolve/<REVISION>/<name>`, a `ValueError` for a name not in `FILES`. No question or answer text is in the files read
- `check_pair(pair, registry) -> dict`, over parsed `pair.json` and parsed `models.json`: `{"cheap": id, "strong": id}`, each `openai/<model>` of that arm's `arms.<arm>.model`, after its `prices_usd_per_million.<model>` `input` and `output` (decimal strings in the release, a number also taken, never a bool) are checked equal, as floats, to that registry row's `price_in` and `price_out`. Each refusal a `ValueError` whose message opens with its case: `pair format` (a `format` other than `routerbench-openai-pair-v1`), `registry:` (no `models` list of objects), `pair:` (an arm or its model absent, a model that is not a non-empty string, or a price absent), `model not in the registry`, `pair price` (not a finite number `>= 0`), `price differs` and `same model in both arms`
- `grade_rows(grades, split, ids) -> list`, over one parsed grades file: one record per row and arm, in file order, cheap before strong, with the keys `task` (`<dataset>/<task>`, each space of the task an underscore), `item` (the row's `id`), `family`, `split`, `model` (`ids[arm]`), `correct` (`<arm>_correct == 1`), `cost_usd` (`<arm>_cost_usd` as a float) and `valid` (`<arm>_valid`), in that order. Refused, each a `ValueError`: `grades format` (a `format` other than `routerbench-paired-grades-v1`, or a `split` other than `split`) and `no rows`, each opening its message; then, per row in this order, a row that is not an object (`<split> row <n>: not an object`, n the 0-based position), an `id` that is not a non-empty string (`<split> row <n> id must be a non-empty string`), a `role` other than `split` (`row role: <split> row '<id>'`), a `dataset`, `task` or `family` that is not a non-empty string (`<split> row '<id>' <key> must be a non-empty string`, the `dataset` checked first and refused next if it holds `/`, `... holds '/'`), and per arm, cheap first, a `<arm>_correct` that is not the int 0 or 1, a bool or float included (`<split> row '<id>': <arm>_correct ... is not 0 or 1`), a `<arm>_cost_usd` that is a bool, not an int or float, not finite or below 0 (`... is not a finite number >= 0`), a `<arm>_valid` that is not a bool (`... is not a bool`) and `invalid cell scored 1`, which opens its message. Nothing else of a row is read
- `convert(calibration, final) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]`, over the two splits' `grade_rows` records:
  - `ValueError`, before any output, opening with its case: `calibration must be a non-empty list or tuple` (or `final ...`), `item in both splits`, `repeated cell` (an (item, model) twice in one split), `item task differs` (records of one item with two tasks or families) and `incomplete item` (an item some model has no record for, the message naming the item and one such model)
  - the models are every model the records name, ascending; the rows, one per item and model, have the keys `task`, `item`, `model`, `correct` and `cost_usd`, in that order, sorted by (task, item, model); they do not depend on the order of the input, and the input is not modified
  - the report has the keys `models`, `tasks` (per task ascending: `items`, `calibration` and `final`, its items in each release split, and `invalid_cells`, its cells with `valid` false), `families` (`families`, the distinct values; `shared_families`, those of two or more items; `shared_items`, the items in them; `in_both_splits`, the families with items in both splits; `across_tasks`, those with items in two or more tasks) and `rows`
- `default_cache_dir()` is `~/.cache/ai-model-routing-evidence/registry-pair/`, the folder `research/registry_pair.py` uses, so one download serves both; `verify(path, size, sha256)` as in 12.14; `fetch(cache_dir=None) -> dict` as 12.20 `fetch` (a missing file in a subfolder gets its folder first); `read_json(path, name=None)` parses one file, invalid UTF-8 or JSON or nesting past the recursion limit a `ValueError` naming the file
- CLI: `python evidence/registry-pair/convert.py --out PATH [--cache DIR]`, entry point `main(argv=None) -> int`, as 12.20: options are checked first (`--out` passes the 12.14 `--out` check, the same `_check_out` source as `evidence/llmrouterbench/convert.py`), so a bad one downloads nothing; then it fetches, checks the pair against this checkout's `model_routing/data/models.json`, reads both splits with `grade_rows` (calibration first), converts, writes the rows to `<out>.part`, prints the report as `json.dumps(report, indent=2)` with `print_report`, and only then renames it onto `--out`; `<out>.part` is removed on any failure; 0 on success, 2 with one `error:` line (a newline or carriage return escaped) on a `ValueError` or `OSError`
- Choices (v1.431):
  - split, the choice row E24 asks for: the two release splits are joined and 12.2 draws its halves by seed, as on every other committed file (12.20 joins its release's splits the same way). Kept: one `evaluate` call with no package change, a spread over seeds that one fixed split cannot give, and rows comparable with the other datasets'. Given up: the release keeps each family of related questions in one split (0 in both on the pinned files), and seeded halves of items do not, so 808 of the 6,099 items, the 276 families of two or more (each inside one task), can sit on both sides of a seed's split. `research/registry-pair.md` is the run on the release's own split, so the results file (12.24) puts its rows beside that note's as the family-held check. A fixed-split option for 12.3 would be a package change and a minor bump for one dataset, so none is made
  - one routing task per (dataset, task) pair, the note's 31: 14 `bbh` of 92 or 93 items, 3 `korbench` (`cipher` and `counterfactual` 80 each, `logic` 20, whose calibration half is under `min_samples` 30 on every seed, so 12.3 falls back there) and 14 `mmlupro` of 141 to 526
  - success: the release's strict declared-label equality, so no model judges; an answer it marks invalid stays a miss and keeps its charge, its own rule, and is counted (1 cell on the pinned files)
  - cost: `<arm>_cost_usd`, the release's estimate from each call's token counts at the list prices `pair.json` names, which `check_pair` requires to be the registry's; the files hold hashes of the usage, not its counts, so a row has no token counts. `recordings/grades-train.json` is not read, as in 12.22 v1.430
- Default output on the pinned files (the cached-file test pins it): the models `openai/gpt-6-luna` and `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`; 31 tasks, 6,099 items, 3,056 in the calibration split and 3,043 in the final; `invalid_cells` 1 (`korbench/cipher`); families 5,567, `shared_families` 276, `shared_items` 808, `in_both_splits` 0, `across_tasks` 0; 12,198 rows, 1,630,121 bytes of JSONL (not committed), none with a `cost_usd` of 0.0. It runs in under a second
- Not in this version: the results file, its RESULTS.md with the card's licence lines quoted and the evidence README (12.24, rows E24b and E24d), and the 12.13 workflow lines (v1.443, row E24e); still not in any version: the README subsection (row E24c, after row DOC28); the converter itself is added in v1.432 (row E24a)
- Test status: `tests/test_evidence_registry_pair.py` was committed before the script, under a module-level `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, raises=ModuleNotFoundError)`, which the implementing commit (v1.432) removes. Every test uses small synthetic records or files in a temporary folder, except one on a CLI run on the three pinned files, a module fixture that runs only when all three are in the default cache and skips otherwise (CI never downloads them)

### 12.24 Registry-pair results (`evidence/registry-pair/results.json`, v1.433)
Purpose: the evaluator's numbers on the 12.23 matrix in the shape of 12.7, 12.10, 12.15, 12.17, 12.19 and 12.21, in both flavors since every row has a `cost_usd` above 0 (12.23), regenerated byte for byte from stated commands and checked against the pinned files when they are cached (row E24b)
- Script: `evidence/routerbench/results.py` (12.7) is reused unchanged, as in 12.10, 12.15, 12.17, 12.19 and 12.21
- Matrix: the converter's default (12.23: the 2 models, 31 tasks, 6,099 items, 12,198 rows), its two release splits joined, so 12.2 draws each seed's halves (12.23 Choices, split)
- Config: the one of `evidence/routerbench/results.json` (12.7), bars `0.6 0.7 0.8 0.9`, 50 seeds, `calibration_fraction` 0.5, `min_samples` 30 and confidence 0.95, both flavors. `research/registry-pair.md` runs the same bars, `min_samples` and confidence on the release's own split, so each committed row has a family-held counterpart at its bar, which row E24d sets beside it
- Bars, not the 12.17 rule: on this matrix the per-task, per-model success rates run from 0.710 (`openai/gpt-6-luna` on `mmlupro/law`, 304 of 428) to 1.000 (18 (task, model) pairs on 12 `bbh` tasks), so every tenth strictly inside the span, the rule of 12.17, 12.19 and 12.21, would give only `0.8 0.9`. ### 12.25 Public evidence: the Longtail-SWE converter (`evidence/longtail-swe/convert.py`, v1.478)
Purpose: a public outcome matrix in the 12.1 format on agentic coding, each item an issue of a source repository that a model's agent run resolves or not by the task's own tests, the dataset `research/datasets.md` (12.22) recommends in its 2026-11-18 section (row E26), whose four registry models are priced from each run's tokens at the registry's list prices. Standard library only (argparse, hashlib, json, math, os, re, sys, urllib, pathlib, imported at the top of the script) but for the parquet reader `pyarrow`, in the `evidence` extra, which only `read_rows` imports, when called, so the rest of the script and its tests run without it; it reads `model_routing/data/models.json` as JSON and never imports the package, and the package never imports it
- Source, pinned: the Hugging Face dataset `DATASET = "nebius/Longtail-SWE-trajectories"` at `REVISION = "dfd6075c56b7841b9c254cc70a57e39c1df0076c"` (last modified 2026-11-16), `LICENCE = "cc-by-4.0"`, its card's field, beside the CC BY 4.0 `LICENSE` text and a `LEGAL.md` that applies it to the compilation and the publisher's own material. `FILES` maps the four files read, ascending, to `(size, sha256)`, the sizes and sha256s the tree API gave on 2026-11-18: `data/swelike__claude-opus-5.5-high.parquet` (36,213,846 bytes), `data/swelike__gpt-5.6-luna-xhigh.parquet` (94,695,456), `data/swelike__gpt-5.6-sol-high.parquet` (56,147,793) and `data/swelike__gpt-6.1-sol-high.parquet` (49,548,306), 236,605,401 bytes in all; the release's other seven parquet files are not read. `url(name)` is `https://huggingface.co/datasets/<DATASET>/resolve/<REVISION>/<name>`, a `ValueError` for a name not in `FILES`
- `COLUMNS`, the only columns read, in this order: `instance_id`, `programming_language`, `canonical_model`, `run_index`, `resolved`, `initial_statement_matches_release` and `trajectory`; of `trajectory`, a JSON string, only its `usage.tokens` record is kept, never a prompt, message, tool call or patch, and `model_patch` is not read
- `model_id(canonical) -> str`: `anthropic/<canonical>` for a name that `re.fullmatch` takes by `claude-[a-z0-9.-]+` and `openai/<canonical>` for one it takes by `gpt-[a-z0-9.-]+` (so a trailing newline is refused), a regex over the canonical name instead of a vendor list; anything else, a non-string included, a `ValueError` opening `model name`
- `tokens(trajectory) -> tuple`, over one row's `trajectory`: `(input, output)` of its `usage.tokens`. Refused, each a `ValueError` opening with its case: `trajectory` (not a string, not JSON, or not an object), `no tokens` (no `usage` object, or no `tokens` object in it), `token count` (an `input`, `output` or `total` that is not an int `>= 0`, a bool included), `token total` (a `total` other than `input + output`) and `cached tokens` (a `cached_input` or `cache_creation` that is neither null nor an int `>= 0`, a bool included, or the two, null as 0, above `input`). On the four pinned files `total` is `input + output` on every run; `reasoning` is above 0 and at most `output` on every run of the three `gpt-` models, so it is inside `output`, and 0 on every `claude-` run; `cache_creation` is null on every `gpt-` run; and the record's `source` and `note` are `harness_reported` and `Token counter semantics are provider- and harness-specific.` on every run
- `run_records(rows, registry) -> list`, over one file's rows, each a dict of `COLUMNS`, and parsed `models.json`: one record per row, in row order, with the keys `task` (`issue_resolution`), `item` (`instance_id`), `language`, `run`, `model` (`model_id`), `correct` (`resolved == 1`), `scored` (`resolved` not null), `statement_matches` and `cost_usd` (`(input * price_in + output * price_out) / 1_000_000` at that model's registry row), in that order. Refused, each a `ValueError` whose message opens `row <n>` (0-based, within its file) and then its case, in this order: `not an object`, `instance_id` or `programming_language` not a non-empty string, `run_index` not an int `>= 0` (a bool included), `resolved` not 0, 1 or null (a bool or float included), `initial_statement_matches_release` not a bool, `model name` and `model not in the registry`, `price tiers` (a registry row with `price_tiers`: a run's usage sums many calls, so no per-call threshold can be applied), `registry price` (a `price_in` or `price_out` that is not a finite number `>= 0`, a bool included), then the `tokens` refusals
- `convert(records, run=0) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]`, over the records of all files:
  - `ValueError`, before any output, opening with its case: `records must be a non-empty list or tuple`, `run must be an int >= 0` (a bool included), `repeated run` (an (item, model, run) twice), `item language differs` (records of one item with two languages) and `incomplete item` (an item, of every item any record names at any run, that some model has no record for at `run`, the message naming the item and one such model, so a `run` no record has is refused this way); then, after the drop below, `no items` (every item dropped)
  - only records at `run` are used; an item that any model's record marks `statement_matches` false is dropped for every model; a record not `scored` is a miss that keeps its charge
  - the models are every model the records name, ascending; the rows, one per kept item and model, have the keys `task`, `item`, `model`, `correct` and `cost_usd`, in that order, sorted by (task, item, model); they do not depend on the order of the input, and the input is not modified
  - the report has the keys `models`, `run`, `tasks` (per task: `items`), `languages` (per language ascending, its kept items), `dropped_statement` (the dropped items, ascending), `resolved` (per model, its kept items with `correct`), `unscored` (per model, its kept items not `scored`, ascending, an empty list for none) and `rows` (their number)
- `default_cache_dir()` is `~/.cache/ai-model-routing-evidence/longtail-swe/`; `verify(path, size, sha256)` as in 12.14; `fetch(cache_dir=None) -> dict` as 12.20 `fetch` (a missing file in a subfolder gets its folder first); `read_rows(path) -> list` reads `COLUMNS` with `pyarrow.parquet.ParquetFile(path).iter_batches(columns=list(COLUMNS))`, a `ValueError` naming the file for one it cannot read or that lacks a column, and, with no `pyarrow`, a `ValueError` saying to install the `evidence` extra
- CLI: `python evidence/longtail-swe/convert.py --out PATH [--cache DIR] [--run N]`, entry point `main(argv=None) -> int`, as 12.23: options are checked first (`--out` passes the 12.14 `--out` check, the same `_check_out` source as `evidence/llmrouterbench/convert.py`; `--run` decimal digits only, so `-1`, `+1`, ` 1` and a non-ASCII digit are bad, one `error: --run must be decimal digits only, got ...` line (v1.486 and v1.488, review iter-343 nit 1 and iter-346 should-fix 1 and 2), default 0), so a bad one downloads nothing, and a missing `--out` or a bad option is, as in 12.23, one `error:` line and 2, not argparse's usage text and exit; then it fetches, reads `REGISTRY`, this checkout's `model_routing/data/models.json`, builds each file's `run_records` in `FILES` order, a refusal's message prefixed by that file's `FILES` name and `: ` so that the `error:` line names the file as well as the row within it (v1.479, review iter-342 nit 2), converts, writes the rows to `<out>.part`, prints the report as `json.dumps(report, indent=2)` with `print_report`, and only then renames it onto `--out`; `<out>.part` is removed on any failure; 0 on success, 2 with one `error:` line (a newline or carriage return escaped) on a `ValueError` or `OSError`
- Choices (v1.478), the rules row E26 asks for:
  - pool: the four registry models alone, priced by the registry; the other seven configs' models have no registry row, and vendor-page prices for them, as `research/llmrouterbench_prices.py` gave LLMRouterBench's, are a later row's, so their 601,005,089 bytes are not downloaded (the 49 runs with no token counts, all `deepseek-v4-flash`, are among them)
  - item: an `instance_id` at one `run_index`, run 0 by default, so 12.2's seeded halves split by `instance_id`; pooled as items, the three runs of one task could sit on both sides of a seed's split, which 12.2 cannot prevent without a package change. `--run 1` and `--run 2` give the same matrix on each re-run, which the results file may set beside run 0
  - statement: the 8 tasks whose `initial_statement_matches_release` is false, on all three runs of `claude-opus-5.5`, `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-5.6-luna` and on no run of `gpt-6.1-sol`, are dropped, so all four models are scored on one statement per task
  - the 4 null `resolved` runs, all `gpt-6.1-sol` (`babashka__cli-162` at run 0, one at run 1, two at run 2): misses that keep their charge, as 12.23 keeps an invalid answer's, and listed in `unscored`; dropping their items would drop them for the other three models too
  - cost: every `input` token, the cached part (`cached_input`, and `cache_creation` on `claude-` runs) included, at `price_in`, and every `output` token, reasoning included, at `price_out`. The registry holds one input price per model, so a row's cost is its tokens at the list input and output prices with no cache discount, an estimate and not a bill (the vendors' cache rates, which the registry does not hold, would lower it wherever cache reads outweigh a cache-write premium), by one rule for all four; the release's `usage.cost_usd` is null on every run of the four
  - one routing task, `issue_resolution`, over the 13 languages: one task per language would leave 6 to 13 items in each calibration half, under `min_samples` 30 on every seed, so 12.3 would fall back everywhere
- Default output on the four pinned files at run 0 (the cached-file test pins it): the models `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`, `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` and `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`; 1 task of 194 items (Clojure 12, Dart 13, Elixir 22, Erlang 12, F# 16, Haskell 13, Julia 26, Kotlin 11, Lua 13, OCaml 12, R 14, Scala 17 and Swift 13); 8 in `dropped_statement`; `resolved` 162, 140, 152 and 155 in that model order; `unscored` `babashka__cli-162` for `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` alone; 776 rows
- Not in this version: the README subsection (row E26e, after a room row); the converter itself is added in v1.480 (row E26b), its results file is 12.26 (v1.481, row E26c), with its RESULTS.md from v1.484 (row E26g), and its 12.13 workflow lines are added in v1.489 (row E26d)
- Test status: `tests/test_evidence_longtail_swe.py` is committed before the script, under a module-level `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, raises=ModuleNotFoundError)`, which the implementing commit (v1.480) removes. Every test uses small synthetic rows or committed files, except one on a CLI run on the four pinned files, a module fixture that runs only when `pyarrow` is installed and all four are in the default cache, and skips otherwise (CI never downloads them). From v1.479 `tests/test_evidence_closed_stdout.py` (13.11 v1.150) runs the script's `main` with a closed stdout and with an open one, its `fetch`, `read_rows` and `convert` stubbed, so the print-then-rename order holds here too (row E26b)

### 12.26 Longtail-SWE results (`evidence/longtail-swe/results.json`, v1.481)
Purpose: the evaluator's numbers on the 12.25 matrix in the shape of 12.7, 12.10, 12.15, 12.17, 12.19, 12.21 and 12.24, in both flavors since every row has a `cost_usd` above 0 (12.25), regenerated byte for byte from stated commands and checked against the pinned files when `pyarrow` is installed and the four files are cached (row E26c)
- Script: `evidence/routerbench/results.py` (12.7) is reused unchanged, as in 12.10, 12.15, 12.17, 12.19, 12.21 and 12.24
- Matrix: the converter's default (12.25: run 0, the 4 models, 1 task, `issue_resolution`, of 194 items, 776 rows), so one agent run per (item, model); runs 1 and 2 (`--run`, 12.25) are not in this file
- Config: the one of `evidence/routerbench/results.json` (12.7) and of 12.24, bars `0.6 0.7 0.8 0.9`, 50 seeds, `calibration_fraction` 0.5, `min_samples` 30 and confidence 0.95, both flavors. Over the 50 seeds the one task's 12.2 calibration half holds 79 to 111 of the 194 items, so `min_samples` 30 is met on every seed
- Bars, not the 12.17 rule: on this matrix the four models' success rates run from 0.722 (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, 140 of 194) to 0.835 (`anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`, 162 of 194), so every tenth strictly inside the span, the rule of 12.17, 12.19 and 12.21, would give only `0.8`, one bar, which shows no trade of success for cost as the bar moves. The 12.7 bars are kept: 0.6 and 0.7 sit under every model's rate, 0.8 inside the span and 0.9 above it, and because a model clears on its calibration bound, not its rate, they separate: the routed `cost_effective` cleared rate is 1.000 at 0.6, 0.940 at 0.7, 0.080 at 0.8 and 0.000 at 0.9. The file of the four bars is 21,500 bytes, under the 300,000 a committed results file may take
- Complementary halves: a seed's two halves split one pool of 194 items, so a model's held-out count is its count on the pool less its calibration count. At 0.8 the calibration bound of `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` clears on 4 of the 50 seeds, 9, 13, 26 and 27, with 87 of 97, 79 of 88, 92 of 102 and 78 of 87 resolved, which leave it 75 of 97, 83 of 106, 70 of 92 and 84 of 107 held out (0.773, 0.783, 0.761 and 0.785), so in both flavors each of the 4 cleared cells is under the bar, a bar-violation rate of 1.000 against the nominal one-sided 0.025, though the model's rate on the pool is 0.835: on one pool a lucky calibration half leaves an unlucky held-out one, a strong case of the re-split correlation that 12.3 (Reading the numbers) names. At 0.7 `cost_effective` clears 47 cells and 1 is under the bar (0.021); `cost_blind` clears 47 with none under
