## 13. Delegation: inline or sub-agent (`delegation.py`, v1.4; cost accounting v1.8)
Purpose: an agent (the **parent**: a model already running with its own context) reaches a piece of work that is one call of a task, or from v1.38 K successive calls of it (13.1). It can do the work itself (**inline**) or hand it to a fresh sub-agent running the model the router picks (**delegate**). The decision weighs what routing weighs, the measured success rate against the task's bar and list-price cost, plus what each path does to the parent's context. The delegate is chosen by `Router.select`, so the 5.2 rules, the Wilson admission rule and both flavors apply unchanged.

Its size budget is in the opening of section 12 (v1.386, row DOC21).

### 13.1 Inputs
`Router.decide_delegation(task_name, parent_model, flavor="cost_effective", *, context_tokens, brief_tokens, result_tokens, carry_turns=0, work_calls=1, inline_separate_call=True, cached_read_ratio=1.0, output_reread_share=1.0, brief_output_tokens=None, generator_model=None, exclude_models=(), policy=None) -> DelegationDecision`
- `parent_model`: the parent's model ID. An unknown task, parent or `generator_model` raises `KeyError`; an unknown flavor raises `ValueError` (5.1)
- `context_tokens` (C): tokens already in the parent's context
- The work is one call of the task unless `work_calls` says more (v1.38): each call reads S_in = `task.expected_input_tokens` and writes S_out = `task.expected_output_tokens`; from v1.33 the cost of each path uses the 5.2 sizes of the model doing the work (13.2)
- `work_calls` (K, v1.38, default 1): the work is K successive calls of the task on one path. Each call takes S_in of new input and writes S_out, and call j (j = 1 to K) reads its path's base context (C inline, B delegated) plus the j inputs and the j - 1 outputs so far, so the path's context grows by S_in + S_out per call. K must be an integer `>= 1` that is not a bool, else `ValueError` naming `work_calls`, checked after `carry_turns`
- The bar and the bounds stay per call whatever K: K changes the cost of each path (13.2), the 13.4 context check and the delegate's `select` (13.3), never a success count, a bound or a bar check, so the 13.5 rows read the same bounds. `DelegationDecision` (13.6) has no field for K
- `brief_tokens` (B): what the parent writes to hand the work off. `result_tokens` (R): what the parent reads back
- `carry_turns` (T): parent calls after the parent's next call (13.2) that still re-read what this work leaves in its context. The next call itself is always charged, so T = 0 means the parent makes one more call after the work and stops. When the work is one of several sibling subtasks that the parent would otherwise do one after another, each later sibling done inline re-reads this one, so those calls count in T
- `inline_separate_call`: True (the default) when inline work takes a parent call of its own, False when the parent folds the work into its next call (13.2). It must be a bool, else `ValueError`
- `cached_read_ratio` (rho, v1.41, default 1.0): the price of the parent's cached re-reads of its existing context C, as a fraction of the parent's list input price, for a parent whose provider caches the prompt prefix it has already read; 13.2 says which reads it prices. It must be an `int` or a `float` that is not a bool, with 0 <= rho <= 1 (so NaN and the infinities fail), else `ValueError` naming `cached_read_ratio`, checked after `inline_separate_call`. It moves `inline_cost_usd` only: never `delegate_cost_usd` (from v1.219 except, on a parent with `price_tiers`, the dearer re-read of C in a shared parent call that a path takes over a threshold, on both paths, 13.2), the delegate's `select` (13.3), the 13.4 checks, a bound or a bar check. `DelegationDecision` (13.6) has no field for it
- `output_reread_share` (sigma, v1.404, default 1.0): the share of each work call's output S_out that later calls, work calls and parent calls alike, re-read, for a model whose history keeps each reply and drops its reasoning (`research/ledger-cost-model.md`); 13.2 says which reads it scales. It must be an `int` or a `float` that is not a bool, with 0 <= sigma <= 1 (so NaN and the infinities fail), else `ValueError` naming `output_reread_share`, checked after `cached_read_ratio`. One sigma serves the parent and the delegate. It never shrinks a written output or a context check: the 13.4 check and the delegate's 5.2 rule 5 (13.3) keep each S_out whole, an upper bound on what the context holds, so no sigma admits a path that 1.0 refuses. `DelegationDecision` (13.6) has no field for it. The CLI passes it from v1.408 (`--output-reread-share`, 13.7, row D11c); the 13.9 evaluator keeps 1.0, since a point has no key for it and one with the key fails as any unknown key does, so every committed delegation result re-reads each S_out whole (the one measured share, the ledger runs of 13.15, is no 13.9 input). Not modelled: a share per model, or one for the work calls and another for the parent's later calls
- `brief_output_tokens` (W, v1.405, default None, meaning B): the output tokens of the decision turn's brief, the completion of the call that writes it, for a parent whose call writes more than the brief it hands off, its reasoning for one (`research/ledger-cost-model.md`: a note's call wrote a median 281.0 to 320.0 completion tokens for notes of 163.0 to 176.0, review iter-262 must-fix 1). W replaces B in the brief's output charge alone, `P.cost(0, W)` in 13.2 and `W * out(C)` on a tiered parent (13.2 v1.219, written with B up to v1.409); the delegate's read of the brief, the parent's re-reads of B + R, the delegate's `select` (13.3) and every other term keep B, the brief's own size, so of the two costs W moves `delegate_cost_usd` alone, and through it the 13.5 rows that compare them, never `inline_cost_usd`, the delegate, a bound or a context check. It must be None or an integer >= 0 that is not a bool, else `ValueError` naming `brief_output_tokens`, checked after `output_reread_share`; W is not checked against B. W = B gives the None costs bit for bit, so with the default every decision, reason and committed delegation result keeps its v1.404 bytes. `DelegationDecision` (13.6) has no field for it. The CLI passes it from v1.409 (`--brief-output-tokens`, 13.7, row D12); the 13.9 evaluator keeps W = B, since a point has no key for it and one with the key fails as any unknown key does, and so does every committed delegation result, the ledger runs of 13.15 included (its decision (2)). README `### Inline or sub-agent`'s condition (13.8 v1.256) names the flag among its preconditions (no `--brief-output-tokens`), since at W above B its `B * p_out / p_in` is `W * p_out / p_in`. From v1.412 (row DOC31) README Limitations' inline-or-delegate cost bullet names the flag in the sentence after the `output_reread_share` one: it sets the output tokens of the call that writes the brief, which the brief's size under-states when that call reasons before it writes, with the note calls' medians above and their depths, 20 to 100, which its test reads from the note's Results block. From v1.420 (row DOC33, the Recommendation of the 13.16 v1.413 note) the sentence after that one says that the committed delegation results keep sigma and W at their defaults and how far re-deciding their cells at sigma 0, sigma 0.5 and W = 2 B, each with the other input at its default, moves them, from `research/reread-sensitivity.md`, which it links: the largest share of a file, flavor and bar's cells that changes on AutoBench 2026, LLMRouterBench and the LLM Routing Response Bank, none on tau2-bench and none in `cost_blind`, which compares no costs, and the range of the cost over all of a file, flavor and bar's cells as a factor of the committed picks', each number read by tests/test_research_reread_sensitivity.py from the note's Results blocks to build the sentence, pinned once in that place; the note's Recommendation says that README Limitations links it
- `generator_model` and `exclude_models` mean what they mean in 5.2 and are passed to the delegate's `select`. `exclude_models` limits the delegate only; it never stops the parent working inline
- `policy` (v1.624, row POL1c, default None): a tenant's `Policy` (5.1 v1.622), passed to the delegate's `select` (13.3) and read on the parent's registry row (13.4 rule 4), so neither path reaches a model it rules out. A value that is neither None nor a `Policy` raises `ValueError` naming `policy`, checked after `brief_output_tokens` and before the parent is looked up, so an unknown parent with such a value raises `ValueError`, not `KeyError`. The parent is a model the caller already runs: the policy decides only whether this work may run on it inline. `None` and `Policy()` limit nothing, so every decision is v1.623's bit for bit
- `context_tokens`, `brief_tokens`, `result_tokens` and `carry_turns` must be integers `>= 0` that are not bools, else `ValueError`
- The router is not modified: `router.tasks` is the same after the call

### 13.2 Cost of each path (list price, reported in both flavors)
The accounting follows the parent's calls, each of which re-reads the parent's whole context. Both paths are charged for the same calls, and each only for what that path adds to them:
- The **decision turn**, the parent call that makes this decision, happens on both paths. On the delegate path it also writes the brief, so W (B unless `brief_output_tokens` is set, 13.1) is charged once as parent output; on the inline path it writes nothing extra. Fetching the work's input is free on both paths; reading it is charged on both
- The parent's **next call** after the work is done (on the delegate path, the call that reads the result) and the T calls after it happen on both paths and re-read C on both, so C is not charged in them. Each of these 1 + T calls is charged for the tokens that the path left in the parent's context. What a call writes besides the work, the parent's own next step, is the same on both paths and is not charged
- The work itself: the delegate reads the brief and the work's input in a fresh context and writes the output. Inline, the parent does it either in a call of its own over its whole context (`inline_separate_call=True`) or inside its next call (`inline_separate_call=False`), which then also reads S_in and writes S_out. A separate call fits work that is a step of its own, for example output that goes into a tool call or a file before the parent goes on; folding fits work the parent would do as part of its very next reply anyway. The default, a separate call, gives the higher inline cost

With P the parent's model and D the delegate, for work of one call (K = 1; the v1.38 bullet below gives K calls):
- `delegate_cost_usd = P.cost(0, W) + D.cost(B + S_in, S_out) + (1 + T) * P.cost(B + R, 0)`: the brief written, the delegate's call, then the brief and the result re-read by the next call and the T after it
- `inline_cost_usd = P.cost(C + S_in, S_out) + (1 + T) * P.cost(S_in + S_out, 0)` when `inline_separate_call` is True: the parent's own call for the work, then its input and output re-read by the next call and the T after it
- `inline_cost_usd = P.cost(S_in, S_out) + T * P.cost(S_in + S_out, 0)` when `inline_separate_call` is False: the next call also reads S_in and writes S_out, and both are re-read by the T calls after it
- With K = 1, C appears only in the separate inline call. With a separate call, inline minus delegating to the parent's own model (D = P) is, in exact arithmetic, `P.cost(C, 0) - P.cost(B, W) + (1 + T) * (P.cost(S_in + S_out, 0) - P.cost(B + R, 0))`, so delegating even to its own model can save in two ways: the separate call's re-read of a large context C (the context-isolation case), and later calls that re-read a short brief and result instead of the work's input and output. When the work folds into the next call, C cancels, and delegating to the parent's own model is cheaper only when `T * P.cost(S_in + S_out, 0)` exceeds `P.cost(B, W) + (1 + T) * P.cost(B + R, 0)`, so never with T = 0
- Each expression is evaluated left to right as written, in floating point, from `Model.cost` (4.1); `1 + T` is an integer. `delegate_cost_usd` is `None` when there is no delegate
- v1.212 every `Model.cost` that 13.2 and 13.9 name is `Model.base_cost` (4.1): a total of K calls and a re-read increment carry no one call's input size, so no tier applies to them. On a model without tiers the two are the same value bit for bit, so every decision, reason and committed delegation result keeps its v1.211 bytes; on a model with `price_tiers` both paths stayed at the base prices from v1.212 to v1.218. With K = 1 the delegate's `select` (13.3) is a 5.2 select over one call of the briefed sizes and keeps `Model.cost`, so on a tiered model it ranked the delegates at that call's tier while `delegate_cost_usd` charged the base prices; with K > 1 its candidates were priced at their K calls' total with `Model.base_cost`, as 13.3 v1.38 states (v1.214). From v1.219 (below) a term a tiered model pays is priced per call, so this bullet holds only for a model without tiers, and at K = 1 the delegate is charged what its `select` ranks it at; from v1.222 the 13.9 held-out costs of a tiered model are priced per call too (13.9 v1.222)
- v1.219 per-call tiers (row P1b): on a model with `price_tiers` (4.1) each term of the expressions above that this model's calls pay is priced call by call, each call at its own tier, in place of the v1.212 `Model.base_cost` of a total. A term paid by a model without tiers keeps its v1.212 expression, so on a registry without tiers every decision, reason and committed delegation result keeps its v1.218 bytes (no committed delegation registry has a tier). Write in(n) and out(n) for a model's prices in a call that reads n input tokens (the 4.1 tier of that call, else `price_in` and `price_out`); each call's cost is its tokens times those prices over 1,000,000, in floating point. C, B, R, T, K, rho, S_in and S_out are as above, the sizes those of the model doing the work (v1.33):
  - Work calls. Call j of a path's K (j = 1 to K) reads X + j * S_in + (j - 1) * S_out, X the path's base context (C inline, B delegated), and writes S_out. On a tiered model it pays in(its read) on its charged input and out(its read) on its S_out output; its charged input is its read on the delegate, and rho * C + j * S_in + (j - 1) * S_out inline, C at rho as in v1.41, while its tier is that of the whole read whatever rho. The work term is the `math.fsum` of the calls' costs, j ascending. So with K = 1 the delegate's work term is `D.cost(B + S_in, S_out)` exactly, the cost its K = 1 `select` ranks it at (13.3), and from K = 2 that `select` prices each tiered candidate the same way (13.3 v1.38)
  - Shared parent calls. The decision turn, the parent's next call and the T calls after it happen on both paths and read C, and each is charged only for what the path adds to it, A input tokens (and, for a folded next call, the S_out it writes). On a tiered parent such a call is charged `A * in(C + A) + rho * C * (in(C + A) - in(C))` on input, plus its added output at out(C + A): the added tokens at the tier of the call's whole read, and the dearer re-read of C when A takes the call over a threshold that C alone is not over, at rho like every cached read of C (13.1); the second part is 0 when in(C + A) = in(C), and negative when the tier the call reaches is cheaper than C's own, since the path then lowers the price of the whole call (4.1 does not require a tier to be dearer; no packaged tier is cheaper). So the decision turn's brief on the delegate path is `W * out(C)` (A = 0), each of the 1 + T calls after delegated work has A = B + R, and each after separate inline work has A = K * (S_in + S_out)
  - Folded inline work. The K-th work call is the parent's next call, a shared call with A = K * S_in + (K - 1) * S_out and S_out written, so the folded work term is the `math.fsum` of the K - 1 work calls before it (the work-call bullet) and that next call's charge, in that order, and each of the T calls after it has A = K * (S_in + S_out)
  - Each path is then the v1.212 sum with its terms so priced, evaluated left to right: delegated, brief + the delegate's work + (1 + T) * one call after it; separate inline, the work + (1 + T) * one call after it; folded, the folded work term + T * one call after it. A tiered delegate under a parent without tiers moves only the delegate's work term, and a tiered parent only the parent's terms
  - Not charged, as before: the parent's own output in a shared call, the same tokens on both paths, so where a path's additions take such a call over a threshold the higher price of that output is left out, an under-statement that README Limitations states. The 13.4 context check, the bounds and the 13.5 rows are unchanged
  - v1.242 why that output stays uncharged (row P1d): no input gives it a size. Of the shared calls, only the 1 + T calls after the work can be at a tier that differs between the paths: the decision turn reads C on both paths, A = 0, so it pays in(C) and out(C) on both, and its brief on the delegated path is the `W * out(C)` above. What each of the 1 + T calls writes besides the work, the parent's own next step (in a folded next call, besides its S_out), is the size of no 13.1 input: W is what the decision turn writes, R what the next call reads back and S_out what each work call writes, and each is charged where this section charges it. So a call of those 1 + T that reads C + A on one path and C + A' on the other leaves out o * (out(C + A) - out(C + A')) of the difference between the paths, o that call's own output, which no input states: 0 on a parent without tiers and wherever both reads are in one tier, else an under-statement of the path whose read is in the dearer tier. Pricing it would need a new input, the size of the parent's own output in each later call, which v1.242 does not add: the 13.9 rows record only the work's calls, so no committed delegation result could set it. No cost, reason, check or committed result changes
- v1.33: S_in and S_out in these expressions are the 5.2 sizes of the model doing the work on that path. In `inline_cost_usd` they are the parent's, S_in(P) and S_out(P), in its call for the work and in the later re-reads of that input and output; in `delegate_cost_usd` they are the delegate's, in `D.cost(B + S_in(D), S_out(D))`. For a model without measured token counts they are the task's expected tokens, so with no token totals each expression is the v1.32 one. With D = P both paths use the same sizes, so the D = P difference above holds with S_in(P) and S_out(P). The 12.3 evaluator builds its stats from counts alone, so its results do not move; from v1.35 the 13.9 harness adds each model's calibration-half token totals to its stats, so its decisions price each path at these per-model sizes (13.9)
- v1.38, K work calls (13.1). Write w_in = K(K + 1) / 2 and w_out = K(K - 1) / 2, both integers. The K calls of a path with base context X read `K * X + w_in * S_in + w_out * S_out` tokens in all and write `K * S_out`, and each path prices its K calls as one `Model.cost` of those integer totals (from v1.212 `Model.base_cost`, below), which is the sum of the K calls' costs at the base prices in exact arithmetic since `Model.base_cost` is linear (4.1); on a model with `price_tiers` it is not the sum of the K calls' tiered costs. S_in and S_out are the sizes of the model doing the work, as in v1.33. With P the parent and D the delegate:
  - `delegate_cost_usd = P.cost(0, W) + D.cost(K * B + w_in * S_in + w_out * S_out, K * S_out) + (1 + T) * P.cost(B + R, 0)`: the brief written once, the delegate's K calls, then the brief and the result re-read by the next call and the T after it
  - `inline_cost_usd = P.cost(K * C + w_in * S_in + w_out * S_out, K * S_out) + (1 + T) * P.cost(K * (S_in + S_out), 0)` when `inline_separate_call` is True: K parent calls of the work's own, each over the whole context, then the K inputs and outputs re-read by the next call and the T after it
  - `inline_cost_usd = P.cost((K - 1) * C + w_in * S_in + w_out * S_out, K * S_out) + T * P.cost(K * (S_in + S_out), 0)` when `inline_separate_call` is False: the last of the K calls is the parent's next call, which re-reads C on both paths, so C is charged only in the K - 1 calls before it. Folding takes the last work call into the next call, never all K
  - With K = 1, w_in = 1 and w_out = 0, so the token totals are the integers of the three expressions above and every cost, reason and check is the v1.37 one bit for bit
  - With a separate call, inline minus delegating to the parent's own model is, in exact arithmetic, `P.cost(K * C, 0) - P.cost(K * B, W) + (1 + T) * (P.cost(K * (S_in + S_out), 0) - P.cost(B + R, 0))`: each inline call re-reads C where each delegated one re-reads B, which is where context isolation pays most. Folded it is `P.cost((K - 1) * C, 0) - P.cost(K * B, W) + T * P.cost(K * (S_in + S_out), 0) - (1 + T) * P.cost(B + R, 0)`, so from K = 2 a large C can make delegating to its own model cheaper even with T = 0
- v1.41, cached context reads (13.1). The reads rho prices are the parent's reads of C in the inline work calls: the K calls of its own when `inline_separate_call` is True, the K - 1 calls before its next call when it is False. They are the only reads of C that 13.2 charges (the decision turn, the next call and the T calls after it read C on both paths and are not charged), and each of them finds C as the prefix of its prompt, just read by the decision turn. Those K * C or (K - 1) * C tokens are priced at rho times the parent's list input price; everything else stays at list price on both paths: the work's input and output, their re-reads by later work calls and by the 1 + T later parent calls, the brief, the result, every read of the delegate, and all output. With P the parent:
  - `inline_cost_usd = P.cost(K * C * rho + w_in * S_in + w_out * S_out, K * S_out) + (1 + T) * P.cost(K * (S_in + S_out), 0)` when `inline_separate_call` is True
  - `inline_cost_usd = P.cost((K - 1) * C * rho + w_in * S_in + w_out * S_out, K * S_out) + T * P.cost(K * (S_in + S_out), 0)` when `inline_separate_call` is False
  - `delegate_cost_usd` is the v1.38 expression whatever rho, and so is the delegate
  - The first argument of `P.cost` is evaluated left to right: the integer `K * C` or `(K - 1) * C`, times rho, then the integer terms added, so with a float rho it is a float. With rho = 1.0 its value is the v1.38 integer total, and `Model.cost` (from v1.212 `Model.base_cost`) converts an int to that same float before it multiplies by a float price, so every cost, reason and check is the v1.40 one bit for bit (while the token totals and their products with the prices stay below 2^53, about 9e15); with the int rho = 1 the argument is the v1.38 integer itself. Folded work of one call has no C term, so its cost is the same for every rho
  - In exact arithmetic rho scales the C term of each inline minus delegating difference in the v1.38 bullet. With a separate call it is `P.cost(K * C * rho, 0) - P.cost(K * B, W) + (1 + T) * (P.cost(K * (S_in + S_out), 0) - P.cost(B + R, 0))`, so at rho = 0 the parent's context no longer favours delegating to its own model, and only later calls that re-read a short brief and result instead of the work can; folded, the C term is `P.cost((K - 1) * C * rho, 0)`
  - Not modelled: a surcharge for writing the cache, a cache that expires between calls, a discount on any other re-read on either path, and a cached price for the delegate. rho is one number the caller states for the parent; the AutoBench pool (13.9) has no cached prices, so evidence with rho < 1 states it as an assumption
- v1.404, output re-reads (13.1, row D11a): sigma scales each re-read of a work call's S_out and nothing else. In the v1.38 and v1.41 expressions each read `w_out * S_out` is `w_out * sigma * S_out` and each read `K * (S_in + S_out)` is `K * (S_in + sigma * S_out)`; on a tiered model (v1.219) call j reads X + j * S_in + (j - 1) * sigma * S_out, which sets its tier, and the folded next call has A = K * S_in + (K - 1) * sigma * S_out. The written outputs, B, R and every read of C keep their sizes, and sigma = 1.0 gives every v1.403 cost bit for bit, the v1.41 first argument then being a float of the v1.38 integer's value even at the int rho = 1
- This is still an approximation. It assumes that each of the K work calls reads its path's base context and every earlier work call in full (each earlier S_out at sigma from v1.404), with nothing summarised between calls (13.8), no prompt caching beyond the v1.41 ratio on the parent's reads of C, the same parent output after the work on both paths (checking a delegate's result may take more), and that the parent's later calls fit its context on both paths: C + K * (S_in + S_out) is checked for inline (13.4) but C + B + R is not checked for delegate

### 13.3 The delegate
- The delegate is the primary of `Router.select(task_name, flavor, generator_model, exclude_models)` run with the same registry, stats and priors on a copy of the task whose `expected_input_tokens` is `S_in + B`, so the context rule (5.2 rule 5) and the `cost_effective` ranking see the brief the delegate actually reads. It may be the parent's own model
- `route` is that `RouteDecision`, or `None` when that `select` raises `NoModelClearsBar`. `delegate_quality_lb` is the `quality_lb` of the route's primary candidate. The delegate clears the bar when `route.below_bar` is False
- The parent's share of `delegate_cost_usd` is the same for every delegate, so the `cost_effective` primary of this `select` is also the passing delegate with the lowest `delegate_cost_usd`
- v1.33: in that `select` every model's input size is its 5.2 input size plus B, so a model with measured token counts is priced at `model.cost(mean input + B, mean output)` and any other at `model.cost(S_in + B, S_out)`, which keeps the bullet above true; rule 5 still checks the copy's expected tokens, S_in + B + S_out. One way is a private copy of the stats with B times `token_trials` added to each input total, since rounding up `(I + B * n) / n` gives the rounded-up `I / n` plus B exactly. `router.stats` and `router.tasks` are the same after the call
- v1.38, K work calls: in that `select`, rule 5 checks each model's window against the delegate's last call, `B + K * (S_in + S_out)` with the task's expected sizes (that call reads B + K * S_in + (K - 1) * S_out and writes S_out), not against the K calls' total, and each candidate's `list_cost`, and its `routing_cost` in `cost_effective`, is the cost of its K calls, `model.cost(K * B + w_in * S_in + w_out * S_out, K * S_out)` (from v1.404 with `w_out * sigma * S_out`, 13.2; from v1.212 `model.base_cost`, the K calls' total at the base prices; from v1.219, on a model with `price_tiers`, the `math.fsum` of its K calls each at its own tier, 13.2) with its 5.2 sizes (13.2), so the `cost_effective` primary is still the passing delegate with the lowest `delegate_cost_usd`, and the 13.7 exit-3 table prints that cost. Pricing a model at its last call alone would rank by the wrong mix of input and output price, since the K calls' input grows as K squared and their output as K. With K = 1 this is the v1.34 `select`, run as v1.34 runs it. One way for K > 1 is a private `Router` subclass whose candidates are checked and priced this way; `router.stats` and `router.tasks` are the same after the call
- v1.573 items per call (row VAR1c): every cost of section 13 prices a model's calls whole, whatever its `items_per_call` (4.1), since the work decided here is one piece of work, not k items: the delegate's `select` prices each candidate at its call cost, undivided, at one work call as at K (v1.38), so its `cost_effective` primary is still the passing delegate with the lowest `delegate_cost_usd`, and the 13.9 held-out costs read each row's tokens as one call. With no variant above k = 1 every decision is v1.572's
- v1.624 policy (row POL1c): that `select` is run with the call's `policy`, on the copy built for K = 1 and on the router built for K > 1 (v1.38) alike, so the delegate and each fallback of `route` met 5.2 rules 5b to 5d, and `route.candidates` give each ruled-out model's reason. When the policy leaves that `select` nothing it may choose, it raises `NoModelClearsBar` and `route` is None, as for any failed `select`, and 13.5 decides. `Executor.call_delegated` runs `route` as decided (7, v1.11), so the hand-off reaches no ruled-out model with no policy argument of its own. Without a policy, or with `Policy()`, that `select` is v1.623's
  - Tests (tests/test_policy_delegation.py): the keyword's place and default on the function and the method, and its check before the parent's lookup; each parent code, the first of 5b to 5d giving it, and rules 1 to 3 coming first; a parent the policy allows still inline; no allowed route with a ruled-out parent raising `NoModelClearsBar`; the delegate and its fallbacks inside the allowed set in both flavors at K = 1 and K = 3, the router left as it was, and at K = 4 the decision of a registry of the allowed models alone; `call_delegated` trying only allowed models; and no keyword, `None` and `Policy()` giving the `decision_sha256` of 960 decisions on the shipped data that a v1.623 copy of the package (b20bc4b) gave. No evidence or research script, nor `delegation_eval.py` or the demo, passes a policy, so every delegation results file keeps its bytes
- v1.627 procedure keys (row BRIEF1, review iter-478 should-fix 3): the private copy of the stats that v1.33 builds for K = 1 holds each procedure key of the task (4.3 v1.577) with its counts and summed `cost_usd` as they are, and no token totals, since a procedure key holds none. That `select` is passed no `procedures`, so no procedure is a candidate there, and with or without a procedure trial on the task every decision is the same. Before v1.627 the copy re-added a procedure key without its cost, so a call with B > 0 on a task whose stats held token totals and a procedure trial raised `ValueError` from `Stats.add`; the router built for K > 1 reads `router.stats` itself and never raised. The copy still holds no cache counts, which that `select` does not read (5.2 v1.588), and, until v1.628 (below), no times (4.3 v1.626). With no procedure key every decision is v1.626's
  - Tests (tests/test_briefed_procedure.py): with a brief, a procedure trial on the task (with a model, without one, and with no trials) gives the decision the same stats without it give, in both flavors, for every parent, inline call folded or separate; the copy keeps each procedure key's counts and summed cost bit for bit and no token totals, and only the task's keys; `router.stats` saves the same bytes after the call; at K = 3 the decision is the same with and without the key; and with a procedure trial on every example task the 960 decisions on the shipped data that tests/test_policy_delegation.py pins keep their `decision_sha256`. tests/test_procedures.py's guard that delegation.py does not read procedures lets it name them only in that copy and its import, and checks it passes `select` no `procedures`
- v1.628 times (row LAT1b, review iter-478 should-fix 3): the private copy of the stats that v1.33 builds for K = 1 also holds each key's times as they are (4.3 v1.626), and both briefed task copies keep `max_p95_ms` and `latency_unknown`, so 5.2 rules 5e and 5f (v1.628) read in the delegate's `select` what they read in the router's own, at one work call or K (the router built for K > 1 reads `router.stats` itself); a time is a trial's as measured, without the brief, as its counts are. So the delegate is never a route the bar rules out, with or without a brief, and when the bar rules out every route 13.5 runs as for any `NoModelClearsBar` there. With no bar every decision is v1.627's

### 13.4 Is inline allowed?
The first rule that applies blocks inline (the parent must delegate) and becomes the reason:
1. the parent's family is in `task.exclude_families`: `parent_excluded_family`
2. `task.independent_of_generator`, `generator_model` is given, and the parent is that model or in its family: `parent_not_independent` (the parent cannot check its own family's output)
3. `P.context_window < C + K * (S_in + S_out)`, with the task's expected S_in and S_out whatever the parent's measured sizes (v1.33, as 5.2 rule 5): `parent_context_full`. The last of the K work calls (v1.38) reads C + K * S_in + (K - 1) * S_out and writes S_out, folded or not; K = 1 gives the v1.37 check C + S_in + S_out
4. v1.624 (row POL1c): a `policy` is given and the parent's registry row fails one of 5.2 rules 5b to 5d, read as that `select` reads them (`allowed_routes` matching its `id` or its `base_id`, an unstated region or retention failing closed): `parent_policy_excluded` (5b), `parent_region_unavailable` (5c) or `parent_zdr_required` (5d), the first that applies. It comes after rules 1 to 3, as 5b to 5d follow rules 1 to 5a in 5.2, so a parent the task, the call or its window already blocks keeps its v1.623 reason. The parent's model fails the same rule in the delegate's `select`, so the delegate is never the parent's own model
5. v1.631 (row LAT1d): the task sets `max_p95_ms` (4.2 v1.628) and the parent's time on the task, read as 5.2 rules 5e and 5f read a route's (`stats.p95_latency_ms` on the key of the task and the parent's ID, known only once that key holds at least `task.min_samples` times), is above the bar: `parent_too_slow` (5e); or that time is unknown and the task's `latency_unknown` is `"deny"`: `parent_latency_unknown` (5f). It comes after rules 1 to 4, as 5e and 5f follow rules 1 to 5d in 5.2, so a parent that an earlier rule blocks keeps its v1.630 reason. In the delegate's `select`, which reads the same key, bar and `min_samples` (13.3 v1.628), the parent's model is ruled out by the same rule or an earlier one, so the delegate is never the parent's own model

The parent clears the bar when its measured trials on the task are at least `task.min_samples` and `parent_quality_lb = wilson_lower_bound(successes, trials, task.confidence)` is at least `task.bar`: the admission test of 5.2 rules 6 and 7. `parent_quality_lb` is 0.0 when the parent is unmeasured; the parent is measured when it has `trials > 0`, as in 5.3
- v1.582 fine-tunes (row SELF1b): rules 1 and 2 read the parent's and the generator's `family`, which for a fine-tune is its base's (4.1). So a fine-tune parent whose generator is its base, or another model of its base's family, has `parent_not_independent`, as does a base parent whose generator is a fine-tune of it, and a fine-tune parent whose base's family is in `exclude_families` has `parent_excluded_family`; the delegate's route reads 5.2 v1.582. Without `base_model` every decision is v1.581's
- v1.628 (row LAT1b): no rule read the parent's time, so a task's `max_p95_ms` never blocked inline: the inline work is the parent's own calls in its running context, not a routed call. From v1.631 rule 5 reads it (row LAT1d, the bullet below)
- v1.631 (row LAT1d), why the parent's time on the task stands for its inline work: the key's times are trials of the parent's model on the task, each the caller's measure from its call to its answer (4.3 v1.626), so each holds whatever that call waited for, queueing and the network included, beside the model's own reading and writing. Inline, the same model reads the task's input after its context C, in a call of its own or folded into its next call (13.2), and writes the same output, but none of that makes a trial's time a bound on the inline work's, either way: a trial that queued can be slower than an inline call that did more work, and a parent fast on its trials can be slower inline over a long C. So the rule is a conservative admission policy, not a measured or proven bound: the trials' p95 is the only time the library holds for this model on this work, and it is the proxy 5.2 rules 5e and 5f already take for every route, whose trial p95 is no bound on its next call either. Holding the parent to it treats both paths alike, so a model `select` rules out as too slow for the task does not do the same work inline. It can rule out an inline path that would have met the bar, and admit one that would not; a caller who knows its inline time differs from its trials' sets no bar on the task, or times its inline calls as trials of their own. The bar is per call whatever K (13.1), so K changes no time read. The row departs from its backlog text, which said to drop the rule if the time is no bound, for the reason above (review iter-484 must-fix 1). The rule moves `inline_allowed` and the 13.5 row alone: the costs of both paths, `parent_quality_lb` and the delegate's `select` are computed as without it. With no bar no rule reads a time, so every decision is v1.630's bit for bit, whatever `latency_unknown` says and whatever times the stats hold

### 13.5 Choosing (the first row that applies wins)
1. Inline blocked: delegate, with the blocking reason and `below_bar = route.below_bar`. With no route, raise `NoModelClearsBar`
2. The delegate clears the bar and the parent does not: delegate, `parent_below_bar`
3. Both clear, `cost_effective`: delegate when `delegate_cost_usd < inline_cost_usd` (`delegate_cheaper`); inline when it is greater (`inline_cheaper`); on an exact tie, delegate when `delegate_quality_lb > parent_quality_lb` (`delegate_better`), else inline (`inline_as_good`)
4. Both clear, `cost_blind`: delegate when `delegate_quality_lb > parent_quality_lb` (`delegate_better`), else inline (`inline_as_good`). Cost is not compared
5. Only the parent clears: inline, `only_parent_clears`
6. Neither clears and `task.on_no_model` is `"refuse"`: raise `NoModelClearsBar`
7. Neither clears and `task.on_no_model` is `"best_available"`: reason `none_clear`, `below_bar` True. Delegate when `route is not None and route.basis == "measured" and (parent unmeasured or delegate_quality_lb > parent_quality_lb)`; else, in `cost_effective` (v1.31), delegate when `route is not None and route.basis == "measured"`, the parent is measured, `delegate_quality_lb == parent_quality_lb` and `delegate_cost_usd < inline_cost_usd`; else inline when the parent is measured; else delegate when there is a route (its basis is `prior`); else raise `NoModelClearsBar`
- `below_bar` is False in rows 2 to 5. A raised `NoModelClearsBar` carries the `.candidates` of the failed `select`
- Costs and bounds are compared with plain `<`, `>` and `==` on the floats as computed, never with a tolerance, so two costs that differ only by rounding are not a tie
- Equal-quality ties go inline in `cost_blind` (rows 4 and 7) and, in `cost_effective`, on an exact cost tie (an exact cost tie in row 3 is settled by the bounds first), because a hand-off has costs the model does not price: a brief can drop detail, and the parent has to trust a result it did not produce. In `cost_effective` a strictly lower `delegate_cost_usd` delegates in row 3 whatever the bounds, and in row 7 when the bounds are equal (v1.31)
- A model below the bar is chosen only under `best_available`, in row 1 or row 7, and then `below_bar` is True
- v1.31: row 7 orders the two paths as 5.3 orders the `best_available` fallback, by bound first and then, in `cost_effective` only, by the path's list-price cost (13.2), so a measured delegate whose bound equals a measured parent's and whose `delegate_cost_usd` is strictly lower is taken. The usual case is the parent's own model as the delegate (its bound is the parent's, from the same stats), where delegating saves the separate inline call's re-read of C (13.2). The costs are compared as computed (no tolerance, as above), so a delegate path that is cheaper only by rounding is taken. With a measured parent, `cost_blind`, an exact cost tie, a lower delegate bound and a `prior` route stay inline; an unmeasured parent still delegates to any route, as before. The reason is `none_clear` in every branch of row 7, so no reason code is added (13.6)
- Row 5 has no equal-model case: a parent that clears in 13.4 reaches 5.2 rule 8 (`passes`) in the delegate's `select` unless rules 1 to 5 stop it, since rules 6 and 7 read the same stats, bar, confidence and `min_samples`, and one passing candidate makes the route clear the bar. So when the route is below the bar, the parent was stopped there by rule 1 (it is in `exclude_models`) or rule 5 (its window holds C + S_in + S_out but not S_in + B + S_out); rules 2 to 4 are the 13.4 blocks that send the decision to row 1. Row 5 stays inline in both flavors, since its delegate does not clear the bar and the parent does; that includes a different delegate whose bound equals or exceeds the parent's but that has too few trials (5.2 rule 6)
- v1.624 (row POL1c): row 1 takes a parent that 13.4 rule 4 blocks, with its policy reason and `below_bar = route.below_bar`, or raises `NoModelClearsBar` with the candidates of the delegate's `select` when the policy leaves it no route. The row 5 bullet stays true under a policy, since 5.2 rules 5b to 5d on the parent are 13.4 rule 4, which sends the decision to row 1 first; the costs and bounds of both paths are read as without a policy
- v1.631 (row LAT1d): row 1 takes a parent that 13.4 rule 5 blocks, with `parent_too_slow` or `parent_latency_unknown` and `below_bar = route.below_bar`, or raises `NoModelClearsBar` with the candidates of the delegate's `select` when the bar leaves it no route, so a parent that clears the success bar but not the latency bar no longer works inline when no other route is left. The row 5 bullet holds under a bar, since 5.2 rules 5e and 5f on the parent's model are 13.4 rule 5, which sends the decision to row 1 first; from v1.628 to v1.630, when 13.4 read no time, a parent those rules stopped in the delegate's `select` could reach row 5 and work inline

### 13.6 `DelegationDecision`
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class DelegationDecision`, fields in this order: `task: str`, `flavor: str`, `parent: str`, `mode: str` (`"inline"` or `"delegate"`), `model: str` (the parent for inline, `route.primary` for delegate), `reason: str`, `below_bar: bool`, `inline_allowed: bool`, `inline_cost_usd: float`, `delegate_cost_usd: float | None`, `parent_quality_lb: float`, `delegate_quality_lb: float | None`, `route: RouteDecision | None`
- `.to_dict()` returns plain JSON-able types, keys in the field order above, with `route` as `route.to_dict()` or `None`
- Module constants with these exact values: `INLINE = "inline"`, `DELEGATE = "delegate"`, and reason codes whose values are their names in lower case: `PARENT_EXCLUDED_FAMILY`, `PARENT_NOT_INDEPENDENT`, `PARENT_CONTEXT_FULL`, `PARENT_POLICY_EXCLUDED`, `PARENT_REGION_UNAVAILABLE`, `PARENT_ZDR_REQUIRED` (the three from v1.624), `PARENT_TOO_SLOW`, `PARENT_LATENCY_UNKNOWN` (the two from v1.631), `PARENT_BELOW_BAR`, `DELEGATE_CHEAPER`, `INLINE_CHEAPER`, `DELEGATE_BETTER`, `INLINE_AS_GOOD`, `ONLY_PARENT_CLEARS`, `NONE_CLEAR`
- `DelegationDecision` is re-exported from `model_routing` and listed in `__all__`; the constants stay in `model_routing.delegation`
- v1.11: `Executor.call_delegated(decision, messages, ...)` runs a `delegate` decision on its route, with fallback and logging as for any call (7)
- v1.38: the fields, `to_dict()` and the constants are unchanged; K is an input only (13.1)
- v1.41: the fields, `to_dict()` and the constants are unchanged; rho is an input only (13.1)
- v1.624: the fields and `to_dict()` are unchanged; `policy` is an input only (13.1), and its three parent codes are constants of `model_routing.delegation`, not exported, as the others are
- v1.631: the fields and `to_dict()` are unchanged, the parent's time being in no field; the two parent codes of 13.4 rule 5 are constants of `model_routing.delegation`, not exported, as the others are

- `model-routing delegate TASK --parent MODEL --context-tokens N --brief-tokens N --result-tokens N [--carry-turns N] [--work-calls N] [--fold-inline] [--cached-read-ratio X] [--output-reread-share X] [--brief-output-tokens N] [--flavor cost_effective|cost_blind] [--generator MODEL] [--exclude MODEL ...] [--policy FILE] [--registry PATH] [--tasks PATH] [--stats PATH] [--priors PATH] [--json]`, with the defaults of section 10; `--fold-inline` passes `inline_separate_call=False`; `--work-calls` (v1.38, default 1) passes `work_calls`; `--cached-read-ratio` (v1.41, default 1.0) passes `cached_read_ratio` as a float; `--output-reread-share` (v1.408, default 1.0) passes `output_reread_share` (13.1) as a float; `--brief-output-tokens` (v1.409, default unset, meaning B) passes `brief_output_tokens` (13.1) as an integer, and with it unset the CLI prints what v1.408 printed, byte for byte
- Prints exactly eight lines, one per key in this order, the key, a colon, spaces, then the value: `mode`, `model`, `reason`, `below_bar` (`true` or `false`), `inline_cost_usd` and `delegate_cost_usd` (6 decimals), `parent_quality_lb` and `delegate_quality_lb` (3 decimals); a `None` value prints as `-`. `--json` prints `DelegationDecision.to_dict()`
- Exit codes: 0 success; 2 bad input (as for `select`, plus a `--parent` that is not in the registry, a token option (from v1.409 `--brief-output-tokens` included) that is not an integer `>= 0`, from v1.38, a `--work-calls` that is not an integer `>= 1`, from v1.41, a `--cached-read-ratio` and, from v1.408, an `--output-reread-share` that is not a number in [0, 1], `nan` and `inf` included), including a missing required option, with exactly one `error: ...` line on stderr and it is the last line (an argument-parsing error prints the usage first, as for `select`); 3 `NoModelClearsBar`, with the candidate table on stderr as for `select`

The eight lines and `--json` keep their form, and with `{}`, or without the option, every output is v1.624's bytes. - v1.206, where delegation pays: `research/where-delegation-pays.md` and its script `research/where_delegation_pays.py` (standard library only; `python research/where_delegation_pays.py [--root PATH]`, PATH the repository root, by default the script's checkout) ask whether the per-task 13.5 decision beats a fixed policy, always inline or always delegate, on the committed delegation evidence (row R17). It reads only the `summary` of the committed delegation files, in this order: `evidence/delegation/results.json` (13.10), `evidence/tau2-bench-delegation/results.json` and `evidence/tau2-bench-delegation/pooled.json` (13.12), `evidence/llmrouterbench-delegation/results.json` (13.13) and (v1.323, row R28) `evidence/response-bank-delegation/results.json` (13.14), five files of four datasets (the first four to v1.322). A row is one (bar, flavor, point, parent) with its three strategies (13.9). The decision's (`success`, `cost_usd`) pair is compared exactly, as floats, with always inline's and always delegate's, and the row takes the first class that applies: `= delegate` or `= inline` (equal to that policy's pair in both), `better` (a success at least both and a cost at most both), `beaten on success` (a fixed policy has a higher success at no more cost), `beaten on cost` (one has the same success at a lower cost), else `trade-off`. A row is `= delegate` exactly when its decision `delegate_rate` is 1.0 and `= inline` exactly when it is 0.0, which the script checks. A changed row is a row of the last four classes; its gain is the decision's success minus the higher of the two fixed policies' successes. Output: a title line; per file a line with its name, path, rows, tasks, bars, the number of points and of parents, a header, and one line per flavor and bar in the file's config order with the rows of each class and `top success`, the changed rows with a gain above 0; then per flavor the changed rows by point index, a line against always delegate (the changed rows, those that cost less than it, of those the ones at no less success, and the rest) and the changed row with the largest gain, the first in file order on a tie, with the three pairs and the gain, or `no changed row` on both lines; last, `All five files` (`All four files` to v1.322), the header and one line per flavor over the five files, bar `all`. Successes and costs to 4 decimals, the gain signed. Exit 2 with one `error: ` line naming the file when a file is missing, is not JSON or not a JSON object, lacks a key the report reads, a row lacks a strategy or repeats one, a success or a cost is not a number (an `int` or a `float` that is not a bool), or the rate check fails. (v1.208) The rate check is a consistency check on the committed files, not a property of 13.9: a file whose two fixed policies share one pair, or whose mixed decision ties a policy exactly, would fail it. Counts of rows, tasks, points, parents and changed rows print as `1 row` and `2 rows`. With inline work in a call of its own, inline minus delegating to the parent's own model is, in exact arithmetic on a model without tiers, `p_in * K * (rho * C - B) - p_out * B + (1 + T) * p_in * (K * (S_in + S_out) - B - R)`, with p_in and p_out the parent's list prices per token and S_in and S_out its 5.2 sizes (the 13.2 difference for D = P, in its v1.38 and v1.41 forms). Where the parent is a candidate that passes the delegate's `select`, the `cost_effective` primary costs no more on its work than the parent's own model would (13.3), and where no candidate passes, the 5.3 order puts a measured primary at a bound at least the parent's and, at an equal bound, a work cost at most its own; so a separate inline call costs more than delegating whenever that difference is above 0, and since the sizes are at least 0 it is at every size when `slack * p_in > B * p_out`, `slack = K * (rho * C - B) - (1 + T) * (B + R)` tokens: for B > 0, a parent whose output price is under slack / B times its input price. A positive slack makes B < C, so a parent that clears 13.4 also passes 5.2 rule 5 in that `select` and 13.5 row 5 cannot occur (its bullet above); rows 1 and 2 delegate; so in `cost_effective`, at a point and parent that meet the condition, on a run that excludes no model and measures every model (13.9), every cell delegates: row 3 with `delegate_cheaper`, row 7 with `none_clear`.
