### 13.15 Measured hand-off paths: the ledger runs (`evidence/ledger-handoff/results.py`, v1.394)

- Source (row E23, the recommendation of `research/hand-off-data.md` `## A fresh search for paired inline and delegated runs (2026-11-14)`): https://github.com/akshitanchan/attention-handoff-tax at d891b4eb92abf039431be850646830b486f9e5af, the code and data of https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06069. Licence: its LICENSE file gives CC BY 4.0 for `data/` and `config/` and MIT for the code, so attribution only and no licence call. One model, `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (the `model` of each run settings file), makes every call
- What it measures, a surrogate for the 13 hand-off and never that hand-off: `single` runs each item's L ledger steps in one context, the whole history in every call; `decomposed`, called the chain here, runs every five steps in a fresh context that starts from a note the previous context wrote (a call of its own), so a successor takes over and no parent reads a result back. 300 (depth, item) items, 100 at each of depths 20, 50 and 100, the same keys on both paths. The probe (`handoff.jsonl`) takes 100 items 12 steps in and continues them 5 steps in the same conversation (`history`) or from a note of budget 100, 300 or 900 tokens (`note_100`, `note_300`, `note_900`)
- The script, standard library only and outside the package: `python evidence/ledger-handoff/results.py --out PATH [--cache DIR]` checks `--out` before any download, as 13.11 does; downloads the six files `FILES` names, `data/ledger/{single,decomposed,handoff}.jsonl` and `config/ledger/config_{single,decomposed,handoff}.json`, from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akshitanchan/attention-handoff-tax/<revision>/` into a cache outside the repo (default `~/.cache/ai-model-routing-evidence/ledger-handoff`, each under its base name), and checks each by its size and by the sha256 the repository's `SHA256SUMS` lists for it at that revision before any read (a present file that fails is kept and refused, a failed download leaves no `.part` file, a download error is an `OSError` naming the path); reads each JSON Lines file line by line; writes `--out` through `<out>.part` and prints the results file to stdout with 13.11's `print_report` before the rename; on any failure exits 2 with one `error:` line and leaves no `<out>.part`
- Checks, each a `ValueError` naming the file and, in a JSON Lines file, the line: every line UTF-8 JSON holding an object, a blank line skipped and a file with no record refused; each run settings file's `command` is its run and its `model` is `openai/gpt-oss-20b`; `L` an int of at least 1, `item` and every token count an int from 0 to 2**63 - 1 and never a bool; `final_ok`, `inc_ok` and `abs_ok` 0 or 1; `steps` (and the probe's `pre`) a non-empty list of call objects with `prompt_tokens` and `completion_tokens`; a chain record's `notes` a list of call objects, each with `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens` and `note_tokens`; a (depth, item) key once per file and the two files holding the same keys; a probe item once, the last `pre` step's `balance` an int, with exactly the four arms, each note arm's `s` its budget and its `note_tokens`, `note_prompt_tokens` and int `note_balance` present, and every item holding as many `pre` steps and as many continued steps as the others
- The results file, `evidence/ledger-handoff/results.json` (about 4 KB): `source` (repo, revision, licence and each file's path, bytes and sha256), `model`, then `depths`, per depth in ascending order: `items`; `final_ok` per path (`single`, `chain`); `chain_lost`, the items `single` solves and the chain does not, and `chain_gained`, the reverse; `median_prompt_tokens` and `median_completion_tokens` per path, each the median over items of the item's summed counts, the chain's note calls counted on the chain path; `median_notes` per item and `median_note_tokens` over every note of the depth (null when it has none). Then `probe`: `items`, `pre_steps` (12), `steps` (5) and per arm, in the order above, `all_inc_ok` and `all_abs_ok`, the items whose continued steps all hold the flag, and `median_prompt_tokens` over the continued steps; each note arm adds `note_budget`, `inc_ok_lost`, `inc_ok_gained`, `abs_ok_lost` and `abs_ok_gained` against `history` on the same item, `note_balance_kept` (items whose `note_balance` equals the last `pre` step's `balance`, the balance that step's output stated, right or wrong, so a count of what the note carries forward and not of correct balances), `median_note_tokens` and `median_note_prompt_tokens`, the prompt of the note's own call, which read the history and which the arm's prompt median leaves out. Medians are floats, as `statistics.median` gives them. `reasoning_tokens` are not summed: on each of the 37,100 calls of the two ledger files they are at most `completion_tokens`, a part of that count, so the completion medians hold them
- Decisions, each with why: (1) no price. The registry has no `openai/gpt-oss-20b` row; an open-weight model is served by many hosts at many prices, so a row needs a chosen public price page, a data slice of its own; the counts per token kind let a reader apply any price, and with one model on both paths the cheaper path follows from the counts and that model's input to output price ratio alone. (2) No `Router.decide_delegation` beside the paths: one model fills every role, so the delegate is never cheaper per token and none is chosen from a pool, and the chain reads no result back, so 13.1's result size R has no value here; the paths are reported as measured, beside the 13.9 grid, never as a decision's outcome. So no result here sets 13.1's W from the note calls' measured completion tokens (a median 281.0 to 320.0 for notes of 163.0 to 176.0 at depths 20 to 100, `research/ledger-cost-model.md`): every committed delegation result keeps W = B (13.1, v1.409, row D12)
- `evidence/ledger-handoff/RESULTS.md` names the chain a surrogate, gives a table per depth and a table per probe arm from the results file, states each note arm's paired losses and gains beside its aggregate counts and never calls a note lossless, and gives the source URL, the revision, the licence and the regenerate command. From v1.397 its regenerate line says the `evidence` workflow reruns it on GitHub and fails if `results.json` changes by a byte
- README (v1.396, row E23b): the opening of README.md `## Evidence: held-out results on public data` ends, after the 13.16 where-delegation-pays paragraph and a blank line, with one more paragraph, the sixth and last before the first `###` (12.8), built from the results file, figures in braces: "Whether work survives a hand-off to a fresh context, measured with `{model}` in every role and not priced: [evidence/ledger-handoff/RESULTS.md](evidence/ledger-handoff/RESULTS.md) sets a chain of fresh contexts linked by notes, a surrogate for a sub-agent hand-off and not that hand-off, against one context holding the whole history, on {items} ledger items at each depth. The chain solves {chain `final_ok`} against {single `final_ok`} at depths of {depth} steps, but loses {`chain_lost`} of the items the one context solves. In its probe of {probe `items`} items {`pre_steps`} steps in, continuing {`steps`} steps from a note of budget {`note_budget`} tokens keeps every continued step `inc_ok` on {note arms' `all_inc_ok`} items against {`history` `all_inc_ok`} with the history, yet loses {`inc_ok_lost`} of the items the history keeps and gains {`inc_ok_gained`}". - README Limitations (v1.462, row DOC29): directly after the per-item bullet (13.8 v1.236), one bullet built from the results file, figures in braces, states the three limits of RESULTS.md `## Limits` and what they leave the delegation decision: "The ledger runs ([evidence/ledger-handoff/RESULTS.md](evidence/ledger-handoff/RESULTS.md)) measure work handed to a fresh context, not a delegation decision, and have three limits. ## 14. Non-goals for v1 (two-way doors, deferred)
- Native vendor SDK adapters (the OpenAI-compatible adapter covers gateways), async execution, streaming
- Learned or contextual routers (per-prompt difficulty prediction); v1 routes per task
- Online drift detection beyond v1.632's `audited_results`, v1.633's `drift_check` and v1.634's `drift` command and `select --window` (8.3, 10), which judge a recent window of audited calls when the caller runs them: a check that runs, alerts or re-routes on its own (v1.635, row M1e); budgets and alerts beyond v1.595's in-process ledger (4.6), v1.596's windows and `downgrade` mode, v1.597's strict caps and v1.598's budget records and `budget_report` and v1.599's `demo --budgets` with exit code 4, and a limit shared across processes
- Price refresh automation
- In the delegation cost model (13): prompt caching beyond one cached-read ratio on the parent's reads of its context (from v1.41, 13.2), such as cache-write surcharges, cache expiry and discounts on other re-reads, and latency, including the speed-up of parallel sub-agents (multi-call work is costed from v1.38, 13.2)
- Production lessons (v1.562, row PL1a): `research/production-lessons.md` reads public write-ups from teams that run language models in production and names, for each lesson, the change that would turn it into routing behavior or measurement, or why the library does not take it. A change it names is a plan, not part of v1: it is specified in its own section, with its tests, when it lands, and a deferral above that it touches is lifted only then. From v1.563 (row PL1b), a page paywalled past its opening is quoted only from the opening its fetch returned and its Sources item says so, and a number read from a figure is the figure's own label. From v1.564 (row PL1c), a number the note computes from a source's own numbers says it is computed here. From v1.565 (row PL1d), a result measured on a benchmark rather than on production traffic says so, and says who ran it, and a model name in the text, as in a quote, is its author's product name, not a `vendor/model` ID. From v1.566 (row PL1e), a page whose text fetch left out the part quoted is quoted from its raw HTML, and its Sources item says so
